surveys.stateOfGame:
Storm and A trap are table rows with no consumer. TWISTS.storm (missiontypes.js:821) and TWISTS.trap (missiontypes.js:835) are read by rollTwists (863), by the reward product in roll() (965) and by text readers, and nowhere else. The three live twists show where a consumer goes: Night is a sight value in field.js start() (2055), No resupply gates the out-of-fight mending block in sortie.js tick() (435), Hardcore rewrites the terms in field.js escalate() (1537). Seams available for Storm: one movement site (field.js:2103), one hit-point door (combat.js:145 damage()), and one options object that reaches Combat.encounter (sortie.js:176) and today carries only frontage and breakOff. Precedents available for A trap: escalate() rewrites m.win, m.lose, m.bonus, m.duration, m.orders and m.pressure in place and is saved with s.mission, and descend() (field.js:1759) builds a new map mid-run and carries the squad's actors with their hp and pools. Line numbers are as read during this round; wave 1 is editing the same files.

Tools used for every number below. (1) combat.js called directly: exp/t2.js, 150 fights per cell. (2) A combat-backed field runner, exp/real.js: Field.start and Field.step with sortie.js's resolve logic (real fighters from Combat.fromCharacter and Missions.spawn, Field.escapeHatch, REGEN mending), party builders adapted from test/field.harness.js plus a weapon, armour and gifts per class. 'Random squads' are 4 classes drawn uniformly from the 61 classes that have a group. Levels were set so the baseline win rate is about 80%: level 3 for most types, 5 for escort, 2 for hold, survival, assassination, raid, sabotage and retrieval. (3) test/field.harness.js's attrition model, copied with twists pinned to none, for the finish-time distribution and the walking-speed check, because its resolver has no bows, heat or mending. All prototype code is in the scratchpad copy C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\proto (combat.js and field.js patched, experiments in exp\); no project file was edited. Standard error is about 1 point on win rate and 0.01 on deaths per run at 1300 to 1950 runs per condition.

Findings that set the designs. Squads finish at 0.2 to 0.3 of the card's estimate on escort, 0.2 to 0.55 on retrieval, 0.35 to 0.55 on pursuit, 0.15 to 0.85 on expedition and 0.55 to 1.05 on recon (attrition harness, 40 runs per type), so a trigger at a fraction of the estimate would not fire on most escort and retrieval runs; both traps trigger at the way home instead. Environmental effects on a random squad are small: Storm A costs 1.2 points of wins and adds 0.03 deaths per run, about two thirds of which comes from walking x0.8 alone. A rule that depends on equipment concentrates its cost: a squad of bow users loses 13 points. The grade of the trap's enemy is a severity dial with a cliff: a veteran costs 9 points of wins, an elite costs 25 points and multiplies deaths by 6.5. Considered and rejected, with the measurement: weather gated to open ground (the share of fights opened with room for 5 or more varies from 29% on outposts to 100% on roads and from 3% on survival to 99% on siege, so the card cannot predict it); portal formation x2 (+0.004 deaths per run, no effect); accuracy -12% for everyone (-1.7 points of wins and +0.026 deaths with walking x0.8, and no decision attached); frontage -2 (raises wins by 3.2 points); noise masking, alarm reach, alarm life and hunt memory x0.6 (deaths per run 0.29 to 0.16 with tactics on and 0.25 to 0.24 with tactics off, 420 runs per cell; it helps the squad, so it cannot be priced as a complication); half recovery between fights (the same axis as No resupply). Pricing rule used for all four rewards: the contract pays what keeps expected gems per attempt equal for the reference squads, counting a death as PULL_COST (game.js:8, 100 gems): R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), with p the win rate, d deaths per run, subscript 0 without and 1 with the twist, and W0 the pay before the twist (115 gems at level 3, type reward 1). R is rounded up to the next 0.05.

proposals.title: Storm A: heat damage x0.5, bows miss +40% and cannot act from the second rank, walking x0.8, on both sides
proposals.problem: Storm is rolled at weight 10 and multiplies pay by 1.15, and no code reads it. The card says 'Slow ground, smothered fire, and nothing with a bowstring works' and the run plays as it would without the tag. The combat call has no input for conditions of the ground or air: sortie.js passes only frontage and breakOff to Combat.encounter, and field.js advances every actor by its own speed alone. A squad of archers pays the same on a Storm contract as on a clear one.
evidence: missiontypes.js:821 TWISTS.storm: weight 10, reward 1.15, not dungeon and duel, no mods. The id appears nowhere else in *.js except spellcraft.js:56, where 'storm' is the tier-3 spelling of the wind noun.
missiontypes.js:965 the reward product multiplies every rolled twist, so the 1.15 is paid today with no effect in the run.
field.js:2103 'a.move += a.speed' is the only place actors move; field.js:2055 sight is the only twist-derived value in start().
combat.js:145 damage() receives every hp loss with a damage type (swing, spell, riposte, splash, and DoT from tickFighter), so one multiplier there covers all heat damage.
combat.js:99 fighters built from characters carry 'family' (bow, sword, ...); fromMonster sets none, so a family rule never touches a hostile.

combat.js:330, 504, 604 are the three bow exceptions to the rank rule: options() offers blade actions to a reserve-rank bow, reaches() returns true for a bow, tickFighter() lets a reserve fighter act when reaches() is true.
sortie.js:176-178 resolve() builds opts = { frontage, breakOff } and calls C.encounter; combat.js:613 encounter() reads only those two.
missions.js:97-101 missionProfile and 104-126 prepare: loadouts are planned against enemy resists only and cached by signature plus zone id (sortie.js:112 builds the id).
classes.js: 6 of 61 grouped classes have role 'ranged' (ranger, skulker, magic_archer, trapper, beastmaster, scout); 4 list the fire word (grenadier, arcanist, elemental_mage, kineticist).

Measured, combat.js direct, 150 fights per cell, level 4, 4 goblins: deaths per run, melee squad 0.09 to 0.09; squad with 2 rangers and a skulker-class bow 0.19 to 0.47; elemental mage with 3 melee 0.10 to 0.15. Against 4 Fire Slimes a melee squad wins 71% clear and 99% in the storm (deaths 1.87 to 0.42), because hostile heat damage is halved too.

Measured, field runner, 6 types x 70 runs per cell, levels 2-3, full Storm A against clear: archers squad (2 rangers, skulker, cleric, warden) win 73.3% to 60.0%, deaths per run 0.040 to 0.121; mixed squad with 1 ranger 74.3% to 73.8%, 0.062 to 0.036; melee squad 75.7% to 76.9%, 0.040 to 0.026; squad with 1 elemental mage 81.7% to 80.0%, 0.024 to 0.040.

Measured, field runner, random squads, 13 types, 1950 runs per condition: clear 82.4% wins, 0.101 deaths per run; Storm A 81.2%, 0.132; walking x0.8 alone 83.1%, 0.122. Per type, walking x0.8 alone: rescue 77% to 71% wins and 0.07 to 0.12 deaths per run; assassination deaths 0.60 to 0.68 (n=150 each).

Measured, Spellcraft/AI planner, elemental mage with a 5-word lexicon, 60 builds per tier: share of prepared spells that deal heat, with heat resistance +0.5 in the enemy profile: brilliant 75% to 54%; dim 73%, plain 71%, sharp 67% unchanged.
proposals.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO storm-b: approve at most one. The mods keys are additive, so both can be read as one row later, but the reward would then need a new measurement.

MODS ENTRY (missiontypes.js TWISTS, in the shape of the approved honesty unit):
storm: { label: 'Storm', weight: 10, reward: 1.05, not: ['dungeon', 'duel'], mods: { move: 0.8, damage: { heat: 0.5 }, miss: { bow: 0.4 }, noReach: ['bow'] } }
MT.modsOf folds the keys: move multiplies, damage[type] multiplies per type, miss[family] adds, noReach is a union. Defaults: move 1, damage {}, miss {}, noReach []. MT.weatherOf(mods) returns { damage, miss, noReach } or null when all three are empty. The tooltip text comes from MOD_TEXT, so it cannot drift from the numbers: 'Both sides: walking speed x0.8, heat damage x0.5. Bow attacks miss 40% more and a bow cannot act from the second rank.'

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. field.js start() and restore(): s.mods = MT.modsOf(mission). Nothing new is saved; mods derive from the saved mission.twists.
2. field.js step() (line 2103): a.move += a.speed * s.mods.move.
3. field.js escalate() (line 1544): m.duration = s.clock + esc.seconds / s.mods.move, so the Hardcore escape window scales with walking speed. Export F.weatherOf(s) = MT.weatherOf(s.mods).
4. sortie.js resolve() (after line 176): if (F.weatherOf(s)) opts.weather = F.weatherOf(s).
5. combat.js: encounter() copies opts.weather into ctx (line 616). damage() (145) multiplies amount by ctx.weather.damage[type] when defined, before the Math.max(1, round) line. rollHit() (185) adds ctx.weather.miss[attacker.family] to the chance it builds from E.statusMissChance. reaches(f, ctx) (504) returns false for a family in ctx.weather.noReach; options() (330) tests the same list instead of 'f.family !== bow'; tickFighter (604) passes ctx. encounter() logs one line per fight when a bow user or a heat spell is present. I patched exactly these sites in the scratchpad copy; the diff is 9 lines.
6. missions.js missionProfile() (97): for each damage entry in mission.weather, profile.resist[type] += 1 - mult. sortie.js pseudoZone() (112): add weather: MT.weatherOf(MT.modsOf(mission)) and append ':wx' to the id so the loadout cache (missions.js:105) does not reuse a clear-weather plan.
7. sortie.js renderBoard party box (next to the scouting line, ~1081): MT.weatherNotes(c, mods) prints one line per picked member that the mods change. A bow in c.equipment.weapon gives 'bow: attacks miss +40%, cannot act from the second rank'. A heat noun in Classes.lexiconOf(c) gives 'fire words: heat damage x0.5'.
8. sortie.js renderSide() tally and fieldview.js drawMap() (83): the tally appends the short MOD_TEXT form; drawMap draws a blue tint and moving rain streaks when mods.weather is true.

CARD AND MAP. Card: the 'Storm' tag with the generated tooltip, and the itemised factor 'Storm x1.05' from the honesty unit's MT.factors. Party box: the per-member lines above, visible before Set out. Map: tint and rain, the tally line 'storm: walking x0.8, heat x0.5, bows grounded', the existing start line 'Complications: Storm' (field.js:2075) and the per-fight line.

DECISION. Before launch: which bow users and fire casters go. The picker names each affected member, and the brief (Bestiary.brief rows) shows whether the species are heat attackers, so the player sees both the cost and the one case where the storm helps (Fire Slime). During the run: no new control.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat order (u-retreat): walking x0.8 applies to both sides, so the head start in tiles per second falls 20% for the squad and the hunters alike; the walk out takes 1.25x as long, 290 s measured maximum becomes 363 s against STRAGGLE 900, so every retreat still terminates. Wounds (u-wounds): bow squads take more damage, so the lowest-HP sample deepens for them; the share of survivors ending a run under 40% HP is 2.8% clear and 2.6% in the storm for random squads, and 2.7% to 4.2% for the archers squad. Permadeath: the cost lands on specific rosters (archers squad deaths per run 0.040 to 0.121) and on window contracts through the walking term (rescue deaths 0.07 to 0.12).

REWARD x1.05. R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0) = 0.8235/0.8117 + 0.0304 x 100 / (0.8117 x 115) = 1.015 + 0.033 = 1.047, rounded up to 1.05 (inputs: random squads, 1950 runs, level 3 pay). The current 1.15 is 0.10 above that value and has no cost behind it; keep 1.15 only as a deliberate bonus. A player can check the inputs on screen: base pay '25 + 30 x level' from the honesty card, the 100-gem Summon button (game.js:8), and a per-twist record added to settle() beside loop-ledger's per-type record (gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, won, dead }, shown on the card as 'with Storm: 9 sent, 7 won, 1 lost'). test/contracts.js recomputes R from 400 fixed-seed sorties per condition and fails when the row is more than 0.10 below the result.

FREQUENCY. Weight 10, not ['dungeon', 'duel'], unchanged. With the honesty unit's draw rule (odds x weight / 66, odds = 0.2 at level 1, 0.41 at level 10, 0.6 at level 18) a contract has Storm in 3.0%, 6.2% and 9.1% of first draws.

TESTS (test/contracts.js and test/combat.weather.js): modsOf fold for 'storm' and for 'storm' with 'dry'; Combat.damage(ctx with weather, heat 100) returns 50; seeded 4-vs-4 fights in which bow users in the reserve rank record zero attacks; a bow user's miss rate rises by 0.40 within sampling error; Field.start with a storm moves a squad on an empty map 0.8 times as far in 100 steps; missionProfile adds 0.5 to heat resist.
proposals.playerEffect: Roster composition becomes a pre-launch decision with a number attached. A squad of bow users loses 13 points of wins and triples its deaths per run; a melee squad or a squad with one bow loses nothing measurable. The picker says which members are affected, so a player with a deep roster swaps them and collects the premium; a player with only rangers declines or rerolls the board. Fire Slime contracts become easier (melee squad 71% to 99%), and the species list on the brief tells the player which case it is. The decision exists for about a third of squads (6 of 61 classes are ranged, so 1 - 0.9^4 = 34% of random 4-person squads include one), which is why the premium is small.
proposals.secondOrder: Brilliant minds adapt: the planner sees heat as resisted and moves its heat-spell share from 75% to 54%, while dim, plain and sharp minds do not, so acumen (ai.js tiers) pays in a storm without any new code in ai.js. Hardcore plus Storm stays escapable because the escape window scales by 1/move. Tactics and hostiles use field.odds, which ignores bows and heat, so squads do not choose ground differently in a storm; that is unchanged and stated as a limit. Trials roll twists through MT.roll without a filter (quests.js:116), so a star trial can carry Storm. A later weather twist (Fog) reuses ctx.weather and the mods keys. The plain attrition resolver (Field.attrition) shows only the walking term, so test/field.harness.js cannot measure this twist; a combat-backed runner should live in test/ (u-retreat already asks for one; exp/real.js is a working version).
proposals.risks: A spell with several strikes is scaled by the type of its first strike (combat.js passes strikes[0].type to damage()), so a fire-and-ice spell is scaled as heat. The heat note in the picker is a hint, since spells are chosen at launch by the planner. For about two thirds of squads the twist costs almost nothing, so the premium is mostly unbacked for them; 1.05 limits that. Walking x0.8 roughly doubles escort deaths in the runner (0.09 to 0.19 per run, n=150) and the cause is not isolated: the ward walks at 0.31 tiles per second and the route takes 25% longer under the same ambush spawns. Depends on the honesty unit's modsOf and MOD_TEXT; if it lands later, the same keys go into a ten-line local fold. Overlaps wave 1 on sortie.js, field.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js, so line numbers move and one owner should apply it.

proposals.title: Storm B: every combatant starts each fight Wet (3 stacks), walking x0.8; the condition carries the numbers
proposals.problem: Same dead row as storm-a (missiontypes.js:821). Elements already contains the condition the card describes: elements.js:170 'wet' gives heat resistance +8% per stack, lightning and cold -6%, poison -4%, and a heat hit removes a stack; spellcraft.js:54-56 applies it from the water word. The contract layer has no way to put a condition on a whole map, so weather would otherwise be a second set of constants beside the one in Elements.
evidence: missiontypes.js:821 TWISTS.storm has no consumer (see storm-a).

elements.js:170 def('wet'): stacking sum, cap 5, escalates to 'soaked' (elements.js:171: heat resistance 0.8, lightning, cold and poison -0.5); removal on heat damage uses 'unstack' (elements.js:367) which removes one stack per heat hit.
elements.js:444 statusMissChance(b) reads d.missChance only, with no way to key a miss chance to a weapon family; combat.js:99 gives every character fighter a 'family'.

combat.js:613-632 encounter(): the loop that resets every fighter before tick 1 is the one place both sides can be given a status; profileOf (combat.js:659) averages E.bearerResistance(e, t), which already includes status mods, so a status on the sample enemies reaches the loadout planner with no planner change.
facet.schema.ig.js:115 enumerates the status descriptor fields (missChance, incomingMissChance, healCap, ...); a new field must be listed there before the facet files are re-enabled.

Measured, combat.js direct, 150 fights per cell, level 4, melee squad, deaths per run clear to Wet x3 (with bow miss +30%): 4 Ice Slimes 0.05 to 0.23; 4 Thunder Slimes 0.01 to 0.07; 2 Cave Spiders 0.03 to 0.11; 4 goblins 0.09 to 0.09; 4 Fire Slimes win 71% to 76% (deaths 1.87 to 1.67). Bows squad: goblins 0.19 to 0.33, Ice Slimes 0.04 to 0.59, Thunder Slimes 0.03 to 0.35.
Measured, same, squad with one lightning mage or one frost mage: Ice Slimes 0.05 to 0.17 (no upside from the +18% lightning and cold damage was visible with one caster in four).
Measured, field runner, random squads, 13 types x 100 runs: clear 81.0% wins, 0.105 deaths per run; Wet x3 + bow +30% + walking x0.8: 81.9%, 0.138; the same without the bow rule: 82.5%, 0.133.
Measured, field runner, same squads, walking x0.8 plus a 40-second portal (x2): 82.8%, 0.131; portal x2 alone: 81.3%, 0.109. Portal time does not matter, so it is not in this design.
proposals.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO storm-a: approve at most one.

MODS ENTRY:
storm: { label: 'Storm', weight: 10, reward: 1.05, not: ['dungeon', 'duel'], mods: { move: 0.8, status: [{ id: 'wet', stacks: 3 }] } }
MT.modsOf folds move by multiplication and status by union (the larger stack count per id). MT.weatherOf(mods) returns { status } for the combat call. MOD_TEXT generates the tooltip from the status definition: 'Both sides start each fight Wet x3: heat resistance +24%, lightning and cold resistance -18%, poison resistance -12%, bow attacks miss +30%. A heat hit removes one stack from its target. Walking speed x0.8.' The percentages are computed from elements.js, so editing the definition edits the card.

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. elements.js: wet gains missChanceBy: { bow: 0.1 } (per stack); statusMissChance(b) adds (d.missChanceBy && d.missChanceBy[b.family]) || 0 to d.missChance before scaling by intensity. A wet archer from a water spell (spellcraft.js:56) now misses more too. facet.schema.ig.js:115 lists the new field as { kind: 'mod', mortality: 'evade' }.
2. combat.js encounter() (loop at ~627, before the first tick): for each fighter on both sides, apply wet one stack at a time (E.applyStatus(f, { id: 'wet', intensity: 1, duration: 'permanent' }, 'storm', false)) until the fighter holds opts.weather.status[i].stacks stacks. Stacks are counted, not summed in one call: a single call with intensity 3 makes one stack, which the first heat hit would remove whole. The top-up is idempotent, so a fighter who keeps its status from the previous fight is not pushed to 5 stacks and into 'soaked'. One log line per fight: 'storm: everyone is Wet x3'.
3. sortie.js resolve() (after line 176): opts.weather = F.weatherOf(s). field.js start()/restore(): s.mods = MT.modsOf(mission); step() (2103): a.move += a.speed * s.mods.move; escalate() (1544): esc.seconds / s.mods.move.
4. missions.js missionProfile() (97): apply the same statuses to the sample enemies before C.profileOf, so the planner sees wet resistances; sortie.js pseudoZone() (112) carries weather and appends ':wx' to the id.
5. Picker (sortie.js, next to ~1081): per picked member, bow weapon: 'attacks miss +30%'; fire words: 'heat damage x0.76 on the first hit, drying'; spark or ice words: 'damage +18% against Wet targets'. Brief: a row whose species damage type is lightning, cold or poison gets the tag 'storm: squad takes +18% / +18% / +12%'; a heat row gets 'storm: squad takes x0.76'.
6. fieldview.js drawMap(): the same tint and rain as storm-a. Tally: 'storm: Wet x3, walking x0.8'.

CARD AND MAP. Card tag with the generated tooltip and 'Storm x1.05'. Brief rows carry the species-level tags above. Map: tint and rain, tally line, start line 'Complications: Storm'.

DECISION. Before launch the player reads the brief: the same Storm is mild on a goblin or Forest Rat cast and costs a melee squad 4.6x the deaths against Ice Slimes and 3.7x against Cave Spiders. The player can skip those contracts, or send casters of other elements and a squad without bows. During the run: fire dries the target (each heat hit removes a stack), so a fire caster loses 24% on the first hit and recovers; a water caster adds stacks and two applications push a target to Soaked.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat order: the walk out takes 1.25x as long (363 s against STRAGGLE 900 using the 290 s measured maximum). Wounds: share of survivors under 40% HP at the end 3.0% clear and 2.4% Wet. Permadeath: +0.033 deaths per run for random squads, concentrated on Ice, Thunder and Spider casts and on bow squads (0.19 to 0.33 against goblins).

REWARD x1.05. R = 81.0/81.9 + 0.033 x 100 / (0.819 x 115) = 0.989 + 0.035 = 1.024, rounded up to 1.05. Same inputs, same on-screen check and same test as storm-a: base pay line, the 100-gem Summon button, and the per-twist record 'with Storm: N sent, W won, D lost'.

FREQUENCY. Weight 10, not ['dungeon', 'duel']; 3.0%, 6.2%, 9.1% of first draws at levels 1, 10, 18 under the honesty unit's rule.

TESTS: modsOf fold; after Combat.encounter's setup every fighter holds exactly 3 wet stacks and a second encounter on the same fighters leaves 3; a heat hit lowers stacks to 2; statusMissChance for a bow fighter with 3 stacks is 0.30 and for a monster is 0; missionProfile heat resist rises by 0.24.
proposals.playerEffect: The decision is made on the species list of the brief, which the player already reads: a Storm contract against Thunder Slimes, Ice Slimes or Cave Spiders costs a melee squad several times the deaths of the same contract against goblins, and the card says why. Bow squads pay in every case. The decision is more informative than storm-a because it depends on the contract's cast and not only on the squad, and it keeps the flat 1.05 honest by letting the player decline the expensive casts. The measured upside for lightning and frost casters is not visible with one caster in four, so the design is a conditional cost, not a trade.
proposals.secondOrder: Weather becomes a condition like any other: the water word, Water Slime attacks and the storm all feed the same status, and a squad that adds two stacks takes a target to Soaked (heat resistance 0.8, lightning, cold, poison -0.5). The planner reads the changed resistances through bearerResistance with no new planner code; brilliant minds change their spell mix, lower tiers do not. Archers get a rule that exists outside Storm (wet bowstrings), which changes Water Slime fights too. A later Fog or Snow twist is a status id in a mods row. test/field.harness.js still cannot see any of this.
proposals.risks: Species coupling: the swing is 4.6x deaths on Ice Slime casts for a flat 1.05, so the price is right on average and wrong on those casts; the brief tags are the mitigation, and the stack count (3) is the dial (5 would be Soaked: a melee squad against Cave Spiders went from 95% wins to 51% in an earlier cell). Editing the shared 'wet' definition changes spell-applied Wet for every fight, not only storms. elements.js and combat.js are shared with the facet engine; the new field must be added to the facet schema or it fails the schema check when facets return. Status persistence: wet has no combatEnd removal, so fighters carry it into the next fight on the same map; the top-up logic depends on counting stacks (findStatus(...).stacks). The population effect (+0.033 deaths per run) is the same size as storm-a's; the difference between the two is where the cost falls, not how large it is. Overlaps wave 1 on combat.js and elements.js.

proposals.title: A trap A: when the written work is done and the squad reaches the way home, a named veteran appears 8 to 11 tiles away and 'kill the target' is added to the terms
proposals.problem: A trap is rolled at weight 10... see row: weight 6, pays x1.5 and has no consumer (missiontypes.js:835). The card promises a change of terms partway in; the only code that changes terms mid-run is Hardcore's escalate(). Squads finish early (0.2 to 0.3 of the estimate on escort), so any trigger set as a fraction of the estimate would often fire after the squad has left or never.
evidence: missiontypes.js:835 TWISTS.trap: weight 6, reward 1.5, only recon, escort, expedition, retrieval, pursuit; no other reference to the id (field.js:1812 traps() handles structures of kind 'trap', which is unrelated).

field.js:1537-1561 escalate() rewrites m.win, m.lose, m.bonus, m.duration, m.exitMode, m.orders, m.pressure, resets s.latched, s.phase, s.pushed, raises the alarm and respawns groups; it is saved because save() stores s.mission (field.js:~1995) and s.escalated.

field.js:1321 workDone(s), 1301 inPortal(s, a), 1353 portalTick, 1857 leave and the order in step() at 2118-2120 (portalTick, overtime, leave): a hook between overtime and leave runs before anyone is extracted.
field.js:1662 makeActor(g, p, s) builds an actor from a cast-like group and names the species through s.name; field.js:1154 raise(s, at) sets the alarm; field.js:1648 spawnGroup.
bestiary.js:204-205 Bestiary.brief reads only hostile, patrol and mark groups of m.cast, so a mark created at run time is not on the paper.
tactics.js:201 strikeTarget reads eliminate atoms from s.mission.win and finds actors by name or role, so a mark named 'target' is visible to the existing 'quiet way in' play with no change.

Measured, attrition harness copy, 40 runs per type, tactics off: finish time as a fraction of the card's estimate, p10 / p50 / p90: recon 0.56 / 0.80 / 1.01; escort 0.21 / 0.28 / 0.30; expedition 0.17 / 0.41 / 0.71; retrieval 0.21 / 0.32 / 0.44; pursuit 0.35 / 0.42 / 0.55.

Measured, field runner, random squads, 5 eligible types x 150 runs (750 per condition), veteran mark: clear 80.9% wins, 0.041 deaths per run; trap 72.0%, 0.053. The trap sprang in 591 of 750 runs (79%; the rest ended before the way home) and the squad won 88% of those. By type, clear to trap: recon 68% to 66%, escort 100% to 79%, expedition 81% to 81%, pursuit 79% to 71%, retrieval 77% to 63%.

Measured, same runner, 5 types x 100 runs, severity dial: clear 79.4% wins, 0.040 deaths; veteran mark 70.0%, 0.054; elite mark 54.6%, 0.260 (win 67% of sprung runs; recon 0.45 and escort 0.69 deaths per run).
Measured, prototype integrity: 60 of 60 runs saved at the spring (Field.save), passed through JSON, restored (Field.restore) and finished with the target present.
proposals.change:

surveys.stateOfGame:
The six complications are table rows only. TWISTS (missiontypes.js:818) has nine entries; the only consumers are field.js:2055 (Night, sight 9 becomes 5), sortie.js:435 (No resupply) and field.js:1535 (Hardcore). Reinforcements (row :823, weight 12, x1.3, not duel) and Infested (row :827, weight 10, x1.35) are rolled on 3.4% / 3.4% of level-1 contracts, 7.2% / 7.5% at level 10 and 12.2% / 12.7% at level 20 and pay without doing anything. Everything needed to make them real already exists in separate pieces. roll() builds the cast, applies the horde rule swarm() (missiontypes.js:310) and only then reads the terms (:945-952). mapgen.build() places each cast group at its own points and marks groups with a per or temporal cue as deferred (mapgen.js:340); arrivals() (field.js:1702) spawns deferred groups on the clock. escalate() and the window-shut branch of portalTick() already re-spawn 50% and 30% of the written groups through spawnGroup (field.js:1557, 1373). nameCast() fixes one species per group when the contract is written (sortie.js:61), Bestiary.brief() prints one row per species and level (bestiary.js:201-212), fighterFor() fields a body at mission level + GRADE_BUMP + levelOffset (sortie.js:136), look() marks a hostile spotted and raises the alarm when it sees a squad member (field.js:877), and Missions.prepare plans loadouts only against the species of groups that are on the map at launch (sortie.js:257, field.js:2067 skips deferred groups).

Measurements. test/field.harness.js uses the plain attrition resolver, so I built a combat.js-backed runner that mirrors sortie.js resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast, over a private patched copy of the project. Everything is in C:/Users/mersi/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha/bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109/scratchpad/arrivals (called ARR below): run.js, par.js, variants2.js, tiers.js, the patched copy proj2/ (field.js, missiontypes.js, mapgen.js), and result files under ARR/results/. Squad: 4 random 3-5 star characters from the real generators, no gear or potions, contract level 1-4, tactics on, same seeds in every arm, 15 types (duel not run). Base: 69.5% wins, 0.258 deaths per run, 14.7% of runs with a death, 6.21 fights per run (1500 runs); with the wave-2 wound rule (WOUND_FROM 0.4) 14.4% of survivors and 38% of sorties are injured, which matches loop-wounds' own calibration. The live twists on the same harness: Night 71.3% / 0.286 (900 runs, not distinguishable from base), No resupply 65.1% / 0.321. Four findings decided the designs. (1) First contact (first sighting or first fight) happens in 97% of runs, median 40-190 s by type, but the written estimate is 2-8x the real run (median clock / duration 0.12-0.52), so a trigger as a fraction of duration fires after the contract is over, and a kill-share trigger (half the garrison dead) is reached in 70% of runs (28% assassination, 38% escort). (2) One grade up is not a uniform step in combat.js: hp x damage x speed per body is x3.8 basic to veteran, x4.8 veteran to elite, x1.5 elite to ancient (GRADE_BUMP is +3 levels) and x8.9 ancient to legendary at level 6 (ARR/tiers.js), so promoting a third of every group by grade adds 0.35 deaths per run (win 70.2 to 53.3%), of which basic groups alone add 0.01 and veteran groups alone 0.30. (3) A level offset is a uniform step that fighterFor, castLevel, noteSighting and the brief rows already honour. (4) The horde rule already turns a grade gap into bodies: x2.2 per grade, 4.5 levels lower, in packs.

Shared conventions in the four proposals. Consumers never name a twist: they read folded mods through MT.modsOf (u-honesty), and the three new keys are arrivals (list, folds by concatenation: entries {on, delay, from, share}), promote (folds to the largest share: {share, perLevel}) and swell (integer, folds by sum, capped at 2). Each key needs one MOD_TEXT line and one consumer, which is the unit's own test. All numbers are produced by one price rule so the four multipliers can be compared: the multiplier m at which expected gem income per attempt, fee x m x P(win) + gem drops of the kills made (missions.js:242, paid at sortie.js:555), equals the base contract's plus R gems for every extra death, with R = 200 = 2 x PULL_COST (game.js:8, the Summon button). m = (W0 F0 + L0 + R dd - L1) / (W1 F1) with W the win rate, F the fee per won contract ((25 + 30 x level) x type reward, sortie.js:535), L the drops per run, dd the extra deaths per run. The same rule applied to the live No resupply twist (840 paired runs, 14 types: 69.2% to 63.9% wins, 0.280 to 0.337 deaths) returns x1.28 against its table value x1.25; the standard error of that death difference is 0.039, so R is known to roughly a factor of two. A constant multiplier cannot track level (the fee grows 30 gems per level, R does not), so these are values for the levels 1-4 the harness runs. With the proposed constants the mean contract pay multiplier at level 10 is 1.124 (A + Infested-a) or 1.095 (B + Infested-b), against 1.152 for today's nine rows and 1.064 for the three live ones (u-honesty), so the honesty unit's pay cut is largely undone by the real rows. Frequencies in the proposals are computed with all nine rows in the pool (the state once the six are real) on the board's current rule; with only five rows live, u-honesty's rule (draw probability = odds x weight / 66) makes them about 15% higher (reinforcements-a at level 10: 8.0% against 6.8%).

proposals.title: Rear column: a printed second garrison arrives at the entry 45 s after first contact and walks at the squad
proposals.problem: The board offers Reinforcements ("A second garrison arrives partway through, from the wrong direction") and pays x1.3 for it, but the id appears only in its table row (missiontypes.js:823) and nothing arrives. The player cannot tell when "partway" is, where "the wrong direction" is, how many come or what to do about it. The two obvious triggers fail on measured data: a fraction of mission.duration fires after the contract is over in most runs (median clock / duration 0.12-0.52), and a kill-share trigger is not reached in 30% of runs. First contact (the first hostile that sees the squad, or the first fight) happens in 97% of runs, median 40-190 s by type, and it is the same event that ends the free Call it off window in loop-retreat, so it is the natural start of a clock the player can read on the paper.

It runs after terms(), so win, lose and bonus atoms are those of the written contract (extermination still asks 80% of the written count). grade, levelOffset and horde are copied; species is not, so nameCast gives the second garrison its own species. (2) mapgen.js:340 deferred: !!(group.per || group.arrive || TEMPORAL.has(group.at)). (3) field.js: openSkirmish (:1219) and look (:877) set s.contactAt = s.clock when it is null, beside the counters.fights / spotted increments loop-retreat adds; start() initialises contactAt to null and save() / restore() carry it. arrivals() gets one block: for each s.map.spawns entry g with g.arrive and not g.fired, due when s.contactAt !== null && s.clock >= s.contactAt + g.arrive.delay; on due set g.fired = true (the spawn list is inside the saved map, field.js:1993, so a reload does not fire twice), call spawnGroup(s, g) and say one line with the body count and the walking distance from the group's first point to the nearest squad member (fieldTo, tiles and tiles / BASE_SPEED seconds). spawnGroup sets march = true on bodies from a group with g.arrive. chooseGoals (:797) becomes switch (e.march ? 'waves' : m.pressure), so a marching body takes the default branch hunt() in every contract type. ACTOR_KEYS (:1943) gets 'march'. The re-spawn loops at :1373 and :1557 skip groups with g.arrive. (4) bestiary.js brief() puts g.arrive in the row key and copies it to the row; sortie.js briefBox prints "arrives 0:09 after first contact, at the entry"; missionCard's expect line appends " +5 later". (5) sortie.js launch (:257): species = species of s.actors plus species of mission.cast groups with arrive, so Missions.prepare plans against the column (pseudoZone's id includes species.length, so the loadout cache key changes). (6) fieldview.js drawMap: the entry ring is labelled "relief 0:07" while an arrival is pending; drawActors already draws unrevealed hostiles at alpha .38, so the marching column is visible. (7) sortie.js renderSide: one line under the portal line, "relief in 0:07" or "relief: 4 bodies, 34 tiles from the squad". (8) sortie.js settle: gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, won, dead }, beside loop-ledger's per-type tally; the tag title prints it once sent > 0. (9) test/arrivals.harness.js (the scratchpad runner, moved) and test/contracts.js cases: clone counts equal max(1, round(count * 0.35)); terms identical with and without the twist; fire exactly once at contactAt + 45 across a save / restore at +20 s; escalate and the window-shut loop spawn no arrival group.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Reinforcements x1.25"; its title lists the factors ("25 + 30 x level 3 = 115 / Assassination x2.5 / Reinforcements x1.25") and the generated desc; the expect line lists the extra rows. Brief: the column is its own row per species with the arrival text, subject to the contract's intel as every row is (at intel 0 the rows collapse and the card tooltip still states the share and the delay). Map: the entry ring carries the countdown, then the column appears as ghost tokens at the ring and walks at the squad; the log gives the body count and the walking time.

REWARD x1.25. Rule in the shared conventions. Inputs for this design, 1300 paired runs: wins 68.6 to 64.8%, deaths 0.251 to 0.410 per run, fee per won contract 168 / 169 gems, kill drops 57.7 to 70.4 gems per run (390 paired runs; the column adds 2.4 kills per run): (0.686 x 168 + 57.7 + 200 x 0.159 - 70.4) / (0.648 x 169) = 1.23, rounded to 1.25 (fee-only it would be 1.34). The player's check: the card title itemises the factor; the brief lists the exact extra bodies, so +35% is countable; gs.field.twists shows their own sent / lost record with the twist; node test/arrivals.harness.js prints the five inputs and the computed multiplier and fails if the table value differs by more than 0.10.

FREQUENCY. weight 14 (was 12), not duel, dungeon, escort. Per contract on the board's own rule (missiontypes.js:863, board of uniformly drawn types): 3.2% at level 1, 4.7% at 5, 6.7% at 10, 9.3% at 15, 11.7% at 20, against 3.4 / 4.8 / 7.2 / 9.7 / 12.2% today. P(at least one on a board of 5): 15% at level 1, 29% at level 10, 46% at level 20.
proposals.playerEffect: The decision is made at the board and at the party picker. The paper now says the contract is 35% bigger, that the extra bodies come second, from behind, and when, so a player can compare squad strength against both fights on the same ground and against x1.25. A squad that wins the first fight hurt meets the column hurt (under the wound rule 18.4% of survivors are injured against 14.7%); the measured cost of the twist is +0.16 deaths per run (14.7% to 20.3% of runs with a death) and +1.7 fights per run. In the run the player has one lever, the retreat order, and the table above says what it is worth: ordered at first sight it costs 0.021 deaths per run against 0.410 for staying (saves 0.39, where the base saves 0.24), ordered 30 s later it saves 0.16 and 150 s later 0.04 (the base saves 0.11 and 0.01 at those times). The column therefore raises the value of ordering the retreat at once and does not make it unsafe.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat order (loop-retreat): contact now starts two clocks, the end of the free window and the release of the column, and the order stays the strongest lever (see numbers). Wounds (loop-wounds, WOUND_FROM 0.4): injured survivors 14.7% to 18.4%, sorties with an injured member 39% to 46%, so the twist feeds the downtime that wave 2 introduces. Debrief (systems-one-debrief): fights per run 6.46 to 8.18, so casts and stamina spent per sortie rise about 27%. Permadeath: 14.7% to 20.3% of runs lose someone. Loadouts: the column's species are in pseudoZone, so a brilliant mind plans resistances for them. Bestiary: the column adds species to Bestiary.record, so contracts with it teach the town more. Loot: kill drops rise 22% (57.7 to 70.4 gems per run) and are counted in the price. Hardcore: the escalation re-spawn skips arrival groups, so the two do not stack their spawns. The Tactics retreat play (tactics.js, "a step back") falls back to the way in, which is where the column appears; plays fire 0.01 times per run so this is not measurable. Higher regime (5-star squads, level up to 8, 300 runs): wins 62.7 to 55.7%, deaths 0.440 to 0.650.
proposals.risks: Harness caveats: plain characters without gear or potions, so absolute deaths are upper bounds; confirm on a real save as loop-wounds step 7 does. The column is part-inert where contact comes late: hold 74% fire and 52% reach, siege 71% reach, survival 72%; the multiplier is the average effect over those runs. In 9.8% of firings the nearest squad member is under 20 s of walking from the entry (survival 74%, raid 21%, every other type 7% or less): a squad holding ground near the way in gets the column on top of it. If that is unwanted, hold the release until no squad member is within SIGHT + 2 tiles of the entry, for at most 30 s (not measured). The column's kills count toward counters.killed.hostile, so an extermination quota can be reached by killing column bodies (extermination wins 91% to 86%). Share is a weak dial because every group gets at least one body: 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.35 give deaths +0.114 / +0.128 / +0.163 and wins -4.8 / -3.5 / -3.2 points (780 paired runs, same seeds). Delay is a dial: 20 / 45 / 90 s give deaths 0.448 / 0.429 / 0.407 and fire in 94 / 92 / 81%; 45 s is 9 real seconds on the card at 1x, so the walk takes another 12; a longer delay is gentler and fires less. The pay rule uses R = 200 whose own error is about a factor of two (standard error 0.039 on the No resupply death difference), so the multiplier is good to about +/-0.15. This design depends on loop-retreat's contact definition (counters.fights / spotted) only for the name of the event; contactAt is two lines if loop-retreat is not built. Alternative rejected: a column from the far side on a contact clock (fires 92%, reaches 67%, deaths +0.095, wins -9.2) arrives away from the way home, so it does not contest the exit.

proposals.title: Promoted third: round(count / 3) bodies of each rank-and-file group are fielded about 1.5x stronger, same species
proposals.problem: The card shows Infested ("A third of the cast comes one grade up") and pays x1.35, and the cast is exactly as written. Taken literally, "one grade up" is a poor unit: in combat.js a body one grade up is x3.8 (basic to veteran), x4.8 (veteran to elite) and x1.5 (elite to ancient) in hp x damage x speed, and elite to legendary does not exist for rank and file. Promoting a third of every group by grade is therefore a dial with no consistent setting: basic groups alone add 0.01 deaths per run and veteran groups alone add 0.30, and no single multiplier fits both. A level offset gives the same kind of step as a uniform ratio that the game already handles.
evidence: combat.js:106-107 fromMonster: stats scale (1 + 0.35 x (level - 1)) x tier x rarity, so +k levels is a fixed ratio for a given level: about x1.5 hp and damage when k = round(1 + level / 2), at every level from 2 to 18.

Per-grade body strength, hp x damage x speed averaged over the bestiary tier at level 6 (ARR/tiers.js): basic 5.0e5, veteran 1.9e6 (x3.8), elite 9.1e6 (x4.8), ancient 1.4e7 (x1.5, sortie.js:27 GRADE_BUMP +3 levels), legendary 1.2e8 (x8.9).

Promotion by grade measured, 900 runs each, base 70.2% / 0.263: a third of every group 53.3% / 0.614; basic groups only 63.4% / 0.272; veteran groups only 57.6% / 0.566; a third at +3 levels 61.8% / 0.354 (ARR/r1.json, r2.json, r3.json).

sortie.js:136 fighterFor, :301 noteSighting, :972 castLevel and bestiary.js:201 (levelOf) all add g.levelOffset already, so a positive offset reaches the fighter, the sighting level and the brief row with no change. bestiary.js:211 keys rows by species and level, so a promoted subgroup is its own row.

field.js:84 SWARMED(g) turns a negative levelOffset into a plain-model hp and power factor; for a positive offset it evaluates 1 / (1 + 0.35 x -k) which is negative and is clamped to 0.15, so a promoted body would read as a runt in field.js:1682-1683 and in every odds() call tactics makes. One line fixes it.
sortie.js:61 nameCast names each cast group independently; a group split by promote() needs a shared key so both halves are the same species (two lines).

missiontypes.js:310-318 swarm() and :945 roll(): promotion belongs after swarm so it moves bodies of the final cast, and before side-job casts and terms so counts used by terms() are unchanged (promotion preserves counts).

Measured final design (ARR/results/final-n100; 1500 runs, 15 types, same seeds as base): wins 69.5 to 62.6%, deaths 0.258 to 0.399 per run, runs with a death 14.7 to 20.1%, run-aways 26.6 to 31.0%, wipes 1.8 to 3.8%, injured survivors 14.4 to 16.6%, sorties with an injured member 38 to 42%. By cover (map archetype): wins -7.2 points on wilds and ruins (n=530), -7.5 on cover 0.15-0.25 (n=726), -4.5 on dungeon and arena (n=244): the effect does not depend on the map. Higher regime (5-star, level up to 8, 300 runs): wins 62.7 to 55.3%, deaths 0.440 to 0.543.

Share dial, 900 paired runs on the same seeds (base 70.2% / 0.263): one sixth 65.0% / 0.348, one quarter 62.4% / 0.391, one third 61.9% / 0.392; groups of 1-2 bodies promote nothing, so the dial saturates near a quarter.
proposals.change:
MODS: infested: { label: 'Infested', weight: 10, reward: 1.50, mods: { promote: { share: 1 / 3, perLevel: 0.5 } } } (no only / not: the arena bill lists the promoted rows too). MT.modsOf folds promote by taking the entry with the largest share. Generated desc: "round(count / 3) bodies of each hostile and patrol group of 2 or more (4 of 12 on this paper) are fielded 3 levels above the rest of the group, about 1.5x hp and damage. Same species. Marks, wards and structures are unchanged."

CONSUMERS. (1) missiontypes.js: new pure promote(cast, p, level), called in roll() immediately after the swarm map (:945) and before side-job casts and terms: for each hostile or patrol group g with k = round(g.count * share) >= 1 it replaces g by { ...g, count: g.count - k } and { ...g, count: k, levelOffset: (g.levelOffset || 0) + up, promoted: up }, both carrying a kin id, where up = max(1, round(1 + max(1, level + (g.levelOffset || 0)) * perLevel)) so the ratio is the same for a swarmed group as for a full-size one. Counts are preserved, so terms() reads the same totals. (2) sortie.js nameCast (:61): groups with the same kin get the same species (the first naming is reused), so the promoted third are stronger specimens of the same animal. (3) field.js SWARMED (:84): positive branch 1 + 0.35 x levelOffset, used by makeActor's hp and power (:1682-1683). (4) fieldview.js drawActors: a small "+3" over a body with levelOffset > 0; swarmed bodies (negative) keep no mark. (5) Nothing else: fighterFor, noteSighting, castLevel, Bestiary.brief and the card's expect line already read levelOffset. (6) test/contracts.js: promoted bodies equal the sum of round(count / 3) over groups; terms equal the unpromoted roll; promoted and rest share a species after nameCast; SWARMED(+3) > 1 and SWARMED(-5) < 1. (7) test/arrivals.harness.js reproduces the table.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Infested x1.50" with the generated desc and the factor line; the expect line shows both rows ("Young Wolf lvl 5 x8 / Young Wolf lvl 9 x4"). Brief: the same rows with the town's knowledge of that species at that level (hp, armour and weaknesses come from Combat.fromMonster at the row's level, bestiary.js:223-231, so a studied species shows its real numbers). Map: "+3" over promoted bodies. The rows follow the contract's intel as every cast row does: at intel 1 the species are hidden and the counts rounded ("??? lvl 5 x8", "??? lvl 9 x4"), at intel 0 they collapse into one unknown row.

REWARD x1.50. Same rule. Inputs, 1500 paired runs: wins 69.5 to 62.6%, deaths 0.258 to 0.399, fee per won contract 167 / 162, drops 54.1 to 48.0 gems per run (450 paired runs; run-aways cost 0.9 kills per run): (0.695 x 167 + 54.1 + 200 x 0.141 - 48.0) / (0.626 x 162) = 1.48, rounded to 1.50. Player's check: the card title itemises x1.50; the two rows state the extra strength as a level number in the same column as every other level; gs.field.twists gives their record with it.

FREQUENCY. weight 10 and no only / not, unchanged: 3.4% of level-1 contracts, 5.1% at 5, 7.5% at 10, 10.0% at 15, 12.7% at 20; a board of 5 has one 16% of the time at level 1 and 32% at level 10. The same row appears on arena contracts, where groups of 1-3 per bout promote at most one body.
proposals.playerEffect: The decision is before launch and it is a reading of the paper: the brief now has a second row for the same species at a higher level, and the player compares it with what the town knows (the row shows hp and weaknesses once the species has been studied). A squad built for level 5 goblins meets four at level 9. During the run nothing new has to be decided; the cost is the measured one, +0.14 deaths per run and 6.9 fewer wins in 100. The card claims more danger and the paper shows the same enemy at a stated higher level.
proposals.secondOrder: Wounds: injured survivors 14.4% to 16.6%, sorties with an injured member 38% to 42%. Permadeath: runs with a death 14.7% to 20.1%, wipes 1.8% to 3.8%. Retreat (loop-retreat): the squad's own break-off from a fight it is losing rises from 26.6% to 31.0% of runs, which is the on-foot path wave 2 keeps; the twist does not change the retreat order's value except through the higher base risk. Bestiary: promoted bodies are the same species, so kills still progress the entry the player already has, and the knowledge shown on the brief row applies directly. Loot: drops fall 54.1 to 48.0 gems per run because squads run more; counted in the price. Tactics: no change in play counts (stand 0.18 to 0.19 per run). Interaction with swarm: a promoted third of a swarmed group is a third of its bodies returned toward full size (a level-8 basic swarm of 33 at -5 levels becomes 22 at -5 and 11 at -2), so Infested on a horde contract raises the share of strong bodies, not the count.
proposals.risks: This is the minimal version: the only new decision is the one on the paper, and the only change in the run is larger numbers on a third of the bodies; infested-b is the design with a different lever. The price rests on R = 200 and on n=450 for drops, so x1.50 is good to about +/-0.15; at the literal grade reading the price cannot be set at all (the extra deaths differ by about x30 between basic-only and veteran-only). Positive levelOffset has not been exercised outside this runner: SWARMED is the only place in the repo that assumed offsets were negative (grep levelOffset); check that GRADE_BUMP + levelOffset on an elite or ancient group stays within M.spawn's level handling (no cap at present). Level 12+ contracts promote 6-10 levels; the ratio holds because combat.js:107 is linear in level, but gear scaling of the squad is not in the harness. The Infested rows add a second brief row per promoted group, so briefs get longer (a 4-group cast shows 8 rows); the card's expect line becomes wide, so cap it at 6 rows and print "+N more". Rejected alternatives with data: grade ladder on a third (above), same species at fixed +3 levels (61.8% / 0.354, level-dependent ratio from x2.1 at level 1 to x1.2 at level 15).

proposals.title: Alarm call: a spotter that lives 30 s carries word, and a second garrison walks in from unexplored ground ahead
proposals.problem: Same card, same unimplemented row, different question: what makes a second garrison arrive "partway through" for a reason the player can see and act on, and from a direction other than the one they came in by. A fixed clock does neither. The code already records exactly who knows about the squad: look() sets spotted on every hostile that has a line to a squad member and raises the alarm (field.js:877), and the Leave no witnesses side job (missiontypes.js:763, effect quiet, field.js:467) is written around "nobody carried word" but only clears the spotted counter and the alarm. This design makes the word travel: a hostile that has seen the squad and is still standing 30 s later calls the second garrison, and killing every spotter first prevents it.
evidence: field.js:874-881 look(): for each hostile not yet spotted, if any squad member is within sight with a line, e.spotted = true, counters.spotted++, raise(). Nothing stores when. field.js:2055: Night halves sight, so it halves who can spot.

field.js:461-475 sideCheck: the quiet effect sets counters.spotted = 0 and alarmUntil = 0 ("nobody carried word"); missiontypes.js:763-769 silence is offered on recon, rescue, retrieval, sabotage, assassination, capture and needs dagger, bow, unarmed or psionics.

field.js:875 look() tests canSee(map, e, o, sight) with full sight; the sneak radius (max(2, sight / 3)) is used only for hunting (field.js:777), so a sneaking detail is still spotted. Making look() honour it would also change every FAIL.spotted budget; not part of this proposal.

field.js:1648 spawnGroup, :1702 arrivals(), :797 chooseGoals, :1943 ACTOR_KEYS, :1993 saved spawns: same shared pieces as reinforcements-a (arrive groups, march flag, fired flag in the saved spawn list).

mapgen.js:32-41 ZONE_SLOT: an unknown zone name falls back to the mid slot and draws a ring there; a name mapped to scatter (mapgen.js:218-220 zoneFor returns null) creates no zone, so at: dark needs one ZONE_SLOT line.

Measured (ARR/results/final-n100; 800 runs on the 8 legal types): the call fires in 74% of runs (recon 55, pursuit 56, capture 62, rescue 76, assassination 79, raid 86, sabotage 87, siege 91) and reaches the squad in 43%; walking time median 31 s (p10 24, p90 65); 44% of calls are made after the squad has started to leave. On the other types it fires in 23% (escort), 25% (extermination), 27% (survival), 37% (hold), 42% (retrieval), 47% (expedition) of runs, because the squad kills every spotter inside 30 s: hence the only list.
Lever, 40 runs per type on the 8 types (ARR/results/lever-n40, 320 runs per arm): fired / reached with witness delay 15 s 89% / 66%, 30 s 77% / 42%, 60 s 50% / 27%; with Night at 30 s 55% / 31%.
Retreat at first calm moment after contact, 8 types, n=320: 0.013 base against 0.025 with the call (standard errors 0.010 and 0.015). Final-build no-retreat figures below.
proposals.change:
MODS: reinforcements: { label: 'Reinforcements', weight: 24, reward: 1.35, only: ['recon', 'assassination', 'rescue', 'pursuit', 'sabotage', 'capture', 'raid', 'siege'], mods: { arrivals: [{ on: 'witness', delay: 30, from: 'dark', share: 0.35 }] } }. Same arrivals key as reinforcements-a. Generated desc: "A hostile that has seen the squad and is still alive 30 s (0:06) later calls a second garrison: 35% of each hostile and patrol group (at least 1 body each; 5 bodies on this paper) arrives on unexplored ground at least 13 tiles from the squad and walks at it. Killing every spotter first, or finishing the Leave no witnesses job, cancels the call."

CONSUMERS. Shared with reinforcements-a: MT.arrivalCast (roll() after terms, at: 'dark'), mapgen deferral, spawnGroup march flag, chooseGoals default branch, ACTOR_KEYS 'march', the skip in the two re-spawn loops, bestiary brief row text, the pseudoZone species list, the per-twist tally. Specific to this design: (1) mapgen.js ZONE_SLOT gets dark: 'scatter'. (2) field.js look() (:877) also sets e.spottedAt = s.clock; ACTOR_KEYS gets 'spottedAt'. (3) arrivals(): an entry with on: 'witness' is due when some hostile or patrol e is alive, not extracted, not march, has spottedAt !== null and s.clock - e.spottedAt >= delay. (4) New darkAhead(s): over the map tiles pick the nearest passable tile that is unrevealed (s.seen), has map.dist at least 4 more than the furthest squad member's and is at least SIGHT + 4 tiles from every squad member; g.points becomes that tile and spawnGroup's modulo spreads the bodies around it; if the map is fully explored use the far zone. The cost is one pass over at most 100 x 40 tiles, once. The log line names the witness: "Goblin saw them 30 s ago and is still standing: 5 more come out of the dark, about 33 s away". (5) sideCheck quiet effect (:467): for every hostile set spottedAt = null (not Infinity: JSON turns it into null on save anyway and missiontypes.js:37 forbids it), so "nobody carried word" is true of the call as well as the counter. (6) fieldview.js drawActors: a small mark over each living hostile with spottedAt !== null while the call is pending, which shows the player who can still carry word; a dead spotter's mark disappears with it. (7) brief row text: "arrives from unexplored ground once a spotter lives 0:06". (8) Tests: call fires exactly when a spotter reaches 30 s alive; a spotter killed at 29 s prevents it; quiet clears; save / restore keeps spottedAt and fired.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Reinforcements x1.35" with the generated desc and the factor list; on the 8 legal types only. Map: living spotters carry a mark until they die or the call goes out; at the call a line appears in the log and the column's ghost tokens appear at the edge of the dark and walk toward the squad. There is no ring before the call, because the origin is chosen from what the squad has not yet seen.

REWARD x1.35. Same rule, inputs for this design, 800 paired runs on its 8 types: wins 66.8 to 59.5%, deaths 0.369 to 0.495 per run, fee per won contract 193 / 189, drops 39.9 to 43.4 gems per run (240 paired runs): (0.668 x 193 + 39.9 + 200 x 0.126 - 43.4) / (0.595 x 189) = 1.34, rounded to 1.35. The player's check is the same as in reinforcements-a, plus the log line that names the witness, which makes each call attributable.

FREQUENCY. weight 24, only the 8 types above. The type list limits the twist to contracts where a spotter survives 30 s in at least half the runs (garrisons that are spread out or patrolled). Per contract: 2.9% at level 1, 4.4% at 5, 6.3% at 10, 8.2% at 15, 10.5% at 20, against 3.4 / 4.8 / 7.2 / 9.7 / 12.2% today. A board of 5 has one at least 14% of the time at level 1 and 28% at level 10.
proposals.playerEffect: The twist gives the player two things to read: which contracts carry it (only the patrol and garrison types) and who is carrying word during the run (the marks and the log line). The levers are squad composition (burst and ranged kit that clears spotters inside 30 s), the Leave no witnesses job, and the contract's own sight rule: Night cuts the call from 77% to 55% of runs. The window is a dial the table measures: 15 s calls in 89% of runs, 30 s in 77%, 60 s in 50%. Where the squad wipes the garrison fast (extermination, escort, survival) the call never fires, which is why those types are excluded rather than paid for nothing. The cost when it does fire is concentrated on the contract rather than on lives: on the 8 types wins fall 66.8 to 59.5% and deaths rise 0.369 to 0.495 per run.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat order: the call comes from ahead, so a squad that orders the retreat walks away from it; at the first calm moment after contact deaths are 0.025 against 0.013 for the base (n=320; the difference is inside the error). Without a retreat, 44% of calls are made after the squad has started to leave, so a late call chases rather than blocks. Side jobs: Leave no witnesses gets a second effect, so its x1.3 pay and its risk (the taker walks off alone against every patrol) are now weighed against the call; it exists only on 5 of the 8 types, so on pursuit, raid and siege the only lever is kill speed. Night: halves sight, hence the call. FAIL.spotted bonuses (recon, rescue, assassination, sabotage): the counter the bonus reads is the one that arms the call, so a squad that earns the "never seen" bonus has also prevented the call. Wounds: injured survivors 16.6% to 20.4%, sorties 40% to 47%. Debrief: fights per run 5.30 to 6.00. Higher regime (5-star squads, level up to 8, 160 runs on the 8 types): wins 57.5 to 54.4%, deaths 0.625 to 0.769. Loot: drops +3.6 gems per run, counted in the price.
proposals.risks: The call reaches the squad in only 43% of runs on its own types (fires 74%); the multiplier prices the average over those runs, which means a squad that kills spotters fast keeps the x1.35 without paying for it. That is the intended lever; so that a call or its absence can be attributed, the log names the witness and the marks show who is left. look() ignores the sneak radius (field.js:875), so a strike detail does not avoid being spotted; fixing that changes spotted-bonus budgets and is a separate decision. darkAhead assumes map.dist grows toward the objective; on ring-shaped maps (settlement) "ahead" can mean "around the wall", which is still unexplored ground out of sight. Delay 30 s is 6 real seconds at 1x; the dial table above is the tradeoff. Alternative rejected: the same trigger from the far zone (reach 34%) and a contact clock from the dark (fires 92%, reaches 67%, wins -9.2, deaths +0.095): the witness version is the only one with a lever the player can name. Reinforcements-a and -b can coexist in the code as two entries of the same mods key; they cannot both be on one contract because they are one table row.

proposals.title: Overrun: every rank-and-file group is fielded as if the level expected one more grade, so it arrives as a pack, swarm or tide
proposals.problem: The card says Infested, and a place that is infested is overrun, not upgraded. The game already has the rule for that: swarm() turns every grade a group sits below what its level expects into x2.2 bodies, 4.5 levels lower, in packs, and the brief already prints "a pack / a swarm / a tide" and warns that the ground decides how many reach the squad. Nothing makes a contract that is not already below its level's grade use it. This design raises the expected grade by one for the contract: the same enemy, more of it, smaller, and fought on the ground the map gives. Measured on the harness it costs contracts and wounds but not lives, and the extra kills pay through drops, so it needs no pay multiplier.
evidence: missiontypes.js:286-318 NATIVE(lv) (0 below level 6, 1 from 6, 2 from 12, 3 from 17), HORDE_SWELL 2.2, HORDE_STEP 4.5, HORDE_CAP 40 (HORDE_CAP_PER 20 for per groups), HORDE_PACK [0, 5, 9, 14]; swarm(group, lv) computes gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)) at :312 and returns the group unchanged when gap < 1 or the count would not rise.

proposals.change:
MODS: infested: { label: 'Infested', weight: 13, reward: 1.00, not: ['duel'], mods: { swell: 1 } }. MT.modsOf folds swell by sum, capped at 2. Generated desc: "Hostile and patrol groups are fielded as if the level expected 1 more grade than it does: x2.2 bodies and 4.5 levels lower per grade of gap, in packs of 5, 9 or 14; a group already at 40 bodies (20 per wave) is unchanged. On this paper: 10 to 22 basic, 5 to 11 veteran." The card shows no multiplier tag for it (the reward is 1.00) and the title says why: "paid in kill drops: +7 kills x 6 gems on this paper".

(1) missiontypes.js swarm(group, lv, bonus = 0): gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) + bonus - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)); roll() (:945) maps each group through swell(g) = { plain = swarm(g, lv); inflated = swarm(g, lv, mods.swell); return inflated.count > plain.count ? inflated : plain }. The comparison matters: a group already at the cap would otherwise get a deeper levelOffset with no extra bodies (checked on rolled casts at level 13: basic x40 at -9 would become x40 at -14, a weaker body for the same count). (2) MOD_TEXT.swell line with the counts. (3) Nothing else. CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Infested" (no multiplier) with the generated desc; the expect line shows "Water Slime lvl 1 x26" with the horde tag. Brief: the existing pack / swarm / tide tag and the note "How many can reach the squad at once is set by where the fight opens". Map: packs of small bodies together (mapgen.js packs), and the existing log text for ground ("meet ... in a doorway") on each fight. The decision the card supports is the map: the contract names its ground (Ruins, Wilds, Warren, Outpost...) and MAPS[...].cover is the number behind it.

REWARD x1.00. Same rule. Inputs: wins 69.5 to 62.1% (the lost fee is 11.5 gems per run), deaths 0.258 to 0.253 (no death premium), kills 9.4 to 16.6, drops 54.1 to 96.3 gems per run (+42.3): (0.695 x 167 + 54.1 + 200 x (-0.005) - 96.3) / (0.621 x 173) = 0.68. A multiplier below 1 would read as a penalty, so the value is 1.00 and the surplus stays with the player: expected income per attempt is about +18% (fee 109.6 + drops 96.3 against 121.1 + 54.1 gems per run). The player's check is the brief: the kill count is on the paper (the quota rows are larger) and the drops are the number they already see in the settle line. If the overseer wants the surplus gone, the lever is the drop formula (missions.js:242 does not scale with the body's level), not this row.

FREQUENCY. weight 13, not duel (a bout group of 1-3 veterans at level below 6 has gap 0 even with the bonus, so the row would be inert there). Per contract: 3.4% at level 1, 5.1% at 5, 7.5% at 10, 10.1% at 15, 12.4% at 20 (today 3.4 / 5.1 / 7.5 / 10.0 / 12.7%).
proposals.playerEffect: The decision is the ground and the squad. The card names the map and the brief says how many bodies come; on open ground a tide of 26 reaches the squad at once, in a doorway it reaches two at a time. Players pick Infested contracts on Ruins or Wilds (wins fall 2.7 points there against 11.0 on the middle covers) or bring a squad that holds a line or hits an area, and the existing stand play does the rest (0.08 to 0.14 per run at levels up to 8: a 75% increase in how often the squad chooses its ground). The pay arrives as drops: 7 more kills per run at about 6 gems each.
proposals.secondOrder: This is the wounds twist: deaths do not move (14.7% to 14.1% of runs), while injured survivors go 14.4% to 18.3% and sorties with an injured member 38% to 47%, so under loop-wounds it converts death risk into recovery time and into contracts the squad breaks off (run-aways 26.6% to 32.9%). Lodging and meals matter more with it (restFor, FED_REST in the wound recovery rate), and a support role is worth more (u-wounds: 12.6% against 16.2% injured). Retreat order: a retreat ends the contract as a loss, and this twist already makes the squad quit more often, so the order's cost is the contract fee that the twist makes harder to earn. Debrief: fights per run fall 6.21 to 5.77 while bodies per fight rise, so casts are spent in fewer, bigger fights. Hardcore: escalate() re-spawns 50% of g.count, which is the swollen count, so Infested + Hardcore escalates harder (a 22-body group adds 11); this is consistent with the labels and rare (Infested with Hardcore on 0.06% of level-1, 0.25% of level-10 and 0.63% of level-20 contracts). Existing quirk surfaced: gem drops per kill do not scale with the body's fielded level, so every existing horde contract pays through the same channel; fixing that would change this twist's price.
proposals.risks: Income per attempt is about 18% above the base at multiplier 1.00, so a player who reads the brief will prefer these contracts. If that is not wanted, change the drop formula first (it does not scale with the body's level). Above level 12 the basic groups are already at the 40-body cap, so only veteran and elite groups swell (the capped-group guard); the harness reaches level 8, not 12+, so the effect there is predicted by the code, not measured. Packs of 40 at -9 levels cost the simulation time (hostiles 21 to 35 at level 8; field.js attrition and combat.js caps already bound a fight). Wins fall most on arena, settlement, warren, outpost and road (-11 to -16 points, n = 51-175 each), which are open or built maps, but dungeon (cover 0.10) loses only 4: "tight maps are cheap" holds for cover 0.35-0.45 and is not a monotone rule. Rejected alternative with data: promotion by species grade (infested-a's problem).

surveys.stateOfGame:
Hunted (missiontypes.js:829) and Turncoat (:833) are table rows with no consumer. The board rolls them (current table, 60000 rolls per level: Hunted 2.2 / 3.4 / 4.7 / 8.1% of contracts at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20, Turncoat 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.2%) and each multiplies the payout (x1.4, x1.5), so a tagged contract plays exactly like an untagged one. Movement model: hostiles are placed at launch and walk only after they see the squad, remember it for GIVE_UP = 20 s, or sit inside an alarm (field.js chooseGoals hostile loop :766-815). Nothing moves behind the squad. Fights are grouped at ENGAGE = 2 tiles (findSkirmishes :1197), resolved once when they open (openSkirmish :1219, combat.js encounter :613) and then played back. The ward of escort and rescue is not a combatant: it has no species, so sortie.js fighterFor returns null for it (:133). Measured over 960 baseline escort and rescue sorties, 0 ended with a dead ward, and the cast flag frail (missiontypes.js:414, 599) is read nowhere.

Method. Combat-backed runner: a copy of the retreat unit's loop2/real.js, which calls combat.js C.encounter through the same resolve, REGEN tick and tactics as sortie.js; 4 random 3-5 star characters with no gear or potions; contract level 1-4 (escort and rescue also 1-8); 40 seeds per type in 3 seed blocks, identical seeds in baseline and arm. I used this and not test/field.harness.js because the harness runs field.js's plain attrition resolver and cannot show combat.js deaths. Baseline over 1800 sorties: win 68.4%, 0.251 deaths per sortie, 14.2% of sorties with a death, 14.7% of survivors under the 0.4 wound line (the loop-wounds rule gives the same 14% the wounds unit measured, so the runner agrees with it). Reference twists on the same seeds: Night x1.15 gives +3% deaths and +3.5 win points; No resupply x1.25 gives +35% deaths; Hardcore x1.6 gives 0% before it escalates. Fights are short: p50 2.6 s, p90 8.2 s over 3789 fights; 66% of fights and 62% of deaths are 3.6 s or shorter. Over 450 baseline sorties 76 of 100 deaths happen after the squad has started leaving (field.js phase 'leaving'), which is the part of a run that nothing currently threatens from behind. Two ideas were measured and rejected: hostiles that survive a break-off keep tracking the squad (0.21 to 0.22 and 0.68 to 0.69 deaths per sortie, no change); the ward re-raising the alarm every 10 or 20 s (0.50 to 0.49). Extra bodies in a fight and a lower squad HP are the levers that move the numbers. Prototype code and raw runs: C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\pursuit (run.js, run2.js, proj\field.js, proj2\field.js, analyze.js, freq.js, final.sh).

Four designs, one pair per twist. Hunted A (one follower, joins at fight open) and Turncoat A (the ward turns) are the smallest and reuse the most existing code. Hunted B (pack that commits when the squad is weak) and Turncoat B (informant who lifts scouting, then poisons the squad) add a cast member each. All four assume the approved u-honesty build (TWISTS rows with mods, MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, rollTwists draw rule with TWIST_FULL = 66) and read the wave 2 counters (counters.fights, counters.spotted, phase 'leaving', a.low). All four add a trial: false flag so no trial offer, including the one-body solo road (quests.js:116 passes trial: true), rolls them. Every multiplier is kept or moved to the measured relative rise in deaths per sortie; none is derived from a formula, and the proposals say so.

proposals.title: Hunted A: one follower, added to any fight that opens while the squad averages under 70% HP
proposals.problem: Hunted rolls on every type except duel (missiontypes.js:829-830, weight 8, pays x1.4) and has no consumer; the id appears nowhere else in the .js files. The row promises something that follows the squad and joins the fight going worst. The engine has no body that moves behind the squad (field.js:766-815), and a body that walks to a fight in progress arrives too late: fights are resolved once at open and 66% of fights and 62% of deaths are 3.6 s or shorter, which is how long a follower 4 tiles behind needs to close to 2 tiles at 0.55 tiles per second. The join has to be decided when the fight opens. The walk out is the unthreatened part of a run: 76 of 100 baseline deaths happen after the squad has started leaving.
evidence: missiontypes.js:829-830 hunted row (weight 8, x1.4, not duel and arena); no other .js file mentions the id. Frequency on the current table over rollTwists: 2.2 / 3.4 / 4.7 / 8.1% of contracts at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20.

field.js:766-815 chooseGoals hostile loop and :62 GIVE_UP: a hostile moves only when it sees the squad, remembers it for 20 s or is inside an alarm. field.js:1648 spawnGroup, :1662 makeActor and :1702 arrivals (cued(at) at :1705) already place a cast group at a chosen point on a cue.

field.js:1197-1217 findSkirmishes groups actors within ENGAGE = 2 (:55) transitively; :1219 openSkirmish calls s.resolve once before the fight record exists; combat.js:613 encounter resolves the whole fight in one call. A follower is either in the actor lists handed to resolve or not in the fight.
Measured, 3789 fights in 600 sorties: fight length p50 2.6 s, p90 8.2 s, max 40.5 s. Fights longer than 3.6 s are 34% of fights and hold 38% of deaths.
Measured, 450 sorties (block D): baseline 100 deaths, 24 in fights before the squad started leaving, 76 after. field.js withdraw() :381 and leave() set phase 'leaving'.
field.js:917 hpOf and :989-1020 escapeHatch: the engine already treats an average squad HP under 0.7 with someone down as a fight to leave. The join uses the same function and the same constant.

A follower in the cast therefore needs no new combat code and appears in the brief (bestiary.js brief :201-212).

CARD. Tag 'Hunted' with the MOD_TEXT above as its title. Brief row: species, level, x1, 'follows the squad', HP when the town has met the species. Intel applies as for any row. MAP. MEASURED (1800 paired sorties, levels 1-4, 15 types): win 68.4% -> 65.8%; deaths per sortie 0.251 -> 0.361 (+44%; per block +0.10, +0.10, +0.13); sorties with a death 14.2% -> 18.5%; the join rule fires in 14.1% of sorties. Of 450 sorties with finer counters: 533 fights involve the follower (58 joins, the rest the squad running into it, 54% of them after the squad started leaving); deaths in follower fights 52, of which 49 after leaving.

MULTIPLIER x1.4, unchanged. It is the measured +44% deaths per sortie, between No resupply (x1.25 for +35%) and the x1.6 cap; no formula. A player can check what is on the card (the follower row, its level and known HP) and the log line with the HP at each join. For a death-based check, u-ledger can add gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, dead } beside gs.field.types and the card prints 'Hunted: N sent, M lost' (S, only if loop-ledger part A lands).

FREQUENCY weight 8, not [duel], trial false. Under the u-honesty draw rule 2.4 / 3.5 / 5.0 / 8.2% of contracts at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 (current table 2.2 / 3.4 / 4.7 / 8.1%); at least one on a 5-contract board 11 / 16 / 23 / 35%.

NOT SHARED WITH B: this follower never starts a fight alone, is added to someone else's fight, is one body, and has to be decided at fight open; B is a pack that starts its own fight between fights.
proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the brief names the follower (species, level, HP when the town has met it). The lever is how often the squad averages under 70% HP when a fight opens: a support role or potions keep it above the line, a larger party spreads damage, and a squad that wins every fight at full HP never sees the follower join and can kill it when it walks into it. During the run there is no new control; the retreat order is the only action. The walk out is where it bites: 54% of follower fights and 94% of the deaths in them happen after the squad has started leaving, so a retreat order is no longer a safe way to end a contract that has gone badly. Each join costs about one death: 253 joins in 1800 sorties, and sorties with a join average 1.3 deaths against 0.15 for sorties without.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat): the follower is pre-marked spotted, so its release does not close the free window (contacted() reads counters.fights and counters.spotted); the walk out runs back along the route the follower trails, which is where it is met most. A retreat order does not remove it from a fight already open. Wounds (u-wounds): survivors under the 0.4 low line 14.7% -> 15.3%, mean injured ticks per survivor 2.08 -> 2.23. Permanent death: 0.251 -> 0.361 per sortie. Tactics: tactics.closing() (:224) counts a found, spotted hostile within 14 tiles, so the follower is a threat to the squad's plans; 'a stand' plays rose from 0.22 to 0.36 per sortie with no tactics change (the cause was not isolated). Chorokinetic: loneTarget() (field.js:946) accepts an elite with nothing within 3 tiles as a strike target, so a wormhole strike can remove the follower (not measured). The follower is a normal kill, so its drops pay and Bestiary.sight records the species. Debrief (u-debrief): one line 'Hunted: the follower joined N fights' from counters.joined.
proposals.risks: All figures come from a runner with no gear or potions; absolute deaths are upper bounds and only the relative change is usable. The baseline moves between seed blocks (0.21, 0.28, 0.27 deaths per sortie), which is why the comparison is paired; the +44% held in every block. elite at -3 levels was chosen from a sweep: veteran tier gives +5%, elite at 0 / -1 / -2 / -3 gives +148% / +100% / +62% / +48% (one block); the jump between tiers is large, so the offset is the tuning dial. The squad kills the follower whenever its own movement runs into it (about 1.1 fights per sortie), which removes the twist for the rest of the run and still pays x1.4. Dungeon re-release on descend is not covered by the measurement. A follower plus the u-honesty Night twist (sight 5) is unmeasured. If the Reinforcements or Infested builders approve a trailing body, the stance code is shared and should land once. fieldview.js, bestiary.js and sortie.js are being edited by the wave 1 build, so line numbers will move. Needs the u-honesty build first.

proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the decision is whether this squad can kill an elite-tier fighter that starts inside its own ranks in its first fight, which makes escort and rescue the first low-risk contracts with a real death rate. The card says so and the multiplier pays for it. Composition levers are the usual ones: burst, a tank, healing. During the run the turn is visible (token swap, log line, new terms) and the player can order a retreat, which in escort did not exist before the turn; the fight with the traitor is already open when the order can be given, so the order helps only if the squad survives that fight.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat): the rewrite moves exitState from 'homeward' to 'order' in escort, so the retreat button appears exactly while the traitor lives; the turn happens at contact, so it does not coincide with the free window. Wounds (u-wounds): survivors under the 0.4 low line 16.2% -> 19.8%, mean injured ticks per survivor 2.44 -> 3.07 at levels 1-8. Permanent death: +0.23 deaths per sortie at levels 1-8, concentrated in the first fight.
