The ward becomes the first place FAIL.died('ward') and the dead-ward log line (field.js kill() :1253) can matter. Betrayal as a resolve shock (calling grieved(s, ward) at the turn, so Tactics.reaction moves resolve by 0.35 x steel) was measured at levels 1-8: 0.71 -> 0.72 deaths per sortie, no change, so it is not included. Debrief: one line 'Turncoat: the ward turned at M:SS'.
proposals.risks: Narrowing only to two types drops retrieval and siege from Turncoat; that is the reason for B. The strength is one dial: veteran tier does nothing, elite tier at -4 gives +63%, at 0 gives +200% (levels 1-8, one block); the traitor is a Death Knight because it is the only elite-tier species matching the escort and rescue themes, so a new elite humanoid in the bestiary changes the calibration. At levels 1-4 the absolute rise is small (0.06 -> 0.10) and the relative rise is +72%, so the x1.5 reads as generous at low level. The turn lands at first contact, which ends the free call-off for every contract under u-retreat; the player has the card's information and nothing else before it. Unturned wards stay invulnerable; making them killable is a separate change that is not proposed. In rescue the fallback measures progress from the freed position and a squad that never frees the ward never sees a turn. wardD0 and the progress test use the exit distance field (fieldTo(s, 'exit')), which changes if the portal moves in a standfast contract; escort and rescue are not standfast. Needs the u-honesty build first; shares quests.js:109-121 with its MT.current edit.

proposals.problem: Same dead row as A (missiontypes.js:829-830). A different reading of 'something follows the squad': a group the player can see and plan around, which acts between fights instead of inside one. The measurement that motivates it: 76 of 100 baseline deaths happen after the squad has started leaving, and hostiles currently give up (GIVE_UP 20 s, field.js:62; HEADSTART 8 s, :63) so a squad that is hurt is rarely met again. A pack that waits behind the squad and commits when the squad is weak puts a second fight in front of exactly the squads that can least afford it.

proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the brief shows a pack of three that will be on the map the whole run. The decision is composition for the second fight: the pack commits when the squad loses a member or drops under 60% HP, so the squad that loses someone in the first fight meets three more veterans about 15 s later. During the run the approach is visible for those seconds, and a squad with a sharp enough mind uses its existing plays: 'a stand' at tighter ground cuts how many of the three reach it at once (combat.js frontage). The player's own action is the retreat order, but the pack is behind the squad on the route out: 98% of the deaths in pack fights happen after the squad has started leaving.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat): pack members are pre-marked spotted, so releasing them leaves counters.spotted and the free window alone; the first commit or adjacency fight closes it like any fight. The walk out meets the pack in 74% of pack fights, so under Hunted B the order is a way to end a bad contract, not a way to be safe. Wounds (u-wounds): survivors under the 0.4 line 14.7% -> 17.1%, mean injured ticks per survivor 2.08 -> 2.49, the larger wound effect of the two Hunted designs. Permanent death: 0.251 -> 0.359 per sortie. Tactics: 'a stand' plays 0.22 -> 0.37 per sortie; step-back plays 0.002 -> 0.011. Chorokinetic wormhole (breakOut :1024) puts the squad at the gate, which is where the pack is closing; the blink does not shake it. proposals.risks: Shares the follows plumbing (TEMPORAL 'trail', arrivals cue, stance key, brief tag) with Hunted A; approve one of the two for the Hunted row. Overlap with the Reinforcements lens: a group that arrives from behind when the squad is hurt is the same mechanism as a Reinforcements design keyed to weakness; if one is approved, do not approve the other. The pack is met on the walk out in most runs regardless of the commit rule, so its effect is partly 'a group stands on the route home'; commit on weakness adds the 23% of sorties where it arrives earlier. Grade is fixed at veteran for all levels; veterans scale with the contract level through M.spawn (35% per level), but the ratio to the contract's own veterans was measured only at levels 1-4 (one block at 1-8 with elite from level 8). Pack members path with the distance field, so a pack behind a long detour arrives late; not measured on the largest maps. Three tokens near the entry add draw cost; negligible. Needs the u-honesty build first.

The squad's use for a guide is the search model: below scouting 80 it has to find the objective before it can walk to it (field.js found :156, known :158, searchBeacon :249), and the party picker already prints the scouting tier ('knows the way' at 80, ai.js SCOUT_TIERS).

NOT SHARED WITH A: the person is added, not the ward; the squad gets something first (scouting 80); the cost is a one-time stat hit with no new hostile and no change to the terms; it covers retrieval and siege.
proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the card says that scouting is lent and that a 30% HP and pool hit follows at the first fight. The decisions: support roles and healing keep the squad's HP up through the hit (in-fight healing and potions count from the first tick); a party with its own scouting at or above 80 gets nothing from the loan and still pays the hit; a party at 0 gets the largest loan (win 55% -> 65% while it lasts). During the run the player sees the hit land with the squad list and can order a retreat: contact has already closed the free window, so the order ends the contract as a loss, taken with the squad at 70% HP.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat): the reveal and the end of the free call-off are the same event (first fight); the order is available right after, and the withdrawn share rises 38.5% -> 46.5%. Wounds (u-wounds): the hit lowers the end-of-fight HP of the first fight and everything after, so survivors under the 0.4 line rise 16.8% -> 22.9% and mean injured ticks per survivor 2.49 -> 3.10, the largest wound effect of the four designs. Permanent death: 0.199 -> 0.283 per sortie. Healing potions supplied by Outfit and support classes matter in the first fight of every Turncoat contract. If No resupply also rolls, both stop recovery through the same check, so the 60 s is absorbed. Debrief: one line 'Turncoat: the informant left at M:SS; HP and pools -30%'. The informant never fights and is never part of any win or fail atom, so a rescue or escort ward and an informant can coexist on one contract.
proposals.risks: Most of the measured cost is the flat 30% hit; the gift is worth about 4 win points against the harness's own scouting mix, so the twist is mostly a stat debuff at first contact. The reveal coincides with the end of the free abort, so a player never sees the betrayal while calling off is free. The hit has no counterplay except composition and retreat. The informant has no function on retrieval or siege except the gift. The measurement does not model the informant as an actor; the new surface is an ally in ours lists (combatant must treat guide like a ward, and extract atoms with who 'squad' ignore it, :1503). Block variance is large (deaths +0.07, 0.00, +0.19 per block), so the +43% has a wide interval. Overlap with Reinforcements is avoided by construction (no spawn); the measured spawn variant is documented above for that lens. scoutOf touches found, known and searchBeacon, which every search-driven contract reads; a bug there changes all of them, so the test list covers the unturned path. Needs the u-honesty build first.

verdicts.attack: It bolts three special cases into combat.js (a noReach family list, a per-family miss add in rollHit, a per-type multiplier in damage()) for a twist whose measured cost on random squads is +0.02 to +0.03 deaths per run and -1.2 win points, and by its own numbers two thirds of that comes from walking x0.8, a term with no decision attached. The one decision it creates ('do not send bows or fire casters in rain') is learned once and never changes per contract. x1.05 is 6 gems on a level-3 contract; no player will notice the tag. The flat price hides where the walking term lands: makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308) and is not scaled by move, so window contracts (escort, rescue: deadline true, exitFor missiontypes.js:192-196) take the whole tax; the builder's own file shows rescue 77% to 67% wins and 0.07 to 0.12 deaths from the move term alone, while recon and extermination lose nothing. storm-b uses the Elements status the card describes and is the shape the user's axes preference asks for.

verdicts.demand: Not salvageable as a separate design: approve storm-b reworked instead. If any storm keeps a walking term it must either exempt or scale window contracts (shutsAt, field.js:1308) and state the per-type cost on the card.

Soaked is a cliff (5 stacks: heat 0.8, lightning/cold/poison -0.5, elements.js:171): a Water Slime cast adds stacks to a squad that starts at 3, and the card's 'Wet x3' does not say two hits away from Soaked. The walking term carries the same unpriced window-contract tax as storm-a. Status persistence across fights (no combatEnd removal) and the facet schema list (facet.schema.ig.js:115) add coupling for a twist that moves nothing on average.

verdicts.demand: Drop missChanceBy from the shared wet definition (or propose it separately as a water rule with its own measurement across all water spells). Drop walking x0.8 or scale window shutsAt by 1/move as well as the Hardcore window, and report escort and rescue separately. Put the Soaked threshold on the card ('two more Wet applications on a member reach Soaked: ...') and tag Water Slime rows on the brief. Re-derive the price after those changes with the same formula and state it as data on the row. Add trial: false so a solo star trial never carries it.

verdicts.attack: A single veteran at mission level against a squad that has just finished the job is won 88% of the time; the mid-run 'decision' (retreat = certain loss, fight = 88% win) has one rational answer, so nothing is decided during the run and the pre-launch lever (bring a healer) is the generic one. The escort loss (100% to 79%) is attributed to 'the ward stands in the fight', which the code does not support: the ward has no fighter (sortie.js:133) and is dropped from the party list and the dead list (sortie.js:155-156, 180). The likelier cause is a stall: escort's pressure is 'ambush' (missiontypes.js:411), under which a hostile moves only while it sees the squad (field.js:805), while guard orders leash every squad member within 2 tiles of the ward (field.js:738-740), so a mark spawned 8-11 tiles away behind cover never closes and the squad never reaches it; the run then ends by ABANDON or the doneAt rule, which is minutes of nothing on screen and a loss. Fixed grade 'veteran' makes the twist weaker as level rises and the price drifts. Pay drops 1.5 to 1.15 on 1.2% of contracts: the player will not notice the tag.

Scratchpad proto/exp holds real.js, t2.js and the patched field.js; the 750-run trap table was not found as a file, so those figures are unverified beyond the method existing.
verdicts.demand: Explain the escort loss with a log sample before escort stays in 'only'; if it is the ambush-pressure stall, give the mark an unconditional hunt (the same march flag reinforcements-a adds to chooseGoals) or drop escort. Set the mark's grade from the cast (the cast's top grade, or NATIVE(lv)+1) so it stays a threat at every level, and re-measure the price. Add trial: false. Keep weight 6. The log line must state the mechanic ('veteran <species> spawned 9 tiles away; new term: kill the target'), not 'The paper was wrong'.

verdicts.attack: An L-size second-mission state machine (18 mission fields copied, about 20 state fields reset, a new map, a rebuilt portal) for an effect the player cannot tell from trap-a's: -7.6 win points, +0.005 deaths, sprung runs won 89%. The one thing that differs, loadouts planned for the written species, is information the player cannot act on because the inner species are not on the paper. It excludes the two cargo types the card lists, so the twist shrinks to three types at 0.7% of contracts, and the difficulty follows the inner type's own curve while pay stays the written type's, so the card figure stops describing the run. The log line 'The floor gives way' is metaphor (ui-prose-engineer-style).

The per-inner-type table (duel 73.3%, survival 39.6%, raid 0.467 deaths) and the 450-run extermination figure were not found as files.
verdicts.demand: None that saves it. If a type change is wanted later it needs the cargo move solved and a reason the player would prepare differently than for trap-a; until then trap-a's term rewrite covers the card.

verdicts.attack: It is mostly a bigger fight: 35% more bodies, printed on the paper, with a timer and a direction. The decision it adds is the timing of the retreat order, which u-retreat already provides; the column only raises that lever's value. +0.16 deaths per run (+63%) and 20.7% of runs with a death for x1.25 prices a death at 200 gems, which the user does not accept as a price. 14% of firings land after the squad has already withdrawn, so a squad that broke off from a lost fight walks into the column at the entry: the worst permadeath case is the one the design does not treat. Trials are not excluded, and a one-body solo trial gets at least one extra body per written group. Column kills count toward the extermination quota.

Name the arriving actors' field flag the same as the pursuit lens's (one key in ACTOR_KEYS for 'moves on its own trigger').

verdicts.attack: On its own eight types the call fires in 74% of runs and reaches the squad in 43%, so on most contracts the x1.35 is paid for nothing; where it does not fire that is because the squad's AI killed the spotters inside 30 s (6 real seconds), not because the player did anything. The spotter marker is information with no control: no tactics play targets spotters, and look() ignores the sneak radius (field.js:875-876) so a strike detail cannot avoid making one. 44% of calls come after the squad has started leaving. Weight 24 doubles the row on eight types to compensate for 'only', an arbitrary hike. darkAhead is a new placement routine for a reach rate of 43%.

The 8-type subset itself was not re-aggregated.
verdicts.demand: Do not build as the Reinforcements row. Keep the witness trigger as a later second entry of the arrivals key, only on the five types that offer Leave no witnesses, where the job is the player's lever and its x1.3 pay is weighed against the call; weight back to 12-14. If it is to stand alone it needs a control the player holds during the run or a mind-tier play that hunts spotters, measured.

verdicts.attack: A level bump wearing a tag. A third of each group at +3 levels is the same decision as a higher-level contract, nothing about the fight changes (same species, same count, same ground), and the builder says so ('the only new decision is the one on the paper'). It raises pay to x1.50 for stat inflation and adds a second brief row per group (8 rows for a 4-group cast). It also produces the same cost class as reinforcements-a (+0.14 deaths, -6.9 points) for a higher multiplier, so the two cannot both be right.

Scratchpad final2.txt and final-n100: inf_lvh 62.6%/0.399 (n=1500) matches the proposal exactly.
verdicts.demand: None that saves it. If the card's literal text is wanted, infested-b's swell is the implementation that changes how the fight is played. The SWARMED positive-offset fix should land anyway as a one-line hardening.

verdicts.attack: At x1.00 it pays about +18% expected gems per attempt because kill drops use the mission level, not the body's (missions.js:242), so a player who reads the brief prefers Infested contracts: a complication that is a bonus. Deaths are flat and wounds rise (14.4% to 18.3% of survivors), so under u-wounds it is a downtime tax paid in gems. Above level 12 basic groups already sit at HORDE_CAP 40, so only veteran and elite groups swell; unmeasured. Infested with Hardcore re-spawns 50% of the swollen count (field.js:1557). The generated desc example is wrong for the level it implies: veterans swell only from level 6 (NATIVE 1 + bonus 1 against GRADES index 1), so a paper with '10 to 22 basic' at level 3 shows '5 veteran' unchanged, not '5 to 11'. Trials are not excluded.

Correct the desc example or generate it from the real cast. Measure one level 12-18 cell. Add trial: false. Add one line to the Hardcore MOD_TEXT: escalation re-spawns 50% of the fielded count, swollen or not.

verdicts.attack: The card's idea, joining the fight going worst, is a minority path in the builder's own counters: the join fires in 14% of sorties and accounts for 58 of 533 follower fights; the cost comes from an elite standing on the route out that the squad walks into (54% of follower fights after leaving, 49 of 52 deaths in them). That is the same effect as reinforcements-a's column and hunted-b's pack, with a different trigger. A pre-spotted elite within NEAR 14 tiles counts as 'closing' for tactics every tick (tactics.js:224-231 reads a.spotted), so stand plays rose 0.22 to 0.36 against something that never attacks. The premise '76 of 100 deaths happen after the squad started leaving, the unthreatened part of a run' conflates two states: withdraw() (field.js:383) and leave() (field.js:1875) both set phase 'leaving', so that count includes squads already broken and running. x1.4 for +0.11 deaths against reinforcements-a's x1.25 for +0.16.

Re-measure; the price is then for the join and the design is distinct from Reinforcements. Either exclude stance actors from Tactics.closing() or state the stands as intended. Split the 'leaving' statistic into after-leave() and after-withdraw() before using it as a premise. Thread the trial flag through quests.js:116 explicitly as a change.

verdicts.attack: By the builder's own sensitivity table the commit rule does not matter (0.5/0.6/0.7 HP give 0.34/0.33/0.34 deaths; committing on the walk out changes nothing) and 475 of 639 pack fights and 84 of 86 pack-fight deaths are on the walk out: it is three veterans standing on the route home, which is reinforcements-a's column with a different trigger and no printed arrival time, and the builder says not to approve both. The visible approach the squad's plays react to is the same tactics false-alarm as hunted-a (pre-spotted bodies within NEAR).

verdicts.demand: None; superseded by reinforcements-a (same mechanism) and by a reworked hunted-a (the distinct join).

verdicts.attack: The turn lands at the first fight beside the ward, which is first contact, the same second the free call-off ends under u-retreat: an elite Death Knight appears inside the squad's ranks in its first fight with no reaction window and nothing the player decides during the run. +63% deaths at levels 1-8 (0.371 to 0.606) on the two safest contract types, and the weight hike 5 to 12 puts it on one escort or rescue in eight at level 20. The pre-launch decision is a difficulty gate (can this squad kill a level-3 elite); a squad that can does so on any escort. The traitor is always a Death Knight because it is the only elite species with humanoid or undead tags, so a merchant becomes a Death Knight on every Turncoat contract. Unturned wards stay invulnerable and frail (missiontypes.js:414, 599) stays unread.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS.turncoat missiontypes.js:833 (weight 5, x1.5, four types); ward has no species so fighterFor returns null (sortie.js:133) and resolve's one-sided fight cancels with noFightUntil +120 (:158-160); combatant() ward rule field.js:1185-1195; escalate() rewrites and saves :1537-1561; ward goal exit :757-764, GUARD_LEASH 2 :49; makeActor :1662-1688; ACTOR_KEYS has role/side/grade/species/hp/power/speed/wits/levelOffset :1943; escort and rescue are deadline true so exitFor gives 'window' (:192-196, :409, :595); elite bestiary entries missions.js:51-56: three slimes, stone golem, death_knight, the last the only one tagged humanoid/undead, matching escort (humanoid, beast, goblin) and rescue (humanoid, goblin, undead) themes. Scratchpad f_tbase8_*/f_ta8_*: 70.4%/0.371 to 63.8%/0.606 (n=480), matching; f_tbase4_*/f_ta4_*: 85.2%/0.060 to 82.1%/0.104, matching. quests.js:116 passes no trial flag today.
verdicts.demand: Trigger only at the progress point (half the walk, rescue after freeing), never at the first fight, so the squad meets the garrison at full strength first and the turn is a second act with a visible lead; re-measure. Keep weight 5. Thread trial: false through quests.js:116 as an explicit change. Decide what frail means: either an unturned ward becomes killable (so FAIL.died can fire and the retreat state is honest) or delete the flag. The turn log line states species, grade and offset, not 'is not what the contract said'.

verdicts.attack: A flat 30% HP and pool debuff at first contact with a scouting loan worth about 4 win points attached. The builder's own risks say it: 'mostly a stat debuff at first contact', 'no counterplay except composition and retreat'. The informant never fights, is never in a term, and on retrieval and siege does nothing but the gift. The final-run files do not support the price: tbbase 61.7%/0.199 to tb 53.2%/0.315 deaths per sortie (+58%, -8.5 points), not the 53.5%/0.283 (+43%) the x1.4 was set from. scoutOf reaches found(), known() and searchBeacon(), which every search-driven contract reads, for a twist with no decision.

Scratchpad f_tbbase_*/f_tb_* re-aggregated (720 paired sorties, the design's own final.sh arm TURN=b TRIG=contact POISON=0.3 NOSPAWN=1): 61.7%/0.199 to 53.2%/0.315, which contradicts the proposal's 0.283.
verdicts.demand: None. A debuff is not a complication; the Turncoat row is served by a reworked turncoat-a.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

verdicts.attack: Depends on code that is not in the tree: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current or TWIST_FULL (grep over *.js returns nothing); u-honesty is approved but unbuilt, and its spec removes the storm row to a comment block, so this unit must be sequenced after it. Hidden cost: six types carry deadline: true (escort :409, assassination :524, rescue :595, pursuit :618, sabotage :640, capture :708) and exitFor (missiontypes.js:195) gives them the window exit, whose shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313); walking x0.8 lengthens every walk 25% against an unchanged window, and the generated tooltip says nothing about it (only Hardcore's clock is scaled). The rescue figures in the builder's own data (77% to 71%, 0.07 to 0.12 deaths, walking alone) are that term. Heat typing is inconsistent: combat.js:303 types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type, :308 types its splash 'arcane', so heat splash escapes the x0.5. The row duplicates an axis that exists: Elements wet (elements.js:170) already models 'heat resisted'; damage: {heat: 0.5} is a second constant for the same thing. For about two thirds of squads the twist does nothing measurable, so the paper carries a tag that changes nothing on most contracts.

The scratchpad combat.js patch is exactly the 9 lines claimed, at the cited sites. verdicts.attack: Same population effect as storm-a (random squads 0.133 vs 0.132 deaths per run; the builder says so) for a larger surface: it edits the shared 'wet' definition (elements.js:170), which changes every water-word spell (spellcraft.js:54 'water' inflicts wet) and every Water Slime attack in the game, not only storms; it adds a status descriptor field (missChanceBy) keyed on a weapon family, a new axis in elements.js that facet.schema.ig.js:115 has to learn; and it relies on statuses persisting across fights on cached fighters (sortie.js:120 caches a.fighter; combat.js:655 fires combatEnd for the party only), which the top-up loop papers over. The cost is species-coupled by design (melee squad deaths x4.6 against Ice Slimes, x3.7 against Cave Spiders at the same flat 1.05), so the printed price is wrong on exactly the contracts where the twist matters, and the proposed fix is a brief tag. 'Approve at most one' of the two storms: storm-a is the smaller, verified diff.

verdicts.attack: Re-arms the abandonment rule: springAmbush sets s.doneAt = null, and verdict() withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (field.js:1636); a squad that reaches the way home late (the builder's own recon p90 is 1.01 of the estimate; ABANDON is 2.5) is pulled out at the spring instead of fighting. The mark is fixed at 'veteran' with GRADE_BUMP 0 (sortie.js:27), while NATIVE(lv) (missiontypes.js:286) makes veterans the rank and file from level 6 and elites from 12, so the ambusher is weaker than one written body from level 6 on and the twist decays to nothing while still paying 1.15; the scratchpad springA already derives the grade from the cast's top grade and the proposal discards that. On escort the ward can be delivered a step before the first squad member enters the ring (leave() :1895-1900 extracts the ward on inPortal; the predicate counts squad members only), so the 'ward in the fight' claim holds only sometimes and escort still loses 21 points. Depends on u-honesty (mods) and u-retreat (contacted/exitState), neither built.

verdicts.attack: Largest and most fragile of the twelve for the same measured effect as trap-a (-7.6 win points, +0.005 deaths against trap-a's -8.9 and +0.012). pit() copies 18 mission fields and resets about 20 run fields by hand; save() (field.js:1975-1999) enumerates the run state explicitly, so every field pit() forgets (the prototype springB leaves beaconAt, leaveNow, sideWin, floorNo, counters.floor semantics) is carried into the new map and saved. The squad's loadouts stay planned for the written cast because missions.js:105 caches by signature plus zone id; the 'flexible builds matter' effect is a cache artefact, not a design. Card, ledger (loop-ledger per-type record), ESCALATION[m.type] and intel all key on the written type while the run is a different one. Cargo types are excluded because the prototype could not carry a ward or relic across (0% and 2% wins), leaving only recon, expedition and pursuit: 0.7% of contracts for an L-sized state transplant. The inner list is a lethal-by-data dial (raid 0.467 deaths per run).

verdicts.attack: Three things the proposal does not handle. (1) Stale offers: the column is added to mission.cast at roll time, so every board offer (re-rolled every 6 minutes, sortie.js:97) and every held trial offer (quests.js:112 keeps the pair until the star changes) rolled before this lands carries the tag and no column; only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check. (2) describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast, so the card's hostile figure includes the column while the brief lists it as 'later'. (3) The win quota for extermination (kill 80% of the written count, :352) is met by column kills because counters.killed counts by role; the builder admits it and prices it in rather than fixing it. roll() has to compute tw before the cast (today tw is read at :954, after terms at :952), which changes RNG order for every seeded harness. On hold, siege and survival the column fires in 74-88% and reaches in 52-72%, so 1.25 is paid on contracts where it does nothing. The price rule (R = 200 plus drop income) is one of three different rules across the lenses. Measured on a private runner with gearless parties, not on test/sortie.harness.js.

Scratchpad proj2 diff matches (arrive groups, march flag, contactAt in look and openSkirmish, SWARMED positive branch, mapgen dark slot and deferred). results/final-n100 aggregated by me: base n 1500 69.5% / 0.258 (exact match), reinf_a 64.9% / 0.423 over 15 types, consistent with the quoted 13-type 64.8% / 0.410. dry1.txt matches the Night/No resupply figures exactly. Frequencies: my simulation of the current rule gives reinforcements 3.1/4.8/7.1/11.9% at L1/5/10/20 against the quoted 3.4/4.8/7.2/12.2.
verdicts.demand: After u-honesty and u-retreat. Add the stale-offer check (MT.current compares the twist's expected cast groups), exclude march bodies from describe().hostiles and from the written kill quota (or print that they count), and skip arrive groups in both respawn loops as written. Build the arrive/march plumbing as the one cue-spawn mechanism the hunted and trap designs also use (see conflicts). Reproduce the 1300-run comparison on test/sortie.harness.js and price with the agreed rule before 1.25 is fixed.

verdicts.attack: Sound mechanically, but it ships three things unsettled. The price 1.50 comes from the arrivals rule (R = 200, drop loss counted); under the terrain lens's rule (R = PULL_COST, no drops) the same inputs give about 1.31, so the two lenses would print incompatible factors side by side on the honesty card. A promoted kin group is a separate cast group, and mapgen.build() (:329-340) places each group on its own scatter/around/packs call, so the 'stronger specimens of the same nest' stand somewhere else on the map unless placement shares points by kin. A held trial offer or board entry rolled before this lands carries 'Infested' with an unpromoted cast and pays x1.50 for nothing until re-rolled (quests.js:112 keeps trial offers). The twist adds +0.14 deaths per run and the builder states the only new decision is reading a second brief row; the alternative row (infested-b) adds no deaths, which is the axis the user weighs most.

Include the SWARMED fix and the kin naming; place kin groups together in mapgen (share the first group's points) or say on the brief that they are placed apart; add the MT.current cast check; price under the one agreed rule; re-measure on test/sortie.harness.js. verdicts.attack: The column reaches the squad in 43% of runs on its own eight types (fires in 74%), so x1.35 is paid on average for a thing that happens less than half the time; the builder calls that the lever. The only list of eight types is tuned to the harness's kill speed (the call fires in under 50% of runs elsewhere), which is a hard-coded behaviour that drifts with any combat change. weight 24 doubles the row's share; under u-honesty's draw rule (odds x min(1, poolWeight/66)) the per-type pool on those types becomes 88-96, so this row suppresses every other twist there (my simulation: night 7.9% to 7.1%, dry 6.5% to 6.1%, hardcore 5.7% to 5.0% at level 10 with the B weights). Marks count as spotters (role mark is not structure), so a bodyguard mark that sees the squad calls a column; unstated. darkAhead assumes map.dist grows toward the objective (settlement rings break it; admitted). Shares every piece of plumbing with reinforcements-a, so it cannot be built independently of the a/b decision.

Replace the tuned only list with the rule itself (the call fires only if a spotter survives the delay) and either price the inert cases or exclude types by a stated criterion, not by harness output. Decide marks explicitly. Build on the same cue-spawn mechanism as reinforcements-a and the hunted follower, and measure on test/sortie.harness.js. The overseer approves at most one of reinforcements-a and reinforcements-b.

verdicts.attack: At multiplier 1.00 the builder's own numbers give expected income per attempt about 18% above the base (drops 54.1 to 96.3 gems per run, fee 121.1 to 109.6), because rollLoot (missions.js:238-242) pays (2 + 1.5 x level) per kill regardless of the body's fielded level. A complication that is strictly favourable inverts the honesty premise: players take every Infested contract and the tag reads as a bonus. The builder names the fix (scale drops by fielded level) and declines to own it. Above level 12 basic groups sit at HORDE_CAP 40 (missiontypes.js:295), so the row is inert for them and only veteran/elite groups swell; not measured (harness reaches level 8). Hostiles per run rise 13 to 24 (35 at level 8), the only perf cost of the twelve that is measured, and not measured in the browser. Hardcore's escalate() respawns 50% of the swollen count (field.js:1559), admitted and rare.

Decide the surplus before it ships: either a separate approved change to rollLoot (gems scaled by the body's fielded level, which changes every existing horde contract) or a reward below 1.00 printed on the card as the drop-share line the builder already drafts. Measure hostiles per run and frame time in the browser at level 8, and the level 12+ inertness on test/sortie.harness.js. The overseer approves at most one of infested-a and infested-b; this is the lower-death, single-axis one, and the only one of the pair without a conventional price.

verdicts.attack: Two respawn loops clone the follower. escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch of portalTick() (:1373-1376) iterate every hostile/patrol group in s.map.spawns with no deferred check; the follower's cast group (role hostile, count 1) is in that list, and makeActor reads g.follows, so a Hardcore escalation adds a second trailing elite and every window shut adds one more. reinforcements-a skips its arrive groups; neither hunted design mentions it. The mechanic the card describes is not what costs: the join fired in 14.1% of sorties, while the follower was in 533 fights over 450 sorties and 49 of its 52 deaths came after the squad started leaving, so the +44% is 'an elite stands on the route home' and the tooltip's 70% rule is decoration. quests.js:116 does not pass trial: true today (mt.roll(type, { level, name })) and roll() has no trial option, so the exclusion is three lines of threading, not a flag read. The follower keeps tactics.closing() (tactics.js:224) armed for the whole run (spotted and found, inside NEAR 14), which is the unexplained rise in stand plays. x1.4 is 'no formula'; under the terrain rule the inputs give about 1.19, under the arrivals rule about 1.24. Depends on u-honesty.

Frequencies 2.4/3.5/5.0/8.2% match my live3-plus-row simulation (2.4/-/4.9/8.1), which is not the all-nine pool.

Build the follower on the same cue-spawn mechanism as reinforcements (a spawn group with {on, from, stance}), not a parallel TEMPORAL/stance path. Make the tooltip state the cost that is measured (walks behind the squad and is met on the way out) or change the follower so it is not on the route home when it has not joined. Thread trial through roll() to rollTwists. Price with the agreed rule on test/sortie.harness.js. The overseer approves at most one of hunted-a and hunted-b.

verdicts.attack: The engineering is the cleanest of the pursuit four, but the price is the most overpaid of the twelve at the levels players will meet it: at levels 1-4 the measured change is 85.2% to 82.1% wins and +0.044 deaths per run for x1.5; the terrain lens's rule gives about 1.07-1.09 on those inputs and the arrivals rule about 1.1; only at levels 1-8 (+0.235 deaths) does it approach 1.3. The builder calls 1.5 'generous at low level' and keeps it. weight 5 to 12 triples the row's share and feeds the TWIST_FULL problem. Under guard orders (GUARD_LEASH 2, field.js:49) nearly every first fight has a squad member within 3 tiles of the ward, so the turn is the first fight on 98% of won sorties: the twist is 'the escort's first fight includes an elite Death Knight at level-3', which the tooltip should say in those words. Depends on u-honesty (mods), u-retreat (exitState 'order' after the turn) and the trial threading that quests.js:116 does not have.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: row :833-834; fighterFor returns null without a species :133; resolve() cancels a fight with no fighters on one side :158-161 and sets noFightUntil; frail at :414 and :599 with no reader; escalate rewrites terms :1540-1541 and save() stores mission; ward goal :758-764; combatant() ward branch :1185-1195; makeActor :1662-1688 lines are the ones to copy; ACTOR_KEYS carries role, side, grade, species, hp, maxHp, power, speed, wits, levelOffset; matches() :98 by name keeps 'ward' atoms pointing after the role changes; BESTIARY elite tier is slime_arcane, slime_dark, slime_holy, stone_golem, death_knight and only death_knight carries humanoid or undead, so the Death Knight claim holds for escort (humanoid/beast/goblin) and rescue (humanoid/goblin/undead). Logs reproduce every quoted figure: tbase4 84/85/87% 0.06/0.06/0.07, ta4 80/83/83% 0.11/0.06/0.14, tbase8 68/73/71% 0.50/0.32/0.29, ta8 62/64/65% 0.71/0.58/0.53, grade sweep t_a_vet8 0.49, t_a_lv8 1.11, t_a_e-2 1.04, t_a_e-4 0.71, t_a_e-6 0.59 against t_base_lv8 0.50. Frequencies match my live3-plus-row simulation, not the all-nine pool.
verdicts.demand: Price by level band with the agreed rule (or make the multiplier a function of level like the fee), measured on test/sortie.harness.js. Keep weight near 5-8 until TWIST_FULL is owned. State the mechanism plainly in MOD_TEXT. Sequence after u-honesty and u-retreat and thread trial through roll(). Then it can land as the Turncoat row; retrieval and siege lose the tag.

verdicts.attack: Its own sensitivity data says the described trigger is irrelevant: commit at 0.5/0.6/0.7 HP gives 0.34/0.33/0.34 deaths per sortie, committing on the walk out changes nothing, and 84 of 86 pack-fight deaths come after the squad started leaving. The twist is 'three veterans stand between the squad and the entry', which is the reinforcements-a mechanism (bodies at the entry) with a different label; the pursuit lens itself says not to approve both. It carries the same respawn-loop bug as hunted-a (escalate :1557 and the window shut :1373 clone the pack group), on escort (exit 'far', missiontypes.js escort exit) the pack behind the squad is never on the route out and still pays x1.4, and it duplicates the trail plumbing a third time. x1.4 is unpriced.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: the same field.js sites as hunted-a; tactics.js NEAR 14 at :138 and closing() :224; mapgen TEMPORAL :45. Scratchpad proj2 has stance 'vulture' with COMMIT and BTRAIL. Logs reproduce: hb 66/63/66% and 0.33/0.39/0.36 (65.0%, 0.36), joins 134+151+137 = 422 of 1800 = 23.4%; h_b1 0.33, h_b1_n2 0.30, h_b1_leave 0.32 against h_base 0.21 (the 'commit barely matters' claim holds); h_b1_lv8 1.11 against 0.68.
verdicts.demand: Drop. If the Hunted row lands it is hunted-a on the shared cue-spawn mechanism.

verdicts.attack: The informant was not modelled in the measurement (the builder says so); what was measured is a flat 30% HP and pool debuff at first contact plus a scouting loan worth about 4 win points, so the twist is a stat hit with a narrative label and no counterplay beyond composition. It is the most hard-coded of the twelve: a one-off scripted actor with its own role path through combatant() (:1185, role ally returns true today), chooseGoals, leave() (:1890-1895 would extract it), descend(), mapgen :329 and ACTOR_KEYS, plus scoutOf() inserted under found()/known(), which have 10 call sites in field.js (:448-:951), several inside per-actor filters that run every step, so an s.actors scan per call is O(actors squared) per step unless cached. The reveal coincides with the end of the free call-off, so the player never sees it while leaving is free (admitted). It exists to keep retrieval and siege on the row; losing those two types costs less than this.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: found()/known() at field.js:156/158 read s.omniscient; searchBeacon :249-281 reads s.scout/SCOUT_PERFECT as sense; restore() :2022 rebuilds omniscient from scout; sortie.js tick regen block :435-440; resolve :155; mapgen :329 places a non-captive ward around the entry; makeActor gives role ally side ours (:1670). Scratchpad proj2 has TURN=b with GIFT/RV/POISON/NOSPAWN. Logs reproduce: tbbase 61/62/62% 0.21/0.17/0.21, tb2 52/54/55% 0.28/0.36/0.21 (the +0.07/0.00/+0.19 blocks), g_native 61%/0.21, g_scout80 65%/0.17, g_scout0 55%, t2_p 0.25/0.28/0.27, t_c_10/20 0.49, t_bc 0.25/0.40/0.51. The 'extract atoms ignore it' claim holds: matches(x, 'squad') is by role, name or kind.
verdicts.demand: Drop. Turncoat-a covers the row on escort and rescue; retrieval and siege leave the only list.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

(3) test/field.harness.js's attrition model, copied with twists pinned to none, for the finish-time distribution and the walking-speed check, because its resolver has no bows, heat or mending. All prototype code is in the scratchpad copy C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\proto (combat.js and field.js patched, experiments in exp\); no project file was edited. Standard error is about 1 point on win rate and 0.01 on deaths per run at 1300 to 1950 runs per condition.

Findings that set the designs. Squads finish at 0.2 to 0.3 of the card's estimate on escort, 0.2 to 0.55 on retrieval, 0.35 to 0.55 on pursuit, 0.15 to 0.85 on expedition and 0.55 to 1.05 on recon (attrition harness, 40 runs per type), so a trigger at a fraction of the estimate would not fire on most escort and retrieval runs; both traps trigger at the way home instead. Environmental effects on a random squad are small: Storm A costs 1.2 points of wins and adds 0.03 deaths per run, about two thirds of which comes from walking x0.8 alone. A rule that depends on equipment concentrates its cost: a squad of bow users loses 13 points. The grade of the trap's enemy is a severity dial with a cliff: a veteran costs 9 points of wins, an elite costs 25 points and multiplies deaths by 6.5. Considered and rejected, with the measurement: weather gated to open ground (the share of fights opened with room for 5 or more varies from 29% on outposts to 100% on roads and from 3% on survival to 99% on siege, so the card cannot predict it); portal formation x2 (+0.004 deaths per run, no effect); accuracy -12% for everyone (-1.7 points of wins and +0.026 deaths with walking x0.8, and no decision attached); frontage -2 (raises wins by 3.2 points); noise masking, alarm reach, alarm life and hunt memory x0.6 (deaths per run 0.29 to 0.16 with tactics on and 0.25 to 0.24 with tactics off, 420 runs per cell; it helps the squad, so it cannot be priced as a complication); half recovery between fights (the same axis as No resupply). Pricing rule used for all four rewards: the contract pays what keeps expected gems per attempt equal for the reference squads, counting a death as PULL_COST (game.js:8, 100 gems): R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), with p the win rate, d deaths per run, subscript 0 without and 1 with the twist, and W0 the pay before the twist (115 gems at level 3, type reward 1). R is rounded up to the next 0.05.

proposals.title: Storm A: heat damage x0.5 and bow attacks miss 40 points more often, for both sides
proposals.problem: TWISTS.storm (missiontypes.js:821) is rolled at weight 10 and multiplies pay by 1.15, and no code reads it. The card says 'Slow ground, smothered fire, and nothing with a bowstring works'. The run plays as in clear weather, because the caller gives the combat call only frontage and breakOff (sortie.js:183, combat.js:617) and the field has no weather input. A squad of archers or fire casters is paid the same on a Storm contract as on a clear one.
evidence: missiontypes.js:821 TWISTS.storm: weight 10, reward 1.15, not dungeon and duel, no mods. The id appears in no other *.js file except spellcraft.js:56 (the tier-3 spelling of the wind noun). missiontypes.js:965 multiplies every rolled twist reward into mission.reward and sortie.js:679 pays (25 + 30 x level) x reward, so the 1.15 is paid today with no effect in the run.
sortie.js:183 resolve() builds opts = { frontage } plus breakOff and calls C.encounter; combat.js:617 encounter() reads only those two.

combat.js: every hp loss passes one of 8 E.slice call sites (158, 214, 239, 251, 256, 295, 308, 554) or the condition tick (592). The damage printed in the fight log is the slice result (combat.js:242, 302), so a multiplier applied inside damage() (145) would print a number different from the hp lost. The multiplier belongs at the slice.

combat.js:308 passes a spell's splash to damage() as 'arcane' after slicing it with the strike's own type, so a multiplier keyed on damage()'s type argument skips heat splash; keyed at the slice it does not.

combat.js:99 sets family from the equipped weapon (combat.js:60); fromMonster sets none, so a family rule never reaches a hostile. combat.js:185 rollHit() sums E.statusMissChance and E.statusIncomingMissChance, which is where a family miss term adds.

classes.js: 6 of 61 grouped classes have role 'ranged' (ranger, skulker, magic_archer, trapper, beastmaster, scout). Heat comes from the 'fire' noun (spellcraft.js:51, element heat) and from monsters with damageType heat (Fire Slime only, of 25 species in missions.js BESTIARY). The classes with mastery fire are grenadier, artillerist, kineticist, so the picker note is computed from Spellcraft.lexiconOf(c) (spellcraft.js:23), not from a class list.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (real Sortie launch, skip, settle; a scratchpad copy with TWISTS= and GEAR=1 added, GEAR giving each member the weapon of their class role, bow for ranged). 4 random-class members from a 24-member 3-5 star pool, levels 2-4, SEED 1, 14 types x 120 contracts, each contract paired with the same contract and squad in the baseline, details fix (terrain-leaving-clears-details) on in both arms. Baseline 53.5% wins, 0.454 deaths per run; Storm A 50.4%, 0.480. Paired difference -3.2 +/-0.7 points of wins, +0.026 +/-0.016 deaths per run.

Same runs by squad: 736 of 1680 squads hold a bow user: wins 51.6% to 46.7% (-4.9 +/-1.5), deaths per run 0.474 to 0.531 (+0.057 +/-0.030). The 944 without: -1.8 +/-0.7 points of wins, +0.002 +/-0.015 deaths. 1164 squads hold a heat word: -3.1 +/-1.0; the 516 without: -3.3 +/-1.1. Survivors whose lowest hp in any fight was under 40% (the u-wounds trigger): 22.0% baseline, 22.7% Storm A.

Components, same harness, fix off, 14 x 120: heat x0.5 alone R = 1.029 +/-0.017 (wins -1.1 +/-0.5, deaths -0.002); bow miss +40 with bows grounded in the second rank R = 1.081 +/-0.020 (bow squads -3.3 +/-1.5 points, +0.075 +/-0.029 deaths; the 944 squads without a bow are identical run for run); all three together R = 1.095 +/-0.026.

Ablation of the two bow rules, squad ranger, ranger, fighter, cleric, 6 types x 150 contracts: heat + miss + grounded -6.6 +/-1.4 points of wins, +0.076 deaths, R 1.285; heat + miss -7.1, +0.072, R 1.277; heat + grounded -2.3, +0.006, R 1.082; heat alone -0.4, +0.012, R 1.022. The grounded rule adds nothing measurable over the miss term and is dropped.

Walking x0.8 (in the earlier proposal), six deadline types (escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage, capture), 6 x 200 contracts: contract time and window scaled with the slower walk +2.3 +/-1.3 points of wins, -0.007 +/-0.027 deaths; window not scaled +2.0 +/-1.3, -0.003 +/-0.027. The term has no cost and no decision; it is dropped, which removes the window-clock question and four field.js consumers.

Per enemy set, combat.js called directly, 150 fights per cell, level 4, deaths per fight, clear to Storm A: melee squad against 4 goblins 0.09 to 0.09, 4 wolves 0.12 to 0.12; squad with 2 rangers and 2 melee: goblins 0.19 to 0.47, wolves 0.36 to 0.80, Ice Slimes 0.04 to 0.25, Cave Spiders 0.07 to 0.25; melee squad against 4 Fire Slimes 71% wins and 1.87 deaths to 99% and 0.42 (the enemy's heat is halved too).

proposals.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO storm-b: approve at most one. Sequenced after u-honesty: MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT and MT.factors are not in the tree (grep over *.js finds none at 06:45).

MODS ENTRY.
storm: { label: 'Storm', weight: 10, reward: 1.10, not: ['dungeon', 'duel'], trial: false, mods: { damage: { heat: 0.5 }, miss: { bow: 0.4 } } }
The tooltip text is generated from the mods by MOD_TEXT: 'Both sides: heat damage x0.5. Bow attacks miss 40 points more often.' MT.modsOf folds damage by multiplication per damage type and miss by addition per weapon family (defaults damage {}, miss {}); MT.weatherOf(mods) returns { damage, miss } or null when both are empty. Dropped from the earlier proposal: walking x0.8 with its window and Hardcore scaling, and 'a bow cannot act from the second rank' (both measured above).

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. missiontypes.js: the row; the fold; weatherOf; MOD_TEXT lines for damage and miss; rollTwists(typeId, level, max, { trial }) skips rows with trial === false when trial is true, and roll() passes the option through; quests.js:116 passes trial: true. (The same four-line filter is proposed with the Hunted and Turncoat rows and lands once.)
2. combat.js: (a) slice(ctx, target, type, raw, pen, hit) wraps E.slice, multiplies .dealt by ctx.weather.damage[type] when defined, and replaces the 8 E.slice calls; (b) the condition tick at 592 multiplies each rep.damage entry by the same table; (c) rollHit adds ctx.weather.miss[attacker.family] || 0 to the miss chance; (d) encounter() copies opts.weather into ctx.weather and logs one line per fight that has a bow user or a heat attacker: 'storm: heat damage x0.5, bow attacks miss +40 points'. damage(), options(), reaches() and tickFighter() are unchanged.
3. sortie.js resolve() (183): opts.weather = MT.weatherOf(MT.modsOf(run.mission)) when non-null. field.js is not edited. pseudoZone() (117) takes the weather and appends ':wx' to the zone id, so the cache at missions.js:109 does not reuse a plan made for clear weather.
4. missions.js missionProfile() (101): for each damage entry the sampled enemies' resistance becomes 1 - (1 - r) x multiplier, so the planner sees it. Only brilliant minds act on it.
5. UI. Card (sortie.js:992): tag title = desc; the itemised factor 'Storm x1.10' from MT.factors; 'with Storm: N sent, W won, D lost' from gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, won, dead }, incremented in settle() beside u-ledger's gs.field.types. Party box (renderBoard, beside the scouting lines at sortie.js:1274 and 1299): one line per picked member that the mods change, from MT.weatherNotes(c, weather): a bow in c.equipment.weapon gives 'Storm: bow attacks miss 40 points more often'; a heat word in Spellcraft.lexiconOf(c) gives 'Storm: heat damage x0.5'. Brief rows (bestiary.js:232) whose damageType is heat (known at tier 2) get 'Storm: its heat damage x0.5'. renderSide tally (sortie.js:1641) appends 'storm: heat x0.5, bows miss +40'. fieldview.js drawMap (83) tints the map blue and draws rain streaks while a weather is active.
6. Tests: see TESTS. test/sortie.harness.js gains TWISTS= (twist ids or 'none', pinned on every rolled contract) and GEAR=1 (about 10 lines, added by terrain-leaving-clears-details if that lands first).

CARD AND MAP. Card: 'Storm' tag with the generated tooltip, 'Storm x1.10' in the itemised pay, the per-twist record. Map: blue tint and rain, the tally text, the existing start line 'Complications: Storm' (field.js:2102), and the per-fight line.

DECISION. Before launch: which bow users and heat casters go. The picker names each affected member; a Fire Slime row on the brief shows the one case where the storm helps. During the run: no control.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat order: no change (no walking term). Wounds (u-wounds, lowest hp under 40%): 22.0% of survivors clear, 22.7% in the storm. Permadeath: +0.026 +/-0.016 deaths per run overall, +0.057 +/-0.030 on squads with a bow user, +0.002 on the rest.

REWARD x1.10. R = (p0 x W0 + L0 - L1 + (d1 - d0) x C) / (p1 x W0): the multiplier at which expected gems per contract equal the baseline's, with wins paid at m x W0, loot L (kill drops are paid on losses too) and C = 100 gems per death, the Summon cost (game.js:8), a lower bound on what a character is worth. Inputs, n = 1680 pairs: p0 0.535, p1 0.504, W0 229.4 gems (mean contract fee per win), L0 59.9, L1 57.0, d0 0.454, d1 0.480. R = 1.110 +/-0.026 (bootstrap over pairs), rounded to the nearest 0.05. A player can check the inputs on screen: the base pay line '25 + 30 x level' on the honesty card, the 100-gem Summon button, and the per-twist record on the tag. test/contracts.js recomputes R from fixed-seed sorties (400 per arm) and fails when the row is more than 0.10 below the result. The 1.05 in the earlier proposal came from the attrition runner, which has no gear, loot or tactics layer; it is replaced.

FREQUENCY. Weight 10, not dungeon and duel, unchanged. Under the honesty draw rule (odds x weight / 66; odds 0.2 at level 1, 0.41 at 10, 0.6 at 18): 3.0%, 6.2% and 9.1% of first draws.

TESTS. test/combat.weather.js: with ctx.weather.damage.heat = 0.5, a heat swing on a 0-resistance target loses half the hp and the logged number equals the hp lost; a heat condition tick halves; heat splash is halved by its strike type; with miss.bow = 0.4 a bow fighter's miss share over 2000 rolls rises by 0.40 +/-0.03 and a monster's does not; missionProfile with the weather raises sampled heat resistance to 1 - (1 - r) x 0.5. test/contracts.js: modsOf fold for 'storm' and for 'storm' with 'dry'; rollTwists with { trial: true } never returns storm. Reproduce the price: TWISTS=none vs TWISTS=storm, GEAR=1 LEVEL=2-4 RUNS=120 SEED=1 OUT=a.json / b.json node test/sortie.harness.js run, then diff a.json b.json.
proposals.playerEffect: Roster composition becomes a pre-launch choice with a number. Squads with a bow user (44% of random squads in the sample) lose 4.9 points of wins and 0.057 deaths per run; the rest lose 1.8 points and no deaths. The picker names the affected members before Set out, so a player with a deep roster swaps them and collects the x1.10, and a player whose roster is rangers declines or rerolls the board. Fire Slime contracts get easier for every squad (melee squad 71% to 99% wins), and the brief marks the row when the species is known.
proposals.secondOrder: Brilliant minds drop heat spells in a storm (heat 50% to 1% of prepared spells in the 6-word test) and dim to sharp minds do not, so acumen pays with no change in ai.js. ctx.weather is a general channel: a later Fog twist needs a miss entry per family or a sight mod. Solo trials never draw it (trial: false). A run saved before the build keeps its mission.twists, so it gets the weather from the reload on. The details fix changes the baseline (R 1.095 without it, 1.110 with it).
proposals.risks: The loss outside bow squads (-1.8 +/-0.7 points of wins) is not assigned to a rule: heat alone explains -1.1 +/-0.5. 44% of squads hold a bow user only because GEAR=1 equips by class role; the real share depends on the roster. Measured on 3-5 star squads with a role weapon and no armour, potions or meals, at levels 2-4 (baseline 53.5% wins), not on a real save; levels above 6 are not measured. A spell with several strikes is scaled per strike type, so a fire-and-ice spell loses half of its heat strike only. The picker note for heat is a hint: spells are chosen at launch by the planner. Overlaps wave 2 on combat.js, sortie.js, missions.js and missiontypes.js, so line numbers move.
proposals.response: Design (kill). 'Three special cases in combat.js': reduced to one table lookup at the slice (damage by type) and one lookup in rollHit (miss by family); the data is the row, no code branches on 'storm', and the grounded-bow rule was removed by ablation. 'Two thirds of the cost is walking': measured the other way, walking x0.8 costs nothing (+2.0 to +2.3 points on the deadline types, with or without window scaling), so it is dropped. 'Unpriced window tax (shutsAt not scaled)': no tax appears (evidence 11), and the term is gone. 'x1.05 is 6 gems and invisible': the price is now 1.10, 23 gems at the harness's mean win fee of 229, derived on the harness the game uses. 'storm-b is the axes shape': B measures R 1.018 and its cost depends on the cast, which the player can read only for species the town has studied (see storm-b); A's cost is readable from the squad on screen. Engineering (rework). Sequencing after u-honesty: accepted. Window clock: removed with the walking term, measured. Heat splash: fixed by moving the multiplier to the slice (evidence 3, 4). Duplicates wet: A and B are alternatives and A makes no elements.js change. Re-measure on sortie.harness: done (evidence 7-11). Fire-word class list: corrected (evidence 6). One price rule: R above with every input stated. 'Two thirds of squads see nothing': 56% of squads lose 1.8 points and no deaths, so the premium is small for them by construction.

proposals.title: Storm B: both sides start each fight Wet x3
proposals.problem: Same dead row as storm-a (missiontypes.js:821). Elements already contains the condition the card describes (elements.js:170 'wet': heat resistance up, lightning, cold and poison resistance down, a heat hit removes a stack), and the contract layer has no way to put a condition on a whole map, so weather would otherwise be a second set of constants beside Elements'.
evidence: missiontypes.js:821 TWISTS.storm has no consumer (see storm-a).

proposals.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO storm-a: approve at most one. Sequenced after u-honesty.

MODS ENTRY.
storm: { label: 'Storm', weight: 10, reward: 1.00, not: ['dungeon', 'duel'], trial: false, mods: { status: [{ id: 'wet', stacks: 3 }] } }
MT.modsOf folds status by union, keeping the larger stack count per id (default []); MT.weatherOf(mods) returns { status } or null. The tooltip is generated from the status definition so editing elements.js edits the card: sortie.js builds it with E.STATUSES (missiontypes.js has no dependency on elements.js): 'Both sides start each fight Wet x3: heat resistance +24 points; lightning and cold resistance -18 points; poison -12 points. A heat hit removes one stack. Five stacks make Soaked (heat resistance 80%; lightning, cold and poison -50%).' Dropped from the earlier proposal: missChanceBy on the shared wet definition (no elements.js edit now), walking x0.8, the 'wet bowstring' bow rule.

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. missiontypes.js: the row, the status fold, weatherOf, rollTwists(..., { trial }) skipping rows with trial === false (shared with storm-a), quests.js:116 passing trial: true.
2. combat.js: soak(f, weather) is called for every fighter on both sides after the reset loop (637) and before tick 1; it applies E.applyStatus(f, { id: 'wet', intensity: 1, duration: 'permanent' }, 'storm', false) until findStatus(f, 'wet').stacks equals the weather's count, skips a fighter that holds 'soaked', and bounds the loop at 8. Counting stacks makes a second encounter on the same fighters a no-op. encounter() logs 'storm: everyone starts Wet x3'. soak is exported for missions.js.
3. sortie.js resolve() (183): opts.weather = MT.weatherOf(MT.modsOf(run.mission)); pseudoZone() (117) carries the weather and appends ':wx' to the zone id. field.js and elements.js are not edited.
4. missions.js missionProfile() (101): Combat.soak on each sampled enemy before profileOf.
5. UI. Card tag title = desc; 'Storm x1.00' in the itemised pay; the per-twist record. Party box (beside sortie.js:1274, 1299): per picked member, from the lexicon elements: heat words 'Storm: heat spells land at x0.76 against Wet targets'; spark or ice words 'x1.18'; seed or venom words 'x1.12'. Brief rows (bestiary.js:232) with a known damageType: cold or lightning 'Storm: squad takes +18%', poison '+12%', heat 'Storm: squad takes x0.76'; a row whose inflicts include wet 'Storm: its hits add Wet; five stacks is Soaked'; a row below tier 2 'Storm: effect on this species unknown'. renderSide tally appends 'storm: Wet x3'; fieldview.js drawMap draws the same tint and rain as storm-a.
6. Tests: see TESTS.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag with the generated tooltip and the tag 'x1.00' (the row pays no premium). Map: tint, rain, tally, start line, per-fight line.

DECISION. Before launch the player reads the brief: the same Storm costs a melee squad about 4x the deaths against Ice Slimes and 3.7x against Cave Spiders and nothing against goblins, wolves or Water Slimes. The player can skip those contracts, or send casters of other elements. During the run: heat hits dry the target (each removes a stack), so a fire caster loses 24% on its first hit and recovers; a water word or a Water Slime adds stacks and two applications give Soaked.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat: no change. Wounds: survivors under 40% hp at their lowest 22.0% clear, 21.8% Wet x3. Permadeath: -0.023 +/-0.014 deaths per run overall; the increase is on cold, lightning and poison casts (melee squad deaths per fight x2 to x4) and is paid back by Fire Slime and Water Slime casts.

REWARD x1.00. R = 1.018 +/-0.019 with the formula and inputs of storm-a (p0 0.535, p1 0.524, W0 229.4, L0 59.9, L1 58.1, d0 0.454, d1 0.431), rounded to the nearest 0.05. The row therefore pays nothing extra: its average cost is zero, because relief on heat casts offsets the increase on cold, lightning and poison casts. To make it pay, change one data field: stacks 4 gives R 1.02, Soaked at start (status { id: 'soaked', stacks: 1 }) gives R 1.08 and a reward of 1.10.

FREQUENCY. Weight 10, not dungeon and duel; 3.0%, 6.2%, 9.1% of first draws at levels 1, 10, 18.

TESTS. test/combat.weather.js: after encounter setup every fighter on both sides holds exactly 3 wet stacks and a second encounter on the same fighters leaves 3; a heat hit lowers stacks to 2 and the next encounter restores 3; a fighter holding soaked keeps it; resistances at 3 stacks are 0.24, -0.18, -0.18, -0.12; statusMissChance is 0; missionProfile with the weather raises sampled heat resistance by 0.24. test/contracts.js: status fold keeps the larger stack count.
proposals.playerEffect: The decision depends on the contract's cast rather than on the squad: a Storm contract against Ice Slimes, Thunder Slimes or Cave Spiders costs a melee squad several times the deaths of the same contract against goblins, wolves or Water Slimes, and the card states the numbers. Because the row pays x1.00, the player has no reason to take it over the same contract without the twist; the twist works as a reason to read the brief, not as a trade.
proposals.secondOrder: Weather becomes a condition like any other: the water word, Water Slime hits and the storm feed one status, and two extra applications push a target to Soaked. The planner reads the changed resistances through bearerResistance: brilliant minds move from heat to cold spells (heat 50% to 25%), lower tiers do not. Lightning and frost casters gain +18% against Wet targets, which the 1680-contract sample does not resolve. A later Fog or Snow twist is one more status id in a mods row.
proposals.risks: Information: the per-cast cost is readable only for species the town has studied to tier 2 and only when the paper names the species; a Storm B contract against species the player has never killed carries a cost the card cannot show. This is the main reason storm-a is recommended over storm-b. Soaked is a cliff: a water word or two Water Slime hits on top of 3 stacks gives melee squads against Cave Spiders 0.41 deaths per fight against 0.03 clear. The population effect is zero (R 1.018 +/-0.019), so approving this row adds code and tags without a pay incentive. Wet persists across fights on cached fighters (no combatEnd removal); the top-up is idempotent but a status the player cannot remove is new. Overlaps wave 2 on combat.js and sortie.js.
proposals.response: Design (rework). Drop missChanceBy from the shared wet definition: done, elements.js is not edited and the bow rule is gone. Drop walking x0.8 or scale the window: dropped; measured +2.0 to +2.3 points on the deadline types with or without scaling (storm-a evidence 11); escort and rescue are in that sample and show no change. Put the Soaked threshold on the card: done in the generated tooltip. Tag Water Slime rows on the brief: done, gated on knowledge tier 2. Re-derive the price with the same formula and state it as data: R 1.018 +/-0.019, reward 1.00, with the dial values listed. trial: false: done. Engineering (kill). 'Same population effect as A for a larger surface': the population effect is smaller than A's (R 1.018 against 1.110), and the surface is smaller than the earlier proposal's (no elements.js change, no facet schema field, no field.js change); it remains larger than A's in combat.js (one top-up function) and in UI tags. 'Edits the shared wet definition': no longer. 'Status persistence on cached fighters': handled by counting stacks and checked in Node (idempotent top-up, heat hit, Soaked). 'Species coupling makes the flat price wrong': accepted and measured; the price is 1.00 because the average is zero, and the brief tags are the mitigation only where the species is known, which I list as the main risk. I keep the row as an alternative because it is the only design that reuses an existing axis, and recommend storm-a.
