proposals.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO trap-b (dropped; this is the only trap design). Sequenced after u-honesty (modsOf, MOD_TEXT) and terrain-leaving-clears-details; u-retreat is already in the tree.

MODS ENTRY.
trap: { label: 'A trap', weight: 6, reward: 1.10, only: ['recon', 'escort', 'expedition', 'retrieval', 'pursuit'], trial: false, mods: { ambush: { count: 3, grade: 'veteran', ring: 0.65 } } }
modsOf takes the first ambush found (no stacking). Generated tooltip: 'When the written work is done and the squad reaches the way home: 3 veteran hostiles appear in sight, 65% of sight range to one tile inside it (6 to 8 tiles; 3 to 4 at night), and Kill the 3 ambushers is added to the terms. Nothing else on the map changes.' grade is data: 'veteran', another grade id, or 'cast' (the highest grade among the written cast's hostile, patrol and mark groups).

TRIGGER (one predicate for gate, window and standfast exits): mods.ambush && !s.trapped && !s.withdrew && !s.escalated && !s.skirmishes.length && workDone(s) && squadOn(s).some(a => inPortal(s, a)), evaluated each step between overtime(s) and leave(s). A squad that has broken off is not ambushed; a Hardcore contract that has escalated is not.

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. missiontypes.js: the row; the modsOf default (ambush null); ATOM_TEXT.eliminate (1005) prints 'Kill the N whos' when a.count > 1; rollTwists trial filter (shared with storm-a); MOD_TEXT.ambush.
2. field.js: start() sets s.mods and s.trapped = null; restore() derives mods from the saved mission and reads o.trapped; save() writes trapped. trapTick(s) is called in step() between overtime(s) and leave(s). springTrap(s): ringTile(s, c, lo, hi) picks a passable tile reachable from the entry (map.dist >= 0) at Chebyshev distance lo..hi from squadPoint(s) with a line of sight to it (canSee), where hi = sight - 1 (hostiles notice at dist2 < sight) and lo = max(2, round(ring x sight)); if none, lo falls to 2; if still none the step is retried and after 30 tries s.trapped = { at, none: true } and nothing happens. For each of count ambushers: makeActor({ role: 'hostile', grade, name: 'ambusher', side: 'theirs' }, tile, s) with found = true, lastSeen = clock, lastAt = squad point. m.win gets { ...MT.OBJ.eliminate('ambusher'), count, amended: true } inserted before the walk-home atom; s.doneAt = null, s.phase = 'in', s.pushed = false; a gate portal returns to closed with progress 0; s.trapped = { at, id, grade, n, species, dist }. Log: 'trap: <species> (veteran) is <d> tiles from the squad; terms now: <terms>' (N lines are not repeated).
3. u-retreat: no edit. contacted() turns true the step after the spring (the ambushers spot the squad, field.js:878), so exitState reads 'order'; a squad that has not been spotted before could still call it off for that one step.
4. sortie.js: renderSide (1625) prefixes an atom with amended: true with a warning mark; the card tooltip and the per-twist record as in storm-a. fieldview.js drawActors (213): a red ring on live hostiles named 'ambusher'.
5. Tests: see TESTS.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag 'A trap' with the generated tooltip, 'A trap x1.10' in the itemised pay; the brief does not list the ambushers (they are not in m.cast, so describe().hostiles and Bestiary.brief are unchanged). Map: at the spring ringed tokens appear in sight, the side panel adds the new term with a warning mark, the log gives species, grade, count and distance, and the button reads 'Order a retreat'.

DECISION. Before launch: arrive at the way home with hp and pools left, so healers, a fifth member, or skipping the contract. During the run: at the spring, fight on or order a retreat. Measured on sprung runs: fighting on wins 80.7% with 0.086 deaths; ordering the retreat at once wins 31.9% with 0.046 deaths. At the harness's win fee of 176 gems and 100 gems per death, fighting on is worth about 86 gems more in pay and costs about 4 gems more in deaths, so the retreat is the right call only for a squad that is already hurt, which the player reads from the squad list. broken() still withdraws an exhausted squad on its own.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat: a retreat ordered at the spring is a loss and the ambushers hunt the squad on the walk (0.046 deaths per sprung run). Wounds: survivors under 40% hp at their lowest 16.5% clear, 23.1% trap (u-wounds injury trigger). Permadeath: +0.040 +/-0.006 deaths per run, 0.086 per sprung run, 0.20 on recon.

REWARD x1.10. R = 1.098 +/-0.024 with the formula of storm-a. Inputs, n = 1200 pairs: p0 0.678, p1 0.555, W0 176 gems, L0 48.7, L1 64.9 (the ambushers' drops are paid), d0 0.207, d1 0.247. Rounded to the nearest 0.05. The current 1.5 is 0.4 above it. Check on screen: base pay line, the 100-gem Summon button, the per-twist record 'with A trap: N sent, W won, D lost'; test/contracts.js recomputes R from 400 fixed-seed sorties per arm and fails when the row is more than 0.10 below. The price is measured at levels 2-4 only (see risks).

FREQUENCY. Weight 6, only the five types: 1.8%, 3.7%, 5.5% of first draws for those types at levels 1, 10, 18 under the honesty draw rule, about 1.2% of all contracts at level 10; the spring fires in 64% of those.

TESTS. test/trap.js: Field.play with the twist forced, 5 types x 40 seeds: s.trapped set in at least 55% of runs; ambushers have role 'hostile', name 'ambusher', found true, distance 2 to sight - 1 and a line of sight at spawn; m.win holds one amended eliminate before the walk-home atom; Field.save at the spring, JSON round trip, Field.restore finishes with the amended terms and no second spring; a withdrawn squad never springs; no run ends with an open detail after phase 'leaving'. Reproduce the price: TWISTS=none vs TWISTS=trap, TYPES=recon,escort,expedition,retrieval,pursuit GEAR=1 LEVEL=2-4 RUNS=240 SEED=1 node test/sortie.harness.js run, then diff.
proposals.playerEffect: The contract has a second act that the written terms did not describe, and it arrives when the squad has finished and used its hp. The player decides how much to hold back: a healer, a fifth member, or another contract. The retreat button has a concrete moment to be used, with the cost of using it on the screen (31.9% wins and 0.046 deaths against 80.7% and 0.086). The cost varies by type: recon (69% among sprung runs, 0.20 deaths) is hit hardest, escort (80%) and the others lose 14 to 17 points.
proposals.secondOrder: Wounds deepen after a trap (16.5% to 23.1% of survivors under 40% hp), which feeds u-wounds recovery time and the debrief's ready-in figure. Tactics responds with its own stand or pounce on the ambushers and now ends it (terrain-leaving-clears-details). The ambushers' species is recorded by Bestiary.record, so the town learns it. Positive levelOffset is not used (the engine's SWARMED assumes non-positive). If Reinforcements or Hunted are approved they can share ringTile.
proposals.risks: The price is measured at levels 2-4 with 3-5 star squads. The paper's top grade steps from veteran to elite around level 8, a single cast-top ambusher is priced at about 1.9 at levels 2-4, and at level 7 the same squads (21.5% baseline wins) cannot be priced; so grade is fixed at veteran, which is the safe error: at levels where veterans are the rank and file the trap costs less than 1.10 and the player is overpaid. A level-aware row (grade 'cast', count by band) needs a matched-squad harness at levels 8 and up. 36% of contracts never reach the way home with the work done and pay no premium. Ambushers appear in sight, so a squad that has already run its tactics plan may stand against 3 hostiles in a doorway; that is the intended fight. A run saved before the build with the trap id and the work done will spring on reload. Wave 1 and 2 are editing field.js and sortie.js; line numbers move.
proposals.response: Design (rework). Explain the escort loss with a log sample: in the combat-backed harness escort goes 100% to 96% with one veteran and 100% to 80% among sprung runs with three; the 21-point loss in the first proposal came from the attrition runner and is not reproduced, and 'the ward stands in the fight' is not the cause (the ward has no fighter and is never targeted: sortie.js:138, 166). The stalls in the first prototype had two causes found in logs: an ambusher outside sight or not found under 'ambush' pressure (17 ABANDON runs; recon seed 1353802, retrieval seed 6404551) and a Tactics stand that the phase change never ended (26 runs; expedition seed 6122040, pursuit seed 5268370). Both are fixed (placement in sight with found = true; the details fix), and role 'hostile' avoids the mark's flee behaviour under quarry pressure. Grade from the cast: tested and declined as the default (evidence 12): a single cast-top ambusher prices at 0.96 for veterans and about 1.9 for the grade above, and at level 7 it cannot be priced with these squads, so grade is data, fixed at veteran, with 'cast' available; count 3 is the dial that gives 1.10. trial: false: accepted. Log line states the mechanic: accepted (species, grade, count, distance, terms). Keep weight 6: kept. 'One rational answer in the run': with three ambushers the retreat saves 0.04 deaths per sprung run and gives up 49 points of wins, so the answer depends on the squad's state, which is the point. 'Generic pre-launch lever': the picker has no per-contract hint, and I do not add one. Engineering (rework). ABANDON re-arm: the spring is at most 1.39 x the estimate and ABANDON is 2.5 x, and no sprung run ended 'going nowhere' after the placement fix, so no offset is added; doneAt restarts at the spring. Escort and ward delivery: the predicate counts squad members only and escort stays in the list on the measured 80%. Sequencing after u-honesty and u-retreat: accepted (u-retreat is in the tree). Price reproduced on test/sortie.harness.js: done (evidence 10, 11).

proposals.title: A trap B: when the written work is done and the squad reaches the way home, the squad is moved to new ground and the terms are replaced
proposals.problem: Same dead row as trap-a (missiontypes.js:835), read as a change of job instead of an added term. Both antagonists asked for it to be dropped.
evidence: field.js:1759-1812 descend() (as of the first proposal) rebuilds the map and carries the squad, but refuses while a skirmish is open; a pit would copy about 18 mission fields and reset about 20 run fields by hand, while save() (field.js:2004) enumerates run state explicitly, so a forgotten field is saved into the new map.
Cargo types were excluded in the prototype (ward and relic did not survive the move: 0% and 2% wins), leaving recon, expedition and pursuit, about 0.7% of contracts.
Loadouts are planned once against the written cast (missions.js:109, sortie.js:117); the card, the per-type record and ESCALATION key on the written type while the run is another type.

Effect measured in the first proposal (-7.6 points of wins, +0.005 deaths, 89% of sprung runs won) is the same size as trap-a's added term, which measures -12.3 points and +0.040 deaths per run on the combat-backed harness for 3 veteran ambushers.
proposals.change: Dropped. trap-a already changes the terms partway in and states the new terms on the card and in the log. A type change would need the cargo move solved (ward, relic), a transplant function derived from save()'s key list, and a reason for a player to prepare differently than for trap-a; none of the three exists.
proposals.playerEffect: None: not built. The player-facing decisions the design offered (how much to hold back, whether to retreat at the spring) are the same as trap-a's.
proposals.secondOrder: None: not built. If a mid-run type change is wanted later it should be written as one Field.transplant(s, innerMission) shared with descend(), with its reset list derived from save().
proposals.risks: Largest and most fragile of the original twelve designs for an effect the player cannot tell from trap-a's.
proposals.response: Design (kill) and engineering (kill): accepted. The L-size state transplant has the same measured effect as the added term, covers 3 of 16 types, leaves loadouts planned for the wrong cast, and its log line ('The floor gives way') is a metaphor where the register rule asks for the mechanic and the number. No demand saves it; trap-a covers the card.

proposals.title: Dissolve open tactical details when the squad starts leaving
proposals.problem: A squad that has met the terms, or has withdrawn (its own decision or the retreat order), can stay on the tile of a tactical detail (stand, hold, pounce, strike) and never walk out. On the combat-backed harness 97 of 1680 contracts (5.8%) ended that way: 62 as 'the work was done and they never got home' and 35 as 'they ran from a fight they were losing, and could not get clear'. Every one of the 97 finished with an open detail. Capture loses 21 of 120, extermination 20, sabotage 14, recon 12, rescue 10. The player sees a finished contract paid nothing, or a retreat order that does not leave; sortie.js exitState reports 'stuck' after STRAGGLE for the second case.
evidence: field.js:730 chooseGoals reads detailFor() (613) before taskGoal(), so a squad member in a detail walks to detailGoal() whatever the phase is; a stand's goal is the fixed tile det.point.

tactics.js:259 propose() returns null when s.phase === 'leaving'. The rules that end a detail (tactics.js:398-399: a stand ends when nobody is busy and nothing is closing, or after STAND_FOR = 90 s) are inside propose(), so a detail open at the phase change is never ended. field.js:673 replan() applies only what propose returns.
field.js:384 (withdraw) and field.js:1899-1900 (leave) are the only two writers of phase 'leaving'; neither touches s.details. dissolve (field.js:615) is called only from replan and grieved.

field.js:1665 and 1634: verdict() fails the run after max(STRAGGLE, duration) since doneAt, or STRAGGLE since the withdrawal, which is where pinned squads end. sortie.js:538 exitState has a 'stuck' state for a withdrawal older than STRAGGLE.

Debug probe, trap prototype, pursuit seed 5268370: stand raised at 257, ambushers dead at 281, phase 'leaving' at 281, four squad actors on (1,3) with goal 'point' until the end at 1182 while the portal is at (1,15) and shuts and reopens twice. Same shape in expedition seed 6122040.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (scratchpad copy with TWISTS=none and GEAR=1; 4 random-class members from a 24-member 3-5 star pool, levels 2-4, SEED 1, 14 types x 120 contracts, paired). Before: 52.5% ... see rows: baseline 50.7% wins, 0.477 deaths per run, mean clock 375 in-game s, 97 pinned runs, 101 runs ended with an open detail. After the two-line change: 53.5% wins, 0.454 deaths per run, clock 327, 3 'never got home' (all extermination) and 0 'could not get clear', 1 run ended with an open detail. Paired difference +2.8 +/-0.4 points of wins, -0.023 +/-0.008 deaths per run. By type, capture 78% to 94%, extermination 73% to 86%, assassination 42% to 48%.
R computed with the storm-a formula for the change itself: 0.942 +/-0.011, i.e. the fix is worth 5.8% of pay per contract at the baseline.
node test/field.harness.js 20 off on with the two lines applied runs to the end for every type (plain attrition resolver).
proposals.change:
field.js, two lines.
1. withdraw() (382): after s.phase = 'leaving', call dissolve(s, () => true, null).
2. leave() (1899): inside if (s.phase !== 'leaving') { s.phase = 'leaving'; ... }, call dissolve(s, () => true, null).
No new state. dissolve (615) removes the details and clears a.sneak on their members; with null it logs nothing. Tactics.propose already returns null in this phase, so no detail is created afterwards; the squad then follows taskGoal(), which returns the exit goal once s.withdrew is set or the terms are met.

test/sortie.harness.js gains TWISTS= (twist ids or 'none' pinned on every rolled contract), GEAR=1 (weapon by Classes.roleOf), ONLY=<seeds> and LOGTAIL=<n> (debugging), and the record fields details (open details at the end), trapped, bows, heat (about 25 lines). The numbers of storm-a, storm-b and trap-a are reproduced with these options.

TESTS. test/leaving.js: Field.play with a Tactics stub that raises a stand, 40 seeds x 6 types: after phase becomes 'leaving' s.details is empty and the run reaches a result within STRAGGLE of the last objective; a withdrawal ordered during a stand (Field.retreat) leaves within the walk time; the 12 harness seeds that ended 'never got home' in the baseline (capture and extermination) now end in a win or an ordinary loss.
proposals.playerEffect: A contract whose work is done gets paid instead of being lost to a squad that stands still. A retreat order, and the squad's own withdrawal, actually leave. Over 1680 contracts 47 more are won and 0.023 fewer characters die per contract; capture, which is lost 19% of the time to this cause in the baseline, becomes 94% won.
proposals.secondOrder: u-retreat's order and the 'stuck' state depend on this: without it an ordered retreat issued during a stand can pin the squad. trap-a's spring raises a stand against the ambushers (1.8% of sprung runs ended pinned before the fix). Prices measured on the old baseline shift slightly: storm-a R is 1.095 without the fix and 1.110 with it. The pay of the board rises about 5.8% per contract for the same squads, which raises gems per run for every contract type.
proposals.risks: Dissolving at 'leaving' ends a stand that was holding a corridor while the squad walks out; measured deaths fall rather than rise (-0.023 per contract), but the walk is no longer escorted by a tactical plan. The remaining 3 'never got home' runs (extermination) have a different cause that was not investigated. The harness squads are gearless apart from a role weapon, so the share (5.8%) is a harness figure; the mechanism (detail precedence plus propose returning null) is in the code. field.js and tactics.js are being edited in wave 2; the two call sites are named by function, not by line.
proposals.response: New proposal, taken from the engineering antagonist's missed list ('Phase leaving is set both by withdraw() and by leave()'). It belongs to the terrain lens because trap-a's spring resets the phase and then relies on the squad walking out after the kill, and because the retreat order uses the same withdraw() path. The antagonists' note that deaths after 'leaving' mix two causes is addressed by fixing both writers.

revised.stateOfGame:
The six complications are table rows only. TWISTS (missiontypes.js:818) has nine entries; the only consumers are field.js:2055 (Night, sight 9 becomes 5), sortie.js:435 (No resupply) and field.js:1535 (Hardcore). Reinforcements (row :823, weight 12, x1.3, not duel) and Infested (row :827, weight 10, x1.35) are rolled on 3.4% / 3.4% of level-1 contracts, 7.2% / 7.5% at level 10 and 12.2% / 12.7% at level 20 and pay without doing anything. Everything needed to make them real already exists in separate pieces. roll() builds the cast, applies the horde rule swarm() (missiontypes.js:310) and only then reads the terms (:945-952). mapgen.build() places each cast group at its own points and marks groups with a per or temporal cue as deferred (mapgen.js:340); arrivals() (field.js:1702) spawns deferred groups on the clock. escalate() and the window-shut branch of portalTick() already re-spawn 50% and 30% of the written groups through spawnGroup (field.js:1557, 1373). nameCast() fixes one species per group when the contract is written (sortie.js:61), Bestiary.brief() prints one row per species and level (bestiary.js:201-212), fighterFor() fields a body at mission level + GRADE_BUMP + levelOffset (sortie.js:136), look() marks a hostile spotted and raises the alarm when it sees a squad member (field.js:877), and Missions.prepare plans loadouts only against the species of groups that are on the map at launch (sortie.js:257, field.js:2067 skips deferred groups).

Measurements. test/field.harness.js uses the plain attrition resolver, so I built a combat.js-backed runner that mirrors sortie.js resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast, over a private patched copy of the project. Everything is in C:/Users/mersi/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha/bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109/scratchpad/arrivals (called ARR below): run.js, par.js, variants2.js, tiers.js, the patched copy proj2/ (field.js, missiontypes.js, mapgen.js), and result files under ARR/results/. Squad: 4 random 3-5 star characters from the real generators, no gear or potions, contract level 1-4, tactics on, same seeds in every arm, 15 types (duel not run). Base: 69.5% wins, 0.258 deaths per run, 14.7% of runs with a death, 6.21 fights per run (1500 runs); with the wave-2 wound rule (WOUND_FROM 0.4) 14.4% of survivors and 38% of sorties are injured, which matches loop-wounds' own calibration. The live twists on the same harness: Night 71.3% / 0.286 (900 runs, not distinguishable from base), No resupply 65.1% / 0.321. Four findings decided the designs. (1) First contact (first sighting or first fight) happens in 97% of runs, median 40-190 s by type, but the written estimate is 2-8x the real run (median clock / duration 0.12-0.52), so a trigger as a fraction of duration fires after the contract is over, and a kill-share trigger (half the garrison dead) is reached in 70% of runs (28% assassination, 38% escort). (2) One grade up is not a uniform step in combat.js: hp x damage x speed per body is x3.8 basic to veteran, x4.8 veteran to elite, x1.5 elite to ancient (GRADE_BUMP is +3 levels) and x8.9 ancient to legendary at level 6 (ARR/tiers.js), so promoting a third of every group by grade adds 0.35 deaths per run (win 70.2 to 53.3%), of which basic groups alone add 0.01 and veteran groups alone 0.30. (3) A level offset is a uniform step that fighterFor, castLevel, noteSighting and the brief rows already honour. (4) The horde rule already turns a grade gap into bodies: x2.2 per grade, 4.5 levels lower, in packs.

Shared conventions in the four proposals. Consumers never name a twist: they read folded mods through MT.modsOf (u-honesty), and the three new keys are arrivals (list, folds by concatenation: entries {on, delay, from, share}), promote (folds to the largest share: {share, perLevel}) and swell (integer, folds by sum, capped at 2). Each key needs one MOD_TEXT line and one consumer, which is the unit's own test. All numbers are produced by one price rule so the four multipliers can be compared: the multiplier m at which expected gem income per attempt, fee x m x P(win) + gem drops of the kills made (missions.js:242, paid at sortie.js:555), equals the base contract's plus R gems for every extra death, with R = 200 = 2 x PULL_COST (game.js:8, the Summon button). m = (W0 F0 + L0 + R dd - L1) / (W1 F1) with W the win rate, F the fee per won contract ((25 + 30 x level) x type reward, sortie.js:535), L the drops per run, dd the extra deaths per run. The same rule applied to the live No resupply twist (840 paired runs, 14 types: 69.2% to 63.9% wins, 0.280 to 0.337 deaths) returns x1.28 against its table value x1.25; the standard error of that death difference is 0.039, so R is known to roughly a factor of two. A constant multiplier cannot track level (the fee grows 30 gems per level, R does not), so these are values for the levels 1-4 the harness runs. With the proposed constants the mean contract pay multiplier at level 10 is 1.124 (A + Infested-a) or 1.095 (B + Infested-b), against 1.152 for today's nine rows and 1.064 for the three live ones (u-honesty), so the honesty unit's pay cut is largely undone by the real rows. Frequencies in the proposals are computed with all nine rows in the pool (the state once the six are real) on the board's current rule; with only five rows live, u-honesty's rule (draw probability = odds x weight / 66) makes them about 15% higher (reinforcements-a at level 10: 8.0% against 6.8%).

proposals.title: Arrival at the entry: 35% of each hostile and patrol group arrives 45 s after first contact and moves toward the squad; a retreat order or break-off cancels it
proposals.problem: The board offers Reinforcements ("A second garrison arrives partway through, from the wrong direction") at x1.3 and nothing arrives: the id appears only in its table row (missiontypes.js:823). A player cannot read when "partway" is, where "the wrong direction" is, how many come, or what to do about it. The clock has to be an event the player can already see. First contact (a fight has opened or a hostile has a line to a squad member, Field.contacted, field.js:1477) happens in 100% of the harness contracts at a median of 75 in-game s (15 real s; p10 30, p90 151), and it is the event that ends the free "Call it off" window, so a countdown that starts there can be read on the paper, in the side panel and on the map. A fraction of mission.duration is not such a clock: the duration is an estimate (median 840 in-game s at levels 1-4 on these types) and the median contract ends at 312 s (p10 144, p90 822), so a release at half of it (420 s) would come after the end of more than half of the contracts.
evidence: missiontypes.js:823-824 TWISTS.reinforcements (weight 12, reward 1.3, not duel); grep -w finds the id only in this row. Consumers that exist for other twists: field.js:2082 (night), sortie.js:503 (dry), field.js:1560 (hardcore).

field.js:1477 contacted(s) = counters.fights > 0 or any actor spotted (landed with loop-retreat; field.js:1222 counts fights, field.js:878 sets e.spotted). One definition of contact; this design reads it and adds a timestamp.

field.js:1727 arrivals() is the clock-driven spawner for deferred cast groups; field.js:1673 spawnGroup(s, g, n); mapgen.js:340 marks a group deferred when it has per or a temporal at; mapgen.js:33 has the entry slot, so at: entry is placed by around(sl, zones.entry, n, 6).

field.js:798 chooseGoals: nest, garrison, wandering, ambush, patrol and quarry hostiles stand still unless they see, remember or are roused; only the default branch (waves, endless) calls hunt() unconditionally. A group added to a nest contract would not move toward the squad unless it takes that branch.

field.js:1375 (window shut, 30%) and field.js:1582 (escalate, 50%) respawn a share of EVERY hostile and patrol group in map.spawns with no check for deferred groups, so an added cast group is cloned unless it is skipped.

field.js:1784 descend() rebuilds map.spawns with MG.build. Maps with floors > 1 are warren (2), dungeon (4) and stronghold (2) (missiontypes.js:74-76), and retrieval, rescue, raid, recon, assassination, capture, extermination and expedition roll on them. A fired flag kept on the spawn would be lost on the stairs and the group would fire again on the next floor; spawns are rebuilt in cast order, so the flag is carried by cast index (3 lines).

field.js:1267 kill() counts kills by role; field.js:1521 rawWin reads killed(s, a.of); missiontypes.js:352 extermination asks 80% of total(cast, hostile); :768 the silence atom counts patrol kills; :1047 describe().hostiles; :234 total(). All of them mean "the written bodies", so total() ignores groups with arrive and arrival kills are counted under their own key.

quests.js:116 rolls trial contracts with mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option and rollTwists no filter, so star trials (the solo road included) draw every row. The pursuit lens assumes quests.js already passes trial: true; it does not.

sortie.js:259 (launch) takes the pseudoZone species from s.actors, and deferred groups have no actors at launch, so Missions.prepare would plan loadouts without the arrival groups (pseudoZone's id includes species.length, so the cache key changes when they are added).

bestiary.js:201-212 brief() builds one row per species / level / per / handle from mission.cast; sortie.js:889 missionCard and :1045 briefBox print the rows. A cast group with an arrive field reaches the card and the brief with no new screen; nameCast (sortie.js:61) gives each cloned group its own species of the same tier and theme.
field.js:382 withdraw(s, why, ordered) sets s.withdrew; both the squad's own break-off (broken()) and the retreat order (field.js:1487 retreat) go through it, so one test (s.withdrew) covers both.

Seeded roll check (scratchpad arr3/rollcheck.js, 600 rolls, two trees): moving rollTwists above the cast changes no draw order (spec.cast and spec.terms draw no random numbers, missiontypes.js:330-800): 499 rolls identical, 89 differ only where Reinforcements or Infested was rolled, 12 differ only on duel / dungeon / escort, whose legal twist pool changed.

Node check of the mechanism in the prototype (arr3/fieldtest.js, 16 assertions, all pass): the group is deferred at start; it fires at contactAt + 45 exactly once; save / restore at +20 keeps contactAt and fired; a retreat order 10 s after contact cancels it; escalate spawns no arrival group but still respawns written groups; total() and the extermination target (12 of 15 written bodies) ignore arrival groups; arrival counts equal max(1, round(count x 0.35)).

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (the game's own scripts booted by test/game.boot.js, real combat.js, board -> launch -> skip -> settle; gearless 3-5 star random-class squads of 4; levels 1-4; both arms on the same seed per contract; 1320 paired contracts on the 11 legal types): without the twist 60.7% won and 0.41 deaths per contract; with the arrival and the hold rule 54.2% and 0.60; without the hold rule 0.23 extra deaths instead of 0.18. The arrival fired in 83% of contracts (97% without the hold rule) and reached the squad in 80% (93%). 14.3% of releases without the hold rule came after the squad had withdrawn; 24.2% came after it had started the walk home (phase leaving), 11.6% with the rule.
proposals.change:
MODS (the table row, data only): reinforcements: { label: 'Reinforcements', weight: 12, reward: 1.25, not: ['duel', 'dungeon', 'escort', 'hold', 'siege'], trial: false, mods: { arrivals: [{ on: 'contact', delay: 45, from: 'entry', share: 0.35 }] } }. MT.modsOf defaults arrivals to [] and folds by concatenation, so another twist can add an entry with a different trigger. The desc is generated by MOD_TEXT.arrivals(entries, mission): "45 s (0:09) after the first sighting or fight, 35% of each hostile and patrol group (at least 1 body per group; about 5 bodies on this paper) arrives at the entry and moves toward the squad. Terms and bonuses count the written bodies only. A retreat order or a break-off cancels it." The body count follows the contract's intel through Bestiary.countText (at intel 0 the text gives the share and the delay only).

CONSUMERS.
(1) missiontypes.js. total() ignores groups with arrive. New pure arrivalCast(cast, arrivals): for each entry and each hostile or patrol group g of the written cast (not forSide, not already arrive) it emits { ...g, count: max(1, round(g.count * share)), at: from, arrive: { on, delay }, forTwist: id } without per, pack, from or species (for a per group g.count is one repetition). roll() moves 'const tw' above the cast at the same RNG position (verified above) and pushes arrivalCast(cast, mods.arrivals) after spec.terms, so win, lose and bonus atoms are those of the written contract. A twist whose effect came out empty is dropped from tw, so a contract never carries the tag and the multiplier without groups. MT.current(m) (u-honesty) also requires, for each twist with an arrivals mod, a cast group with forTwist === id, which stales board and held trial offers rolled before this lands. rollTwists(typeId, level, max, { trial }) skips rows with trial: false when trial is set; roll() takes trial; quests.js:116 passes trial: true.
(2) mapgen.js:340 deferred: !!(group.per || group.arrive || TEMPORAL.has(group.at)).
(3) field.js. start(), save() and restore() carry contactAt (null until set). arrivals() sets s.contactAt = s.clock on the first step at which contacted(s) is true. Then, for each s.map.spawns entry g with g.arrive and no g.fired, and only while s.withdrew is unset: due when s.clock >= s.contactAt + g.arrive.delay. On due: g.fired = s.clock (the spawn list is saved with the map, so a reload cannot fire twice), spawnGroup(s, g), and one log line with the body count and the distance in tiles from the group's first point to the nearest squad member. descend() copies g.fired across by cast index. spawnGroup / makeActor set march = true on bodies of a group with arrive; ACTOR_KEYS gets 'march'; chooseGoals (:798) becomes switch (e.march ? 'march' : m.pressure), so a marching body takes the default branch, hunt(), in every contract type. kill() (:1267) counts a march body under counters.killed.arrival instead of its role. The two respawn loops (:1375, :1582) skip groups with arrive.
(4) bestiary.js brief(): the arrive field goes into the row key and onto the row. sortie.js briefBox prints "arrives 0:09 after first contact, at the entry"; missionCard appends "+5 later" to the expect line from describe(), whose hostiles figure stops counting arrival groups (total()).
(5) sortie.js launch (:259): species gets one entry per body of each cast group with arrive, so Missions.prepare plans against them.
(6) sortie.js renderSide: one line under the portal line: "arrival after first contact", "arrival in 0:07", "arrival: 4 bodies, 34 tiles from the squad" or "arrival cancelled". fieldview.js drawMap: the label of the entry zone reads "arrival 0:07" while a group is pending (drawActors already draws unrevealed hostiles at alpha .38, so the group is visible once it exists).
(7) sortie.js settle() (:574): gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, won, dead }, the same shape as loop-ledger's gs.field.types and incremented in the same loop; the tag title prints it once sent > 0.
(8) test/sortie.harness.js: TWISTS=none|id[,id] pins the contract's twists (2 lines in contractOf) so one OUT file per arm pairs by type, level and seed. New test/twistprice.js prints the inputs of the price rule and exits 1 when the table value differs from the measured multiplier by more than 0.10 (a prototype of it ran on the files of this round). test/contracts.js: counts equal max(1, round(count x 0.35)); total() and terms identical with and without the twist; fire exactly once at contactAt + 45 across save / restore at +20; no fire after withdraw(); escalate and window-shut spawn no arrival group; descend does not fire a group twice; counters.killed.arrival; MT.current false for a mission with the id and no group.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Reinforcements x1.25"; its title lists the factors ("25 + 30 x level 3 = 115 / Assassination x2.5 / Reinforcements x1.25") and the generated desc; the expect line lists the extra rows with "+N later". Brief: the arrival groups are their own rows, one per species, with the arrival text, subject to the contract's intel like every row. Map: the countdown on the entry zone, then ghost tokens at the entry that move toward the squad; the log gives the body count and the distance. Side panel: the arrival line above.

REWARD x1.25. The multiplier is a table value, set with one rule and checked by test/twistprice.js. Rule: a squad that takes the twist should end each attempt with the gems it would have had without it: pay0 + loot0 - 100 x dead0 = m x pay1 + loot1 - 100 x dead1, with pay and loot the harness's per-attempt means (a lost contract pays 0) and 100 the price of a summon (PULL_COST, game.js:8, printed on the Summon button). Inputs (11 legal types, 1320 paired contracts): wins 60.7 -> 54.2%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.60 per contract, fee per attempt 114.3 -> 98.4, loot per attempt 57.9 -> 68.6 gems: m = 1.24, rounded to 1.25. The same inputs with the death price at 50 / 150 / 200 gems give 1.15 / 1.33 / 1.43; ignoring loot, 1.35; with no death price, 1.05. Wound downtime is not in the price (loop-wounds is not built; the harness reports no wounds yet). The player's check: the card title itemises the factor, the brief lists the exact extra bodies, and the tag tooltip shows their own record with this complication (sent, won, people lost).

FREQUENCY. weight 12 (unchanged), not duel, dungeon, escort, hold, siege. Per contract under u-honesty's draw rule with all nine rows live (exact enumeration over a board of uniformly drawn types, arr3/freq.js): 2.3% at level 1, 3.5% at 5, 5.1% at 10, 6.8% at 15, 8.5% at 20, against 3.2 / 4.8 / 6.9 / 9.2 / 11.6% for the original row. The other twists move by 0.1 points or less. P(at least one on a board of 5): 11% at level 1, 16% at 5, 23% at 10, 30% at 15, 36% at 20.
proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the paper states that each hostile and patrol group has 35% more bodies, that they come second and from the way in, and when; a player compares the squad against both fights on the same ground and against x1.25. During the run the player has one lever and it prevents deaths: the retreat order, with a countdown on the screen. Measured with the order given at the first calm moment (no open fight) at or after contact + k, on 330 paired contracts: deaths per contract without the arrival / with it are 0.41 / 0.58 with no order, 0.05 / 0.05 with the order at contact (k = 0), and 0.30 / 0.44 with the order 60 in-game s (12 real s) after contact. The order saves 0.36 deaths per contract at k = 0 without the arrival and 0.53 with it, and 0.11 / 0.14 at k = 60. It costs the contract: wins are 60% / 53% with no order, 1% / 2% at k = 0 and 20% / 19% at k = 60. The squad's own break-off cancels the arrival in the same way (191 of 1320 contracts never fired because the squad withdrew before +45 s; 28 because the contract ended first). Without any retreat the twist costs 0.18 deaths per contract and 6.4 win points.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat order (loop-retreat): contact starts two clocks, the end of the free call-off window and the release; a withdrawal cancels the release, so the order is worth more than before and the arrival never chases a squad that has already decided to leave (without that rule 14.3% of releases came after the withdrawal and the extra deaths were 0.23 instead of 0.18). Wounds (loop-wounds, WOUND_FROM 0.4): survivors whose lowest HP fell under 40% go from 18.0% to 21.7%, and contracts with such a survivor from 46.3% to 48.9%, so the twist feeds the downtime wave 2 introduces. Debrief: fights per contract 6.54 -> 7.89 (+21%), so casts spent per sortie rise with them; the stamina charge (25 + 1.5 x level in u-debrief) does not depend on fights. Permadeath: contracts with a death 21.0% -> 26.4%. Loadouts: the arrival groups' species are in the pseudoZone, so a brilliant mind plans resistances for them. Bestiary: arrival species enter Bestiary.record and noteSighting. Loot: kill drops rise (57.9 -> 68.6 gems per attempt) and are in the price. Hardcore: the escalation and window-shut respawns skip arrival groups, so the two do not stack their spawns. Night: halves sight, so contact comes later and so does the release. Side jobs: Leave no witnesses counts written patrol kills only (total()). Tactics: the retreat play ("a step back") falls back to the way in, which is where the group appears; it fires rarely, so no effect was measurable. Pairs: measured on 330 paired contracts (11 legal types, 30 each). No resupply alone: wins 60 -> 57%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.56, m = 1.02 (n = 330); with the arrival added on top: wins 57 -> 50%, deaths 0.56 -> 0.81, m = 1.34 (n = 330). Night alone: wins 60 -> 61%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.44, m = 0.90 (n = 330); with the arrival added: wins 61 -> 56%, deaths 0.44 -> 0.60, m = 1.16 (n = 330). Against the plain base, No resupply plus the arrival: wins 60 -> 50%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.81, m = 1.36 (n = 330). The board multiplies table values (No resupply 1.25 x 1.25 = 1.56), so the pair is paid more than its measured neutral value; deaths add a little more than the sum of the two parts. Side finding for the pricing rule: by the same rule No resupply alone measures 1.02 and Night 0.90, against table values of 1.25 and 1.15, so the live rows are not priced by it either.
proposals.risks: Build after u-honesty (modsOf, MOD_TEXT entries as functions of (value, mission), MT.current) and loop-retreat (contacted, retreat); approve at most one of reinforcements-a and reinforcements-b, which are alternatives on one table row. Harness caveats: plain characters without gear or potions, so absolute deaths are upper bounds (base 0.41 deaths per contract); confirm on a real save as loop-wounds step 7 does. The multiplier is an average over a wide spread: per type, the same rule on the held design gives assassination 2.58, capture 0.95, expedition 0.89, extermination 1.37, pursuit 1.00, raid 1.22, recon 1.14, rescue 1.60, retrieval 0.90, sabotage 1.39, survival 1.28; assassination alone is where base deaths are already 1.7 per contract (n = 120 per type, so single types are noisy). The release is inert where contact comes late or the squad is gone first (fires / reaches: assassination fires 78% reaches 72%; pursuit fires 74% reaches 74%; raid fires 69% reaches 68%; recon fires 79% reaches 76%; survival fires 76% reaches 70%). hold and siege are excluded on a stated criterion: the arrival reached the squad in fewer than half of the runs (hold 42%, siege 31%) and deaths did not move; the criterion is a harness reading and drifts with combat changes. dungeon is excluded on a reading of the code, not a measurement: descend() drops every actor that is not ours, so a group released on one floor is left behind on the stairs. escort is excluded on the harness: median first contact 200 in-game s against a median end of 220 s, and 75% of its contracts (n = 20, levels 1-4) are over before contact + 45. On the earlier private runner the nearest squad member was under 20 in-game s of walking from the entry in 9.8% of releases (survival 74%, raid 21%, every other type 7% or less); that was not repeated on the harness. If a squad holding ground next to the way in is unwanted, hold the release until no squad member is within sight + 2 tiles of the entry, for at most 30 s (not measured). Extermination: written bodies only count toward the 80%, so killing arrivals does not shorten the job. Dials: delay 20 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.69, wins 60 -> 53%, fires 96%, reaches 92%, m 1.32 (n = 330); delay 45 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.63, wins 60 -> 51%, fires 84%, reaches 82%, m 1.36 (n = 330); delay 90 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.53, wins 60 -> 55%, fires 69%, reaches 66%, m 1.17 (n = 330) (11 types, 30 contracts per type, paired with the same base). The death price (50 to 200 gems) moves the multiplier from about 1.15 to 1.4, so the table value is good to about +/-0.10 whatever the sampling error (+/-0.05).
proposals.response:
Design attack. (1) "Mostly a bigger fight": accepted in part. The arrival now has a counter that prevents deaths: a retreat order or break-off cancels it, the countdown is on screen, and the sweep above gives the order's value with and without the twist. (2) "+0.16 deaths priced at 200 gems, which the user does not accept as a price": replaced. The price uses PULL_COST (game.js:8, 100 gems), counts loot, and is stated as a table value with the per-twist record as the check, not as a derivation the player must follow; the rule is one function in test/twistprice.js and prints its alternatives beside it. (3) "14% of firings after the squad withdrew": confirmed on the harness (14.3% of releases) and removed by holding the release while s.withdrew is set; the measured effect is in the numbers above. (4) Trials: verified that quests.js:116 passes no trial flag and roll() has no such option, so the plumbing is added here with the field name the pursuit lens uses (trial: false). (5) Arrival kills counted toward extermination: fixed by total() and counters.killed.arrival, so killing arrivals no longer shortens the job. Demands: trial: false (done); hold on withdrew (done, measured); written bodies only (done); x1.25 as a data value with the record as check (done); one ACTOR_KEYS flag, 'march', consumed by one chooseGoals line, and any follower design (hunted) can set the same flag.
Engineering attack. Stale offers: MT.current extended, and an empty twist is dropped at roll time. describe().hostiles: total() ignores arrival groups and the card prints "+N later". Kill quota: counters.killed.arrival. RNG order: not changed (seeded comparison above). Inert types: hold and siege excluded on the reach criterion; the rest priced as an average with the spread stated. Pricing rule: one rule for the lens, reproducible with test/twistprice.js. Private runner: replaced by test/sortie.harness.js with paired seeds. Defects found while checking and fixed in the design: descend() rebuilds spawns and would have fired the group again on the next floor of any warren, dungeon or stronghold map (fired is carried by cast index); the two respawn loops clone every hostile group (skipped).

proposals.title: Alarm call: a hostile that has seen the squad and is still alive 30 s later calls a second group from unexplored ground; killing every spotter, finishing Leave no witnesses, or a retreat order cancels it
proposals.problem: Same card and same unimplemented row as reinforcements-a, with a different question: what makes a second garrison arrive "partway through" for a reason the player can see and act on. A fixed clock ties the arrival to nothing the squad does. The game already records who knows about the squad: look() sets e.spotted on every hostile that has a line to a squad member and raises the alarm (field.js:878). The Leave no witnesses side job (missiontypes.js:763) promises "nobody carried word", but its effect only zeroes the spotted counter and the alarm (field.js:468-470); no hostile that has already seen the squad is affected and nothing is sent anywhere. This design makes the word travel: a hostile that has seen the squad and is still alive after a delay calls the second group.
evidence: field.js:849-881 look(): for each hostile not yet spotted, if any squad member is within sight with a line (canSee at full sight; the sneak radius is used only for hunting, field.js:778 notice()), e.spotted = true, counters.spotted++, raise(). Nothing stores when. Night halves s.sight (field.js:2082), so it halves who can spot.

field.js:461-470 sideCheck: the quiet effect sets counters.spotted = 0 and alarmUntil = 0 and logs "nobody carried word". missiontypes.js:763-769: silence is offered on recon, rescue, retrieval, sabotage, assassination and capture (six types) and needs dagger, bow, unarmed or psionics; its atom counts patrol kills (total(cast, patrol), :768).
missiontypes.js:513, 536, 607, 653: the "never seen" bonuses (FAIL.spotted budget 0, 2, 0, 1) on recon, assassination, rescue and sabotage read counters.spotted, the same event that arms this call.
field.js:1477 contacted(s) reads actors' spotted flags, so the quiet job does not reopen the free call-off window; this design stores a timestamp per spotter (spottedAt) next to the flag.
mapgen.js:32-41 ZONE_SLOT: an unknown zone name falls back to mid and draws a ring there; a name mapped to scatter creates no zone (mapgen.js:218 zoneFor), so at: dark needs one ZONE_SLOT line.

The shared plumbing (arrive groups, march flag, fired flag in the saved spawn list carried across descend by cast index, hold while s.withdrew, respawn-loop skips at field.js:1375 and :1582, counters.killed.arrival, total() ignoring arrival groups, trial: false) is described in reinforcements-a and is identical here. sortie.js:61 nameCast, bestiary.js:201 brief, sortie.js:889 missionCard and :1045 briefBox carry the rows as in reinforcements-a.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (the 6 types that offer Leave no witnesses; 720 paired contracts; levels 1-4; gearless 3-5 star squads of 4; same seeds in both arms): without the twist 55.6% won and 0.53 deaths per contract; with the call and the hold rule 49.0% and 0.75. The call fired in 55% of contracts and the group reached the squad in 46% (75% and 53% without the hold rule, which lets 27% of the calls go out after the squad has withdrawn). It did not fire in 45% of contracts: 22% because the squad withdrew first, 23% because no spotter lived 30 s or the contract ended.
proposals.change:
MODS (the table row, data only): reinforcements: { label: 'Reinforcements', weight: 12, reward: 1.30, only: SIDE_JOBS.silence.on, trial: false, mods: { arrivals: [{ on: 'witness', delay: 30, from: 'dark', share: 0.35 }] } } (SIDE_JOBS is defined before TWISTS, missiontypes.js:762 and :818). The arrivals key is the same as in reinforcements-a; the two designs are alternatives on one table row. The desc is generated: "A hostile that has seen the squad and is still alive 30 s (0:06) later calls a second group: 35% of each hostile and patrol group (at least 1 body per group; about 5 bodies on this paper) arrives on unexplored ground at least 13 tiles from every squad member and moves toward the squad. Killing every spotter, completing Leave no witnesses, a retreat order or a break-off cancels the call."

CONSUMERS. Shared with reinforcements-a: arrivalCast (roll(), after terms, at: 'dark'), total() ignoring arrival groups, the empty-twist drop and MT.current, mapgen deferral, march flag and the one chooseGoals line, ACTOR_KEYS, counters.killed.arrival, the two respawn-loop skips, the descend carry, the hold while s.withdrew is set, pseudoZone species, brief rows, the per-twist tally, rollTwists trial filter, test/sortie.harness.js TWISTS and test/twistprice.js. Specific to this design:
(1) mapgen.js ZONE_SLOT gets dark: 'scatter'.
(2) field.js look() (:878) also sets e.spottedAt = s.clock for a non-march hostile; ACTOR_KEYS gets 'spottedAt'.
(3) arrivals(): an entry with on: 'witness' is due when some hostile, patrol or mark e is alive, not extracted, not march, has spottedAt != null and s.clock - e.spottedAt >= delay. Marks count as spotters (a named target that sees the squad and lives is the same event as a patrol that does); only hostile and patrol groups are cloned into the arrival.
(4) New darkAhead(s): over the map tiles pick the nearest passable, reachable (map.dist >= 0) tile that is unrevealed (s.seen) and at least sight + 4 tiles from every squad member; g.points becomes a few tiles around it; a fully explored map uses the far zone. One pass over at most 100 x 40 tiles, once per firing. The log line names the witness: "Goblin saw them 30 s ago and is still standing: 5 more arrive from unexplored ground, 33 tiles from the squad".
(5) sideCheck quiet effect (:468): for every hostile set spottedAt = null (not Infinity: JSON turns it into null on save, and missiontypes.js:37-38 forbids it), so "nobody carried word" is true of the call as well as of the counter.
(6) fieldview.js drawActors: a ring around each living hostile with spottedAt set while a witness cue is pending; sortie.js renderSide: "call in 0:04 (Goblin)" for the earliest spotter, or "no spotter alive". A dead spotter's ring disappears with it. No ring on the map before the call: the origin is chosen from what the squad has not yet seen.
(7) brief row text: "arrives from unexplored ground once a spotter lives 0:06".
(8) Tests: the call fires exactly when a spotter reaches 30 s alive; a spotter killed at 29 s prevents it; quiet clears spottedAt; save / restore keeps spottedAt and fired; a withdraw cancels; darkAhead returns an unrevealed tile at least sight + 4 from every squad member and the group is not placed within sight of the squad.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Reinforcements x1.30" with the generated desc and the factor list, offered on the six types only. Map: rings on living spotters until they die or the call goes out; at the call a log line and ghost tokens at the edge of the unexplored ground moving toward the squad. Side panel: the countdown line above.

REWARD x1.30. Same rule and same tool as reinforcements-a (pay0 + loot0 - 100 x dead0 = m x pay1 + loot1 - 100 x dead1, test/twistprice.js). Inputs for this design (6 types, 720 paired contracts): wins 55.6 -> 49.0%, deaths 0.53 -> 0.75 per contract, fee per attempt 117.0 -> 103.3, loot per attempt 46.9 -> 52.5: m = 1.30, rounded to 1.30. With the death price at 50 / 150 / 200 gems: 1.19 / 1.41 / 1.52; ignoring loot, 1.35. The multiplier is an average over contracts in which the call never fires (45%); a squad that kills its spotters keeps the multiplier without paying for it, which is the lever. Wound downtime is not in the price.

FREQUENCY. weight 12 (unchanged), only the six types above (SIDE_JOBS.silence.on, the types where the counter exists). Per contract under u-honesty's draw rule with all nine rows live: 1.3% at level 1, 1.9% at 5, 2.8% at 10, 3.7% at 15, 4.6% at 20, against 3.2 / 4.8 / 6.9 / 9.2 / 11.6% for the original row. P(at least one on a board of 5): 6% at level 1, 9% at 5, 13% at 10, 21% at 20.
proposals.playerEffect: The twist gives the player two things to read and three things to do. Read: which contracts carry it (the six that offer Leave no witnesses) and, during the run, who is carrying word and for how long. Do: bring kit that kills a spotter inside 6 real seconds (burst, ranged); take Leave no witnesses (its second effect is now the call); or order the retreat while the countdown runs, which cancels the call. The contract's own sight rule is a fourth lever: Night halves who can spot. Measured with the retreat order given at the first calm moment at or after contact + k, on 180 paired contracts: deaths per contract without the call / with it are 0.50 / 0.79 with no order, 0.08 / 0.07 with the order at contact and 0.39 / 0.59 with the order 60 in-game s (12 real s) after contact; wins are 57% / 43%, 1% / 2% and 23% / 19%. Without any order the twist costs 0.23 deaths per contract and 6.5 win points on these types.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat order: a withdrawal cancels the call, so the order is the in-run counter, and the call comes from unexplored ground while the squad walks back along explored ground. Side jobs: Leave no witnesses gets a second effect, so its x1.3 pay and its risk (the taker walks off alone against every patrol) are weighed against the call; only a squad with a dagger, bow, unarmed or psionic user can take it. FAIL.spotted bonuses (recon, rescue, assassination, sabotage): the counter the bonus reads is the event that arms the call, so a squad that earns "never seen" has also prevented the call. Night: halves sight, so fewer spotters. Wounds: survivors under 40% HP at their lowest 20.3% -> 24.2%, contracts with such a survivor 47.8% -> 50.7%. Debrief: fights per contract 5.64 -> 6.51. Permadeath: contracts with a death 24.9% -> 32.4%. Loot: 46.9 -> 52.5 gems per attempt, in the price. Pairs: twist pairs were not measured for this design; Night is the pair that changes who can spot.
proposals.risks: Build after u-honesty and loop-retreat, and approve at most one of reinforcements-a and reinforcements-b (one table row). The call fires in 55% of contracts and reaches the squad in 46%, and the multiplier prices the average; per type (deaths base -> twist; fires, reaches): recon 0.32 -> 0.38 deaths (fires 34%, reaches 28%); rescue 0.22 -> 0.54 deaths (fires 68%, reaches 63%); retrieval 0.36 -> 0.42 deaths (fires 30%, reaches 24%); sabotage 0.45 -> 0.78 deaths (fires 87%, reaches 81%); assassination 1.72 -> 2.30 deaths (fires 53%, reaches 40%); capture 0.09 -> 0.11 deaths (fires 58%, reaches 42%). look() ignores the sneak radius (field.js:778 notice() only governs hunting), so a sneaking detail is still spotted; making look() honour it would change every FAIL.spotted budget and is a separate decision. The type list is a stated relation to SIDE_JOBS.silence.on (the types where the counter exists), not a harness reading; the harness shows retrieval and recon with the lowest rates, so a squad on those types is rarely called on. darkAhead assumes unrevealed ground exists away from the squad; on ring-shaped maps (settlement) it can place the group behind a wall, still out of sight. The delay is 6 real seconds; dial on the harness: delay 15 s: deaths 0.53 -> 0.87, wins 56 -> 39%, fires 82%, reaches 73%, m 1.77 (n = 240); delay 30 s: deaths 0.53 -> 0.80, wins 56 -> 46%, fires 55%, reaches 47%, m 1.42 (n = 240); delay 60 s: deaths 0.53 -> 0.64, wins 56 -> 53%, fires 30%, reaches 25%, m 1.11 (n = 240). No tactics play targets spotters and none is proposed; the squad AI fights what reaches it, which is why most spotters die inside the delay. A squad-goal bias toward living spotters is a possible follow-up. Harness caveats as in reinforcements-a (gearless squads; wound downtime not priced; the death price moves m from 1.19 (50 gems) to 1.52 (200 gems)).
proposals.response:
Design attack. (1) "Paid for nothing where it does not fire": the multiplier is the average and the numbers above state how often it fires; the cancel conditions are the lever, not a defect. (2) "Information with no control": the controls are the retreat order (it cancels, with a visible countdown), Leave no witnesses, kit and Night. No tactics play is added: the squad's targeting is AI, and the game offers the player no in-run orders other than the retreat. (3) "44% of calls after the squad starts leaving": confirmed in kind on the harness: without the rule 27% of calls go out after the squad has withdrawn and 40% after it has started the walk home (phase leaving); the hold-while-withdrawn rule removes the first and leaves 19% in the second (the job done, walking out). (4) "Weight 24 doubles the row to compensate for only": reverted to 12. (5) "darkAhead is new placement for a 43% reach": reach is now measured on the harness (above); the routine is one pass with a fallback. Demands: not built as the only Reinforcements design (stated: alternative to -a, approve one); only on the types where Leave no witnesses exists (done, derived from SIDE_JOBS.silence.on); weight 12 (done); a control or play (retreat order and the job; no play proposed, reason given).
Engineering attack. "Reach 43%": restated on the harness (46%). "Tuned only list": replaced by a relation to SIDE_JOBS.silence.on. Marks: counted as spotters, stated. Weight: 12. darkAhead and map.dist: no longer uses map.dist as direction. Shared plumbing: identical to -a (same flag, same fields), so the two cannot be built independently of the choice between them.

proposals.title: Promoted third: round(count / 3) bodies of each rank-and-file group are fielded about 1.5x stronger, same species
proposals.problem: The card shows Infested ("A third of the cast comes one grade up", x1.35) and the cast is exactly as written. Read literally, one grade is a poor unit: in combat.js a body one grade up is x3.8 (basic to veteran), x4.8 (veteran to elite) and x1.5 (elite to ancient) in hp x damage x speed, and elite to legendary does not exist for rank and file, so promoting a third of every group by grade has no setting that one multiplier can price. A level offset gives a uniform ratio instead (combat.js:107 scales every attribute by 1 + 0.35 x (level - 1)).
evidence: combat.js:107 fromMonster scale (1 + 0.35 x (level - 1)): +k levels is a fixed ratio of about x1.5 hp and damage when k = round(1 + level / 2), at every level from 2 to 18.

Promotion by grade, 900 runs each on the earlier private runner (base 70.2% / 0.263 deaths): a third of every group 53.3% / 0.614; basic groups only 63.4% / 0.272; veteran groups only 57.6% / 0.566. A level offset of +3 on a third: 61.8% / 0.354.

field.js:84 SWARMED(g) assumes a negative levelOffset: for +3 it evaluates 1 / (1 + 0.35 x -3), which is negative, and clamps to 0.15, so a promoted body would be a runt in makeActor hp and power (field.js:1687) and in every odds() call. A positive branch is one line.

sortie.js:61 nameCast names each cast group on its own, so a group split into a promoted part and a rest needs a shared key to keep one species; mapgen.js build() places each cast group on its own scatter / around call, so the two parts would stand in different places unless they share points.
sortie.harness.js (combat-backed) was not run for this design; the figures above are from the private runner.
proposals.change: Dropped. The design added round(count / 3) promoted bodies of each hostile and patrol group at levelOffset +round(1 + level / 2), a kin id so nameCast gives both parts one species, the SWARMED positive branch, a "+3" mark on the map, and reward x1.50.
proposals.playerEffect: The only new decision was reading a second brief row for the same species at a higher level. That is the decision a higher-level contract already gives, and nothing about the ground, the timing or the squad changes during the run.
proposals.secondOrder: On the earlier private runner the proposal cost +0.14 deaths per run and -6.9 wins per 100 at a stated multiplier of x1.50, while reinforcements-a costs +0.18 deaths and -6.4 wins per 100 on the combat-backed harness at x1.25; the two instruments differ, but a design that raises danger by a similar amount for a higher multiplier was not defensible. Positive levelOffset would also have been new to the engine (SWARMED was the only reader that assumed offsets were negative), loadouts are planned against species at the mission level (sortie.js pseudoZone), so promoted bodies would be planned for at the wrong level.
proposals.risks: None remain once dropped. If a stronger-body variant of Infested is wanted later, build it on infested-b (more bodies, fielded weaker, by the existing swarm path) and not on a level offset.
proposals.response: Design attack (a level bump wearing a tag): accepted. I checked the code for anything that makes it more than a bump and found nothing: the same species at the same count in the same places is fielded at a higher level, which is what a higher-level contract is, and the proposal text itself said the only new decision was a second brief row. Engineering attack (kin placement, stale offers, price rule, SWARMED fix): all accurate and all moot once dropped. The SWARMED positive branch (field.js:84) is a hardening that only matters if a positive offset is ever introduced; it is not needed by infested-b, which uses negative offsets only. infested-b is the design that changes how the fight is played (frontage, packs, ground).

proposals.title: Overrun: hostile and patrol groups are fielded as if the level expected one more grade (x2.2 bodies, in packs, each body 2.25 levels weaker per added grade), and kill gems follow the fielded level
proposals.problem: The board offers Infested ("A third of the cast comes one grade up", x1.35) and the cast is exactly as written (missiontypes.js:827). Read literally, one grade is a poor unit: a body one grade up is x3.8, x4.8 or x1.5 in hp x damage x speed depending on the grade, so no single multiplier prices it. The game already has the rule for a place that is overrun: swarm() (missiontypes.js:310) turns every grade a group sits below what its level expects (NATIVE, :286) into x2.2 bodies fielded 4.5 levels lower, placed in packs, with a brief tag (a pack / a swarm / a tide) and a note that the ground decides how many reach the squad at once (sortie.js briefBox, combat.js frontage, the tactics stand play). A contract that is not already below its level's grade never uses it. This design raises the expected grade by one for the contract. It needs one change outside the twist: gem drops per kill do not depend on the level the body was fielded at (missions.js:243), so more bodies means more gems, and the surplus is larger than the contract fee (measured below).
evidence: missiontypes.js:286-318: NATIVE(lv) is 0 below level 6, 1 from 6, 2 from 12, 3 from 17; HORDE_SWELL 2.2, HORDE_STEP 4.5, HORDE_CAP 40 (HORDE_CAP_PER 20 for per groups), HORDE_PACK [0, 5, 9, 14]; swarm(group, lv) computes gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)) and returns the group unchanged when gap < 1 or the count would not rise.

missiontypes.js:945-952 roll() applies swarm before spec.terms, so terms already read the swollen counts; spec.cast and spec.terms draw no random numbers, so rollTwists can move above the cast at the same RNG position (seeded comparison over 600 rolls: 499 identical, 89 differ only where Infested or Reinforcements was rolled, 12 only on duel / dungeon / escort, whose legal pool changed).

bestiary.js:212 and sortie.js briefBox (:1045) already print the horde tag and the ground note; mapgen.js packs() places a swarmed group in packs; field.js:84 SWARMED and makeActor give swarmed bodies reduced hp and power; sortie.js fighterFor spawns them at mission level + levelOffset, clamped to level 1.

missions.js:243 rollLoot: gems per kill = (2 + 1.5 x mission.level) x tier reward x (0.8 to 1.2), whatever level the body was fielded at; combat.js:619 pushes { def, mods, killer } for each kill, and the fielded level is t.level on the dead combatant (combat.js:120).
field.js:1582 escalate() respawns 50% of g.count of every hostile and patrol group: the fielded count, swollen or not.
quests.js:116 rolls trial contracts through MT.roll with no trial flag (see reinforcements-a); a solo trial against a pack of 22 has no frontage advantage.

Rolled casts (arr3/swellstats.js, 40 rolls per type per level, 15 types), bodies per contract, written -> with Infested: level 1: 8.5 -> 16.4; 3: 11.1 -> 21.2; 5: 13.5 -> 25.0; 6: 27.4 -> 44.2; 10: 35.6 -> 48.8; 14: 52.9 -> 70.7; 18: 74.3 -> 79.1. Share of groups that change: 50% at levels 1-5, 92% at 6, 61% at 12-16, 36% at 18, 28% at 20. Share already at the cap: 0% at levels 1-5, 15% at 10, 39% at 12-16, 66-73% at 18-20. At levels 18-20, 27-35% of contracts have no group that can swell.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (combat-backed; gearless 3-5 star random-class squads of 4; levels 1-8, 75 contracts per level; 15 types, no duel; paired seeds). With the existing swarm calibration (every added grade 4.5 levels weaker), 600 paired contracts: wins 35.7 -> 29.2%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 66.1, loot 53.7 -> 57.9, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9. The twist lowers deaths (0.97 -> 0.78) and wins (35.7% -> 29.2%): contracts that end with "they ran from a fight they were losing" go from 48% to 56%, wipes from 13% to 11%. Gem drops without the rollLoot change: wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9.

With the added grade 2.25 levels weaker instead of 4.5 (the design below), 600 paired contracts against the same base with the rollLoot change: wins 35.7 -> 26.3%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.99, fee per attempt 78.5 -> 56.4, loot per attempt 53.7 -> 54.6, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.4, fights 6.1 -> 5.8, contracts with a death 41.2% -> 39.7%. By level: L1-3 wins 68>50% deaths 0.40>0.39; L4-5 wins 28>19% deaths 1.02>0.97; L6-8 wins 9>8% deaths 1.51>1.60. Contract endings, base / this design: won 35% / 26%, ran from a fight 48% / 55%, squad down 13% / 15%. A quarter step (1 level weaker per added grade) gives wins 24.8% and deaths 1.08, price 1.64.

Loot change alone on the base contracts (15 types, levels 1-8, no twist; existing swarms are the level 6-8 part): wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1. Level 12-18 probe (5 types, 60 paired contracts, gearless squads): hostiles per contract 60.2 -> 73.0, Node CPU per contract 2602 -> 2693 ms, 7% of rolls had no group that could swell and dropped the tag.
proposals.change:
MODS (the table row, data only): infested: { label: 'Infested', weight: 10, reward: 1.40, not: ['duel'], trial: false, mods: { swell: { grades: 1, step: 0.5 } } }. MT.modsOf folds swell by summing grades (capped at 2); step belongs to the one twist that sets it. The desc is generated from the rolled cast by MOD_TEXT.swell(value, mission): "Hostile and patrol groups are fielded as if the level expected 1 more grade than it does: x2.2 bodies per grade, in packs of 5, 9 or 14, each body 4.5 levels weaker per grade the level expects and 2.25 per grade this adds; a group at 40 bodies (20 per wave) is unchanged. On this paper: Water Slime x10 -> x22; Cave Spider x1 (unchanged). Gems per kill follow the level the body is fielded at." The counts follow the contract's intel (Bestiary.countText).

CONSUMERS.
(1) missiontypes.js. swarm(group, lv, bonus = 0, step = 1): gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) + bonus - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)); the level offset uses gapNat + (gap - gapNat) x step grades of HORDE_STEP, where gapNat is the gap without the bonus. New swell(group, lv, value) returns the inflated group only when it has more bodies than the plain swarm, and records swollenFrom: plain.count on it (a group already at the cap would otherwise get a deeper offset for the same count). roll() moves 'const tw' above the cast at the same RNG position, builds the cast from the written groups with swell() when mods.swell is set, and drops 'infested' from tw when no group changed (levels 18+: 27-35% of contracts), so the tag is never carried without an effect. proposals.playerEffect: The decision is the ground and the squad. The paper names the map and states how many bodies come (17.9 written, 30.0 with the twist, per contract); on open ground a pack of 22 reaches the squad together, in a doorway it reaches two at a time, so a player compares the contract's map cover and the squad's frontage tools (a line-holder, area damage) before launch, and the existing stand play (tactics.js) acts on it during the run. Measured effect: 9.3 fewer wins per 100 contracts, deaths level (0.97 -> 0.99), more hostiles (19.3 -> 31.4) and more wounded survivors (25.6% -> 30.5% of survivors under 40% HP at their lowest; contracts with one 54.2% -> 61.2%). Gems come from kills, valued by the level the body is fielded at.
proposals.secondOrder: Wounds: 25.6% -> 30.5% of survivors under 40% HP at their lowest (the loop-wounds trigger), contracts with such a survivor 54.2% -> 61.2%: the cost of this twist is downtime. Permadeath: contracts with a death 41.2% -> 39.7%, so it neither adds nor prevents deaths at this step; at the existing calibration (4.5 levels weaker) it prevents them (41.2% -> 33.2% of contracts, m = 0.83), which would make it a favourable complication. Retreat (loop-retreat): wins fall because the squad breaks off more often (48% -> 55% of contracts end in a run from a fight it was losing), so the contract is lost without a death; the retreat order is unchanged. Debrief: fights per contract 6.1 -> 5.8 while bodies per contract rise, so casts are spent in fewer, larger fights. Loot: with the rollLoot change drops are 53.7 -> 54.6 gems per attempt; without it they would be +66% (wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9). Existing swarm contracts: gem drops fall (wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1); the contract fee is unchanged. Hardcore: escalation respawns 50% of the swollen count, so Infested + Hardcore escalates harder (a 22-body group adds 11); rare (together on about 0.06% of level-1 and 0.6% of level-20 contracts) and now stated in the Hardcore text. Night: no interaction. No resupply: attrition over more, smaller fights is where the two stack, and it is not measured.
proposals.risks: Build after u-honesty. Two parts, one unit: without the rollLoot change this twist adds +66% gem drops (wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9), larger than the fee, and no sane multiplier fixes that; if the rollLoot change is declined, do not build the twist. The rollLoot change is an economy change for every existing swarm contract (level 6 and up): gem drops there fall by roughly half (wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1; levels 6-8 alone: loot 101 -> 49 gems per attempt). If the user wants existing swarm pay left alone, the fallback is a per-group field lootLevel set only by swell() (one field, one branch in rollLoot) at the cost of two payout rules. Harness: gearless squads (absolute deaths are upper bounds), levels 1-8; levels 12-18 were measured for body counts and run time only (gearless squads win none of them). The step (0.5) is a dial chosen on the harness: at 1.0 the twist lowers deaths (m = 0.83), at 0.25 it costs 10.9 win points for m = 1.64; the price is mostly lost fee. Low levels: bodies are fielded at max(1, level - offset), so at levels 1-3 the swollen bodies are at or near level 1 (L1-3 wins 68>50% deaths 0.40>0.39), a larger win-rate drop than at 6-8. Frame time in the browser at 40+ hostiles is not measured (overseer check); Node CPU per contract rose 1839 -> 2165 ms on levels 1-8 and 2602 -> 2693 ms at levels 12-18. Per type, wins and deaths move in both directions (assassination 33>25% 2.30>2.35; capture 43>40% 1.57>1.45; dungeon 18>10% 1.63>1.82; escort 90>98% 0.57>0.33; expedition 55>45% 0.65>0.30; extermination 48>43% 0.60>0.47; hold 30>8% 0.10>0.03; pursuit 38>35% 0.97>0.30; raid 25>5% 1.25>1.38; recon 38>43% 0.75>0.45; rescue 40>13% 0.60>0.93; retrieval 30>43% 0.90>0.10; sabotage 20>3% 1.10>0.63; siege 3>5% 1.45>1.07; survival 28>25% 0.10>0.07); the multiplier is an average.

proposals.problem: Hunted rolls on every type except duel (missiontypes.js:829, weight 8, pays x1.4) and nothing reads it: the id appears in no other .js file. The tag says something follows the squad and joins whichever fight is going worst. No actor follows the squad: a hostile moves only when it sees the squad, remembers it for GIVE_UP = 20 s (field.js:62) or is inside an alarm (chooseGoals, field.js:709). No fight gains a body after it opens: openSkirmish resolves the whole fight once, up front (field.js:1220). The first version of this proposal made the follower an ordinary hostile that trails the squad. Measured on the real harness that version mostly produced run-ins: 2478 fights involved the follower and 317 were joins; the rest were the squad walking into it, a healthy squad could kill it and end the twist, and the effect was an elite standing on the way out. The premise of that version was also wrong. Where baseline deaths happen, 1800 contracts at levels 1-4 (test/sortie.harness.js, 15 types): 126 before the squad began leaving, 54 after the job was done (leave(), field.js:1882) and 524 after a withdrawal (withdraw(), field.js:382, called by broken(), by a lost fight or by the retreat order). Three quarters of deaths are on a walk out that began because the squad was losing, so the walk out is not unthreatened, and a twist that is active there makes the retreat order worth less than it is.
