proposals.playerEffect: Before launch the brief shows one extra row (species, level, x1, "follows the squad", HP when the town has met it). The decision is the 70% line, and it is made during the run. Below 70% average HP between fights the squad has three choices: rest, since REGEN returns 0.5% of max HP per second (60 s of walking is 30 points) and in-fight healing and potions are already counted when the fight ends; keep going, in which case the next fight that opens gets an elite-tier fighter added; or order a retreat, which ends the follower's joins at once. Before the terms are met the order costs the contract. After the terms are met it costs nothing, because the verdict reads the terms before the withdrawal flag, and 40 of the 68 measured joins were in that walk home. A squad that never retreats and never rests below the line paid 0.500 vs 0.386 deaths per contract (+30%); a squad that orders the retreat at 70% paid +4% over the same policy without the twist and lost 1.5 wins per 100 contracts. A squad that stays above the line never sees the follower, and then the contract paid x1.15 for nothing. Composition matters for the rate: under the heavier variant two clerics cut the join rate from 34% to 25% of contracts. During the run the log prints the HP that triggered a join and the tally shows "1 following" while the follower is on the map. Killing the follower is possible only in the fight it joins.
proposals.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat as built: sortie.js exitState, field.js contacted/retreat): the order gains a use it does not have today. In this harness the order at under 70% HP between fights cut deaths 21% with the follower and 4% without it. Releasing the follower does not close the free call-off (it is not spotted, field.js:1477). The squad's own break-off sheds the follower the same way as an order. Wounds (u-wounds): joins are the fights that end with the squad at its lowest, so they feed the lowest-HP trigger; deaths replace wounds for the squads that lose a member. Permanent death: 0.386 -> 0.500 deaths per contract (+30%), 1.4 deaths per join, 28 joins per 900 contracts while the squad is still working. Tactics: tactics.js reads only side "theirs" (:209, :230, :250, :305), so the follower never counts as closing and cannot cause stand plays; the plan layer does not know the follower exists, so its odds readings understate a fight the follower will join. Chorokinetic: loneTarget (field.js:948) and the terror kit read isTheirs, so a wormhole cannot land on it; once it has joined, escapeHatch (:991) can break the fight off like any other. No resupply: the 70% line is crossed for good after the first big fight, so the join rate rises (26% to 33% of contracts under the heavier variant). Bestiary: look() records the species at first sight (noteSighting), so the first Hunted contract adds the species to the town's bestiary. Loot and kill counts: the follower is a normal kill once it has joined (+1 hostile for kill quotas). Overlap with Reinforcements: a body that takes a side at a fight and a group that arrives on a cue are different triggers; both can roll on one contract (max two twists) and their effects multiply.
proposals.risks: All figures come from gearless squads of 4 without potions; absolute deaths are upper bounds and only the relative change is usable. The default has few events: 68 joins in 900 contracts, so the three seeds disagree more than for the other twists (+0.12, +0.19, +0.04); the heavier variant has 463 joins in 1800 and agrees (+0.17, +0.12, +0.15). One join costs 1.4 deaths because a level+1 elite arrives in a fight the squad is already losing. Most joins (40 of 68) are on the walk home after the terms were met, where the only lever is the free retreat order; a player who never uses the order meets the follower there. Choosing between the two gates is a design decision, not a tuning one: afterWithdraw false gives the retreat order a function and a lower, more variable cost; true gives +37% and an order that does not help (-4%). The 70% line is the engine's break-off average (field.js:1015) without the "someone down" clause. Hunted over Night is unmeasured for sight 5 beyond the pair above (the follower at 4 tiles is inside sight 5). The follower is not in the loadout plan unless pursuit-twist-plumbing item 6 lands. Needs u-honesty and pursuit-twist-plumbing first; fieldview.js, bestiary.js and sortie.js are being edited by wave 2 builds, so line numbers will move.
proposals.response: Design attack, accepted in full: the join was the minority path (317 of 2478 follower fights) and the cost was a trailing elite met on the way out. The follower is now unengageable (side "neutral", combatant() false) and only the join remains; re-measured above. The demand was that it keep its distance when approached, reusing the quarry flee goal; I implemented the same guarantee differently because a flee goal needs a distance field from the squad's current position every step and a follower cornered in a dead end would fight anyway, while a one-line combatant() test gives "walking at it never opens a fight" as an invariant that test/contracts.js checks. Tactics.closing: verified, it reads side "theirs" only. The "leaving" statistic is split (126 / 54 / 524 baseline deaths) and the split changed the design: with the follower active on the walk out after a withdrawal, 74% of joins land on squads that are already breaking off and the retreat order is worth 4%, so the default stops the follower at withdrawal. Price: stated rule and inputs, x1.15 (x1.27 at 200 gems per death) against x1.25 for +0.16 deaths on Reinforcements; the x1.4 is gone. Two corrections to what I expected: the unengageable follower is MORE lethal than the fightable one at the same offset (+37% against +25% under the heavier variant), because the squad can no longer end the twist by killing it early; and with the withdrawal clause most joins (40 of 68) move to the walk home after the terms are met. quests.js trial threading is pursuit-twist-plumbing. Engineering attack, accepted: both respawn loops (plumbing item 5), tooltip names the measured cost, trial threading, price rule, one Hunted row only (Hunted B is dropped). Declined in form: building on a Reinforcements cue-spawn shape; I could not see that proposal. The cue used here is the existing TEMPORAL/cued mechanism (mapgen.js:45, field.js arrivals) that last-wave groups use, and the only new actor data is `keep`; no stance and no new goal branch except the one loop in chooseGoals. If Reinforcements lands an `arrive` shape, "trail" becomes one value of its `on`.

proposals.problem: A twist that adds a cast group exists only because it was rolled, and the code has no place for that. Hunted A (this lens) is one; the antagonist review lists Reinforcements and Infested as changing the cast at roll time too. Specific gaps, each checked: (1) roll() adds side-job casts through a spawn hook (missiontypes.js:950) and has none for twists; (2) quests.js:116 rolls trial missions with no trial flag, so a one-character star trial can draw any twist; (3) a board offer or trial offer rolled before a twist gained a cast keeps the tag and the pay multiplier with no bodies behind it; (4) describe() sums every hostile group on the paper into the card count (missiontypes.js:1047), so a twist body would be counted as a paper hostile; (5) escalate() (field.js:1581) and the window-shut branch of portalTick (field.js:1374) re-spawn every hostile and patrol group in map.spawns at 50% and 30% with no check, so any group a twist adds is cloned by a Hardcore escalation and on every shut window. Hunted A needs all five and Turncoat A needs the trial filter; other lenses may need the same hooks and describe their own copies.
evidence: missiontypes.js:947-950: roll() resolves side jobs and pushes `{ ...j.spawn(lv), forSide: id }` into the cast before terms are read; the function stays in SIDE_JOBS and never reaches a saved mission. A twist hook follows the same idiom.
missiontypes.js:952-954: terms are computed from the cast at :952 and twists are rolled at :954, so a twist cast pushed after :954 does not change kill quotas or the terms.
missiontypes.js:863-876 rollTwists(typeId, level, max): the legal filter reads only `only` and `not`; there is no argument for a trial roll.
quests.js:116 `mt.roll(spec[road].type, { level: spec.level, name: spec.name })` (no trial flag); quests.js:94 PARTY = { solo: [1, 1], group: [3, 6] }, so the solo road is one character.

sortie.js:77 rollBoard rolls board contracts with `MT.roll(type, { level })`; the board turns over after REROLL_MS = 6 real minutes (sortie.js:22, checked in the board getter at :98) but trial offers are kept in state.trials until the star changes (quests.js:97-121 offer()).
missiontypes.js:1047 describe().hostiles = total(m.cast,"hostile") + total(m.cast,"patrol") + total(m.cast,"mark"): counts every group by role.

field.js:1374 (window shut, 30% of each group) and field.js:1581 (escalate, 50% of each group): both loop over s.map.spawns, skip roles other than hostile and patrol, and call spawnGroup(s, g, Math.max(1, Math.round(count * share))); neither tests g.deferred, g.at or a twist flag.

sortie.js:263 `const species = s.actors.filter(a => a.species && a.side === "theirs")` is the list pseudoZone (sortie.js:112) plans loadouts against; a deferred group is not an actor yet, so its species is absent from the plan although the brief lists it.
u-honesty (.team/round1/u-honesty.json, change item 3) defines MT.current(m) as "every twist id is known"; it has no clause for a twist whose cast is missing.
proposals.change:
ONE unit, landed once for every twist lens; Hunted A and Turncoat A list it as a requirement.
1) missiontypes.js roll(): add `trial` to the options; after `const tw = ...` (:954) add `for (const id of tw) { const t = TWISTS[id]; if (t && t.spawn) cast.push({ ...t.spawn(lv), forTwist: id }); }`. Terms were read at :952, so quotas ignore the group. A TWISTS row may carry `spawn: (lv) => group` (a function, resolved here and dropped, like SIDE_JOBS.spawn).
2) missiontypes.js rollTwists(typeId, level, max, { trial }): when `trial` is true, rows with `trial: false` are removed from the legal list. quests.js:116 passes `trial: true`; sortie.js rollBoard passes nothing.
3) MT.current(m) (u-honesty) gains a clause: for each twist id with a `spawn` hook, m.cast contains a group with forTwist === id. A held board offer or trial offer that fails it is treated as absent and re-rolled (the three places u-honesty already lists: board getter, Quests.offer, resume keeps the run).
4) missiontypes.js describe(): `hostiles` counts groups without `forTwist`.
5) field.js escalate() (:1581) and portalTick window-shut (:1374): `if (g.forTwist) continue;` in both loops.
6) sortie.js launch (:263): the species list also takes `s.map.spawns.filter(g => g.forTwist && g.deferred && g.species).map(g => g.species)`, so the loadout plan covers a body the brief lists. nameCast (sortie.js:61) already writes g.species into every cast group at board time and mapgen copies it into map.spawns.
7) test/contracts.js: 300 seeded MT.roll(type, { trial: true }) calls never return a row with trial false; a mission whose cast lacks the forTwist group fails MT.current; describe().hostiles is unchanged by a twist cast; escalate() and a shut window leave the number of forTwist actors unchanged; a saved mission with a twist id and no group still plays.
No behaviour changes for Night, No resupply or Hardcore: they have no `spawn` hook and no `trial` field.
proposals.playerEffect: No new play. It prevents three visible defects: a Hunted or Reinforcements tag on a card with nothing behind it after the table changes under a held offer; a one-character star trial drawing a complication that adds bodies; a Hardcore escalation or a shut window adding another copy of a complication's single body (Math.max(1, round(count x share)) is 1 for a group of one).
proposals.secondOrder: Pay: a held offer rolled under the old table is re-rolled instead of paying a multiplier for an effect that does not exist. Trials: with `trial: false` on a row, star trials roll without it, so a star trial never carries a complication that adds bodies. Loadouts: ai.js brilliant minds plan against the deferred body's species, so the brief and the plan agree. Hardcore: its escalation no longer adds a copy of a twist body.
proposals.risks: Touches the same lines as u-honesty (missiontypes.js roll/rollTwists, MT.current), so it lands after it. Other lenses may carry copies of items 1, 3, 4 and 5 (the antagonist review notes that Reinforcements A already skips its own groups in the two loops); approve exactly one copy or the builds conflict on missiontypes.js and field.js. Item 6 changes the planning zone id for new launches (sortie.js:112 keys it by species count); a run saved before the change resumes with the zone it saved (persist() stores run.zone).
proposals.response: New proposal from the missed list (trials, stale offers, describe().hostiles, the two respawn loops, the planning zone). Not measured: it changes no balance number; the tests above are the check.
